relations.to: Memory set to zero: a market dies when a copy of the good arrives at no price, since the price memory is rewritten to zero and every later price reads as a surcharge on free, as the printed encyclopedia died against the free one and the paid article died against the free page; the tell is paying customers asking why they pay; the memory can be reset only by naming a different lot, membership rather than articles, and news took fifteen years to find one that held; the one death in which nothing is missing and the lot still exists, because what was spent was the number.
relations.label: If the bundle's allocation line falls far enough below the old unit price, a third of a cent per stream against ninety-nine cents, the bundle sets the memory to zero from inside, and the reversible death ripens into the irreversible one; unbundling then bears a market whose memory is of nothing.

relations.from: Decreed sacred: a market dies by decree of the good when the community declares it unsaleable, and the transfers do not stop but change kind, moving by gift and by theft, as relics after the Lateran ban travelled by pious theft and organs since 1984 travel by donation chains; the tell is that the gift has a going rate; the death is easy and the reversal nearly impossible, a claim that rests on an asymmetry of standing rather than on any recorded repeal, since a good once declared sacred cannot be declared ordinary without the declarer looking like a seller; adjacent to market-births' Price-proof good, a good that payment changes, this is a good that a decree changes, and the asymmetry between the two directions is the finding.
relations.to: Died into a queue: a market dies by decree of its price when the decree holds the price below what clears, so rationing moves from the price to the line and the market survives as a queue that grows the forbidden sale back as a bribe for a place in it, as rent control breeds key money; the tell is a posted price with a waiting list beside it; reversible by decontrol, but the stock the price was meant to protect has been let rot in the interval and the first free prices are a birth from imported comps, as Cambridge found in 1995; the inverse of market-births' Queue to hijack, which is a market born on a queue, this is a market dying into one.
relations.label: If the decree makes the good unsaleable but not unwanted, the good is rationed by waiting or by lot, as the transplant list rations organs, and the queue grows back the sale the decree forbade as a bribe for a place in line; the sacred recruits a queue, and the queue recruits the parasite market-births' Queue to hijack describes.

relations.from: Print taken back: a market dies from the top when the party that made trades final unmakes one, since every later trade is then provisional, as the London Metal Exchange cancelled a morning of nickel trades in March 2022 and the participants who had won the cancelled trades took their volume elsewhere for two years; the tell is a rulebook that now shows the power, and, where a copy exists, its open interest rising in the same lot; where no copy exists the venue survives, distrusted, and its volume drifts back one uncancelled crisis at a time, as nickel's did; rebirth requires a clearer whose rulebook lacks the power, or the belief in finality rebuilt by crises that pass without a cancellation; not a default, which is a counterparty failing, but the witness declining to witness.
relations.to: Copy takes the crowd: a market whose lot can be copied exactly at another address dies at the old address on the day the copy holds enough of the crowd that the rest follow for the crowd's sake, as the Bund contract left London's pit for Frankfurt's screen within a year once the electronic copy passed its tipping share; the tell is volume falling while open interest holds, since positions are being closed at the old address and opened at the new one; nothing is spent, the market lives at the copy, and the old venue is reborn only by becoming a copy of something else; not a market death so much as the death every other death here is measured against, since it is the one that leaves everything standing.
relations.label: If a copy with the same lot exists when the print is taken back, the participants who lost carry the crowd to the copy, and one event is a death by finality at the old address and a birth by migration at the new; if no copy exists, the same cancellation leaves the market alive and merely distrusted, so the copy decides whether the revoked print kills.

exploration.first_question: By what mechanism does a market that was clearing trades stop being one, and which of those deaths can be reversed: read market-births backward, one death for each precondition that fails.
exploration.changed_question: What does the death leave standing for the next market? Reading the births backward produced three pointers that refused to be deaths: a copy that takes the crowd leaves the market alive at another address, a crash leaves it alive at a lower price, and illegality strips the grade, the fence, and the witness while the trade goes on. Among the deaths that remained, what varied was not which precondition failed but whether the next market could get it back, and the auction-rate case showed a death that spent nothing anyone had built, the buyers' belief that the auctions cleared by themselves. So the second breath asked which deaths refute the belief or the ignorance the next market would need, and found the death that spends ignorance itself.
exploration.new_member: Test before the pool: a market for risk dies when the risk becomes known before the trade, since the pool that priced the unknown dissolves into the certain-loss, who cannot be insured, and the certain-safe, who will not pay, as a genetic test does to a life-insurance pool; the tell is the seller asking for the test; what the death spends is ignorance, which no one can rebuild once the test exists, so rebirth requires a witness built not to see, as Canada's genetic non-discrimination act and the British insurers' moratorium forbid the life insurer to ask, while the American statute of that name covers health cover and leaves life cover to the test; the mirror of Farm comes back, which is death by too little known about the lot, this is death by too much.

priorities.item: Warm corpse: a price kept quoted after its trades have stopped because contracts reference it, so the reference keeps the corpse warm, as the interbank term-lending rate was submitted as judgment for a decade after the lending it named had ended, with hundreds of trillions written on it; the tell is that no submitter can name a trade at the print, and the print moves when the panel changes rather than when supply does; rebirth requires a new witness on an underlying that still trades and a statute to move the legacy contracts, since no single party to a contract can leave the corpse alone; not a fraud, which may or may not attend it, but a quote whose only buyer is the contract.
priorities.why: It is the death an operator is most likely to be standing inside without knowing it, since any contract that references a benchmark is a hand keeping some corpse warm, and the test costs an afternoon.
priorities.next_question: For one benchmark your contracts reference, pull the last twenty prints and count the actual trades behind each; if any print rests on fewer than three, plot the count against time to see whether the witness is starving or already judgment, and write down which of your contracts would need a statute, not a renegotiation, to move.

priorities.item: Test before the pool: a market for risk dies when the risk becomes known before the trade, since the pool that priced the unknown dissolves into the certain-loss, who cannot be insured, and the certain-safe, who will not pay, as a genetic test does to a life-insurance pool; the tell is the seller asking for the test; what the death spends is ignorance, which no one can rebuild once the test exists, so rebirth requires a witness built not to see, as Canada's genetic non-discrimination act and the British insurers' moratorium forbid the life insurer to ask, while the American statute of that name covers health cover and leaves life cover to the test; the mirror of Farm comes back, which is death by too little known about the lot, this is death by too much.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that a pool can be held open after the test exists, high generative promise: if a sealed result lets strangers pool, then ignorance can be rebuilt as an arrangement rather than a fact, and the map's closing item splits into deaths that spend ignorance and deaths that spend only its custody.
priorities.next_question: Assemble a small mutual, ten freelancers against a month of lost income, in which every member takes the relevant test and posts the sealed result to an escrow before the premium is set, with the seal opened only at claim; then let members retake the test privately and see whether those who learn they are safe leave, which would show that a sealed witness delays this death rather than reversing it.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after repairing five items, two that failed the map's own boundary rule (a fenced right still clearing at a tenth, a starving witness whose trades continue) and three whose illustrative cases were overclaimed as history, relabeling the fork edge from Witness starving to Farm comes back so its consequent reaches the mechanism it names, softening two modalities (the Bund's months to a year; Decreed sacred's irreversibility named as an asymmetry of standing), and moving Fence rots and Question nobody asks to the bands their own texts argue for; the closest pair, the boundary case, the seriation, and the band-of-ignorance inference survived.

neighbors.left: Memory set to zero: a market dies when a copy of the good arrives at no price, since the price memory is rewritten to zero and every later price reads as a surcharge on free, as the printed encyclopedia died against the free one and the paid article died against the free page; the tell is paying customers asking why they pay; the memory can be reset only by naming a different lot, membership rather than articles, and news took fifteen years to find one that held; the one death in which nothing is missing and the lot still exists, because what was spent was the number.
neighbors.right: Died with the collectors: a market whose price memory lived in its buyers dies when the buyers become estates, so every holder is a seller with no memory and no buyer inherits it, as common stamps and porcelain figurines fell toward material value once the generation that knew their prices was in the ground; the tell is estate in every provenance, dealers' stock growing, and catalogues quoting prices no one pays; no rebirth of that market is possible, since memory kept in people is not resupplied, and a new generation may make a new market on the same objects with its own reason and its own prices; not Memory set to zero, where the number was rewritten, since here the number survives in old catalogues and the rememberers do not.
neighbors.separating_case: Sheet music after free scores went online: the memory of the music's price was rewritten to zero while the collectors of first editions remained, and their market lived on with its prices. Porcelain figurines: nothing ever became free, the catalogues still print the old prices, and the buyers left with the memory in them. The first is a number rewritten with the rememberers present; the second is the rememberers gone with the number intact, and only the first can be reseeded by renaming the lot.

checks.boundary_case: A price collapse is out: the oil price halved across 2014 and 2016 and the market cleared every day, so it was alive at a lower price. It comes in only where the collapse converts every holder into a seller in the same hour, which is One sentence, all holders, or reveals that nobody was ever on the bid, which is Hand on the saddle. Prohibition is out for the opposite reason: the trade survives with its grade, fence, and witness stripped, which is a deformation, not a death. The critic added a third: a market that stops because the lot itself ceases to exist, Kodachrome processing after the last lab closed, is out, since the good died and not the market; and a venue's insolvency is in, as Copy takes the crowd where a copy exists and as Wall in one head generalized where it does not.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a fork the sequence conceals at Witness starving, which the itinerary places once but which splits by whether a substitute field exists: fed, it drifts into Farm comes back; unfed, it dies into Warm corpse. It shows an incompatibility at the limits between Farm comes back and Test before the pool, the same variable, how much is known about the lot, killing the market at too little and again at too much, so a risk market lives only inside a band of ignorance. It shows a dependency at Bid that never blinks → One sentence, all holders, where the floor manufactures the run that follows its removal, two deaths in sequence from one cause. It shows a ripening along the map's own axis at Sunk into the bundle → Memory set to zero, where the most reversible death ripens into an irreversible one from inside (the critic corrected the author's name for this edge: it is a movement along the axis, not a passage between levels of organization). It shows a second dependency at Decreed sacred → Died into a queue, where the sacred recruits the queue and the queue recruits the sale. And it shows that Print taken back kills only when Copy takes the crowd is available, the two ends of the itinerary joined by an edge the line cannot draw.
checks.target_preserved: Fable critic's judgment (fresh context, 2026-09-07), applied by the repairer: the strange members (a corpse kept warm by contracts, a hand on the saddle, a death by too much knowledge, relics moving by pious theft, a collectibles market that needs rememberers rather than wanters) were tested and kept as mechanisms; the critic tried to domesticate Died with the collectors into 'demand died with the generation' and declined; the five repairs sharpen where a death occurs or correct an overclaimed case, and none replaces a strange mechanism with a respectable one.

name: low-chair-advantages
of: A mechanism by which a low chair confers something the chair above cannot have, named with the carrier that keeps it (the beliefs of those above, the record kept about one, what one holds, the floor itself, or a second order held on purpose), the moment on rising at which it is lost, and what keeping it deliberately would cost.
items: Fool's license: words that arrive pre-discounted cannot be a challenge, so a truth passes from the fool that from a peer would have to be answered, as Lear's fool, or the junior on a trading desk who says the position is insane, is laughed at, and watches the desk quietly re-hedge; carried in the discount others apply, it ends the first time anyone acts on the words in the open, and a riser keeps it only by staying unheard; not credited sincerity, which works by being relied on, but a truth that works by needing no reply.

Word without a move: talk from someone who can gain nothing by it is read as information rather than positioning, so the junior's memo is read as analysis and the chief's as a move, as the Rule of Benedict sends the abbot to hear the youngest, or the shop assistant who says she would not buy it; carried in others' estimate of your stake, it is lost at the first stake, real or suspected; not the fool's license, which works by needing no reply, but credit, which works by being relied on.

Dumb question's price: the cost of revealing that you do not know is proportional to what your chair says you should know, so the obvious question that topples a ten-year ritual can be asked cheaply only from the bottom, as the new hire's 'why do we do this?'; lost on the day you are supposed to know, and it returns at the summit, where a Nobel makes Feynman's dumb question a display of security rather than a gap, so it is dearest in the middle; not fresh eyes, which a new chief also has and which do not lower the price of confessing.

Servant's eye: those above behave as if unobserved before a chair they do not count as an audience, so the low chair sees the natural behaviour no colleague sees, as the night nurse knows which surgeon is dangerous and the cleaner knows who is about to be fired; carried by the contempt of the watched, not by any hiding, it is lost the day they begin to perform for you, which is the day of promotion into the audience; the summit can rent it by disguise, as Haroun al-Rashid walked the market, and the rental expires once disguise is known to be a practice; not a hide, which the watcher builds, but a blindness the watched build themselves.

Barber's chair: the powerful confide on purpose in whoever cannot use what they hear, so the barber, the driver, and the assistant are told what the deputy never is; carried in the confider's estimate of your incapacity, it is lost the moment you gain the capacity to act, as the assistant made a vice-president is told nothing thereafter, and it binds where the servant's eye did not, since what is told is owed secrecy and what was overheard is owed nothing; not unknowing exposure but knowing disclosure.

I just work here: acts and messages are attributed to the chair above, so the low chair can carry word between enemies or execute a decision without owning it, as the cook who passes between the factions or the clerk whose policy is not hers; carried in attribution, it is lost at the first signature, and its price is never being the author; its dark twin is the soldier's 'following orders', the same mechanism with the moral bill visible; not discounted speech but displaced authorship.

Costless no: a refusal says nothing about the asker when nobody expected a yes, so the low chair can ask fifty times where the high chair can afford to ask once, as the unknown freelancer's cold pitches or the intern asking the chief for coffee; the price of a probe is what its refusal reveals, and that is set by the chair; lost when your refusals become news, as the founder turned down in public; not the beggar's mouth, where the ask itself confesses need whether or not it is granted, since here the ask offers something and only the refusal could cost.

No file: nobody stores your failures or reversals, so they do not compound, as the open-mic comic who bombs two hundred nights or the unknown founder who pivots without a press cycle; carried in others' records rather than their beliefs, it is lost when the first success creates an audience that keeps you on file, and unlike a belief a file once opened does not close, so it is the one advantage no riser gets back except under a new name; not a costless refusal or an unguarded opening, but what happens to an event after it.

Beggar's mouth: asking for help costs status, so the chair with none asks for free while the high chair cannot ask without a fall, as the ruined financier who cannot say he is broke or the senior partner who cannot say the caseload is beyond her; carried in the status you hold, it is lost on the first rung, and the loss kills, since the newly high lose the ask before they lose the need; not a costless probe, which offers something, but a confession, paid whether or not it is answered; and not the dumb question, which the summit can wear as curiosity, since need can be worn as nothing but need.

Small change: a published rate is a signal and taking less damages it, so the whole lower market of work is reachable only by the chair whose rate is low, as the star who cannot play weddings or the former executive whom the shop calls overqualified; carried in the price attached to your name, it is lost at the first published high price, which is why a fall from a high chair goes past the floor rather than onto it; keepable by keeping the rate low, that is by refusing the income the rise offered; not favours and not help, but paid work.

Stone's blood: civil enforcement costs more than it recovers from someone with nothing seizable, so the low chair is not worth suing for the small and uncollectible for the large, as the judgment-proof debtor or the tenant whose deposit is the landlord's whole remedy; the shield is civil only, since the state prosecutes the small against the poor at its own expense; carried in your holdings, it is lost at the first attachable asset, a wage or a deed, which is why the first pay rise of a rising person is also the day the creditors return; keepable only by holding nothing in your own name, which is a fraud or a vow; not the freedom to move but the immunity from being moved against.

No hostages: a move that would expose assets is open only to the one who has none, as the immigrant enters the trade the native cannot enter without losing face, or the challenger sells the thing that would cannibalise the incumbent; carried in what you hold, it is lost at the first acquisition worth defending, which is what winning is, and it can be kept only by vow, the monastic engineering of refusing to own; not the price of a refusal but the price of a move, and not immunity from being moved against.

Expendable scout: the low chair is sent first into the new or the dangerous because it can be lost, and so holds the frontier's knowledge before anyone above it, as the junior developer given the untried framework, the private issued the new weapon, the youngest son who emigrates; carried in your expendability, it is lost when you become too valuable to risk, and the knowledge is owed upward, unlike the free mover's; not a move chosen because nothing is held, but one assigned because you are cheap.

Ladder credit: where cash can settle, no obligation accrues, so the one who pays is owed nothing and the one who cannot pay builds credit in favours, the one credit line a cash crash does not close, as the borrowed ladder that comes back as harvest help or the neighbour who minds the children and is repaid in a roof, and the exchange rate favours the poor, since gratitude is priced by sacrifice; carried in the known inability to pay, it is lost the day neighbours learn you can, when they stop owing and start billing; adds to obligation futures the exclusion, that cash sterilises the account; not the allies of many seats but the credit they enforce, and not the susu, which is cash the floor enforces.

Many seats: a chair with many occupants and nothing beneath it has peers who are not rivals, so its honest feedback and mutual aid come free, where the high chair's peers compete and its subordinates cannot be friends, as the enlisted against the officers, the nurses' station, the cell block; lost the day you become the boss of your friends, and kept only by not competing for the next chair, since the same floor that lends is the floor that can hold you down; not the virtue of the occupants but their number.

Bosun's knowledge: the present state of the machine, which valve sticks, which workaround is load-bearing, which gauge lies, lives where the work is done and the chart above it is a model, as the bosun against the captain or the charge nurse against the attending; carried by the work itself, it decays at the rate the machine changes once you leave the floor, and it is the one advantage a riser keeps by continuing to take a shift, at the price of the hours the promotion was supposed to buy; not skill, which is portable and keeps, but the machine's current state, which is neither.

Second chair: a riser keeps the advantages that live in others' beliefs only by holding a genuinely low seat in a separate order, the white belt, the church basement, the amateur choir, where the discount, the harmlessness, and the cheap question can form again; not disguise, which fails once known, since the second chair really is low; lost the day the two orders touch and the dojo learns what you do on weekdays; the map's own proposal, and the one member that is a mechanism for keeping rather than for having.

source.register: Mechanistic and concrete: court fools, trading desks, night nurses, bosuns, barbers, judgment-proof debtors, susus, cell blocks, the Benedictine chapter, the dojo; drawn from trades, institutions, and the lives of people who must keep a floor under themselves.
source.mode: Clearly separated mixture: analytical mechanisms with observed illustrative cases for sixteen members, each simplified to one mechanism; the summit's recovery of two belief-borne members is an analytical reading with a speculative reach; Second chair is the map's own proposal and is marked so in its text.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a taxonomy or a partition; a real low chair usually holds several of these at once, and some hold none, since each depends on a carrier that a particular low chair may lack (the invisible nurse who is nonetheless fully on file).

The seriation is an itinerary by where the advantage is kept, not a ranking of value or of how often each occurs; the assignment of a member to a carrier is an interpretation (Costless no could be read as record-borne rather than belief-borne, and Beggar's mouth, placed with the holdings, is carried by status, which is made of others' beliefs), and map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (Lear's fool, the Rule of Benedict's chapter, Haroun al-Rashid's market walks, the susu, Feynman's questions, the undercover chief) are simplified to one mechanism each and are not claims about the specific histories; the wolf pack was left out because its status science is contested.

The summit's recovery of an advantage (the disguised king, the laureate's dumb question) is claimed for two belief-borne members only, as an analytical reading with a speculative reach; no claim that any other member returns at the top, and Second chair is the map's own proposal rather than an observed institution.

Advantages that are transfers from an audience (sympathy for the underdog, charity) are outside, since the audience can withdraw them and the chair cannot operate them; but that criterion alone is leaky, since the fool's discount is equally others' to withdraw, so the sharper exclusion, the Fable critic's, is that the low bar (credit for a competent deck from the intern), the under-defended first strike, and the first cold pitch that lands are spent by the first success rather than lost by exposure, and this map's axis, where the advantage is kept, has no place for advantages consumed by use; they belong to a map of what the first success costs, with No file at the joint. The costs of the low chair (the scapegoat, the crab bucket, the scout's risk) appear only as the price of a member.

seriation.axis: Where the advantage is kept, and so what moment loses it: from advantages held entirely in the beliefs of those above (lost the instant they look again), through what others record about you (lost when the file opens, which it never un-does), through what you yourself hold, status, a price, seizable things (lost at the first acquisition, keepable by vow), to what the floor holds, the work itself and the floor's own enforcement (lost on leaving the floor for the work-borne pair, keepable by keeping a shift; lost when those above learn you can pay or are worth keeping for the floor-enforced pair, which can happen while you still stand on it), and finally to a second order held on purpose.
seriation.note: An authored itinerary, not a scale of value, rarity, or difficulty. Fool's license opens it because nothing carries it but the discount others apply, and one open act on the fool's words ends it; Second chair closes it because it is not kept in this order at all. The walk passes through four carriers, and each carrier has its own price of keeping and, for three of them, a single moment of loss: belief-borne members (Fool's license through Costless no) are lost on being seen and can be kept only by concealment or, for two of them, regained at the summit; No file alone is record-borne and is never regained; holdings-borne members (Beggar's mouth, Small change, Stone's blood, No hostages) are lost on acquiring and can be kept by refusing to own, which is what a vow of poverty engineers; floor-borne members (Expendable scout, Ladder credit, Many seats, Bosun's knowledge) are kept by the floor's structure and enforcement, and the block's loss moment splits, as the Fable critic showed: Bosun's knowledge and Many seats are lost on leaving the floor and kept by staying on it, while Ladder credit (lost the day neighbours learn you can pay) and Expendable scout (lost when you become too valuable to risk) are lost by a change in the beliefs of those above that can happen while you still stand on the floor, so they sit nearer the belief-borne members than the block label first admitted. Beggar's mouth is placed in the holdings block as status held, but status is what the belief-borne carriers are made of and its loss moment, the first rung, is a being-seen moment; the placement is an interpretation, like Costless no's. The hinge is Bosun's knowledge → Second chair: both keep an advantage by spending hours in a low place, but the bosun's floor belongs to the same order as the captain's chair, so the knowledge flows up and the belief-borne members do not return (the crew performs for a captain who stands a watch), whereas the second chair is a separate order, so the belief-borne members return and the work-borne ones do not transfer; the adjacency teaches that what a riser can keep depends on whether the low place is inside or outside the order they rose in. Inside the holdings block, Stone's blood → No hostages is the pair that shares one carrier and one loss moment, which is why the first rung is the most dangerous: the pay rise that returns the creditors is the acquisition that gives you something to defend.

relations.label: If the unseen one is noticed while still harmless, overhearing becomes being told and the chair rises one level; but what is told is owed secrecy where what was overheard was owed nothing, so the passage trades free information for a bond, and a riser who wants the information without the bond must stay unnoticed.

relations.from: Stone's blood: civil enforcement costs more than it recovers from someone with nothing seizable, so the low chair is not worth suing for the small and uncollectible for the large, as the judgment-proof debtor or the tenant whose deposit is the landlord's whole remedy; the shield is civil only, since the state prosecutes the small against the poor at its own expense; carried in your holdings, it is lost at the first attachable asset, a wage or a deed, which is why the first pay rise of a rising person is also the day the creditors return; keepable only by holding nothing in your own name, which is a fraud or a vow; not the freedom to move but the immunity from being moved against.
relations.to: Ladder credit: where cash can settle, no obligation accrues, so the one who pays is owed nothing and the one who cannot pay builds credit in favours, the one credit line a cash crash does not close, as the borrowed ladder that comes back as harvest help or the neighbour who minds the children and is repaid in a roof, and the exchange rate favours the poor, since gratitude is priced by sacrifice; carried in the known inability to pay, it is lost the day neighbours learn you can, when they stop owing and start billing; adds to obligation futures the exclusion, that cash sterilises the account; not the allies of many seats but the credit they enforce, and not the susu, which is cash the floor enforces.
relations.label: If a court can collect nothing from you, the only credit anyone can extend you is credit the floor enforces, in favours or in a susu's cash rounds, whose sanction is exclusion rather than seizure; so being uncollectible pushes you into the ladder economy rather than out of credit altogether.

relations.from: Ladder credit: where cash can settle, no obligation accrues, so the one who pays is owed nothing and the one who cannot pay builds credit in favours, the one credit line a cash crash does not close, as the borrowed ladder that comes back as harvest help or the neighbour who minds the children and is repaid in a roof, and the exchange rate favours the poor, since gratitude is priced by sacrifice; carried in the known inability to pay, it is lost the day neighbours learn you can, when they stop owing and start billing; adds to obligation futures the exclusion, that cash sterilises the account; not the allies of many seats but the credit they enforce, and not the susu, which is cash the floor enforces.
relations.to: Many seats: a chair with many occupants and nothing beneath it has peers who are not rivals, so its honest feedback and mutual aid come free, where the high chair's peers compete and its subordinates cannot be friends, as the enlisted against the officers, the nurses' station, the cell block; lost the day you become the boss of your friends, and kept only by not competing for the next chair, since the same floor that lends is the floor that can hold you down; not the virtue of the occupants but their number.
relations.label: If favour-credit must be enforced without courts, the enforcement is exclusion from the floor, so ladder credit recruits many seats; and the floor that enforces your credit is the floor that can hold you at the floor, which keeps you uncollectible, so the three close a loop that a rise breaks at every point at once.

relations.from: No hostages: a move that would expose assets is open only to the one who has none, as the immigrant enters the trade the native cannot enter without losing face, or the challenger sells the thing that would cannibalise the incumbent; carried in what you hold, it is lost at the first acquisition worth defending, which is what winning is, and it can be kept only by vow, the monastic engineering of refusing to own; not the price of a refusal but the price of a move, and not immunity from being moved against.
relations.to: Expendable scout: the low chair is sent first into the new or the dangerous because it can be lost, and so holds the frontier's knowledge before anyone above it, as the junior developer given the untried framework, the private issued the new weapon, the youngest son who emigrates; carried in your expendability, it is lost when you become too valuable to risk, and the knowledge is owed upward, unlike the free mover's; not a move chosen because nothing is held, but one assigned because you are cheap.
relations.label: If one arrives at the frontier by choice because nothing is held and another is sent there because they can be lost, the same knowledge comes back carrying different debts, the free mover's their own and the scout's owed to the chair that sent them; the frontier forks by who paid the fare.

relations.from: Beggar's mouth: asking for help costs status, so the chair with none asks for free while the high chair cannot ask without a fall, as the ruined financier who cannot say he is broke or the senior partner who cannot say the caseload is beyond her; carried in the status you hold, it is lost on the first rung, and the loss kills, since the newly high lose the ask before they lose the need; not a costless probe, which offers something, but a confession, paid whether or not it is answered; and not the dumb question, which the summit can wear as curiosity, since need can be worn as nothing but need.
relations.to: Second chair: a riser keeps the advantages that live in others' beliefs only by holding a genuinely low seat in a separate order, the white belt, the church basement, the amateur choir, where the discount, the harmlessness, and the cheap question can form again; not disguise, which fails once known, since the second chair really is low; lost the day the two orders touch and the dojo learns what you do on weekdays; the map's own proposal, and the one member that is a mechanism for keeping rather than for having.
relations.label: If the ask for help must be made by someone whose chair forbids it, it can be carried by no chair at all, the anonymous line, which is disguise and fails when known, or by a separate order in which their chair is genuinely low, the meeting, the white belt; so the second chair exists because the beggar's mouth cannot be faked inside the order that forbids it, and it fails when the orders touch.

exploration.first_question: By what mechanisms does a low chair confer something the chair above cannot have, and which of these can be kept on purpose by someone who rises, as against those available only to someone who genuinely has nothing?
exploration.changed_question: Where is each advantage kept, and is the moment of its loss the moment of being seen, of being recorded, of acquiring, or of leaving the floor? Breath one's members almost all lived in the beliefs of those above, and the answer to 'which can be kept' was a single one: only by not being seen. Sharpening Costless no against No file separated a belief held now from a record kept later, with different loss moments, and the carrier turned out to decide the keeping: what is kept in others' heads is kept by concealment or a second order, what is kept in one's holdings is kept by vow, what is kept in the work is kept by a shift.
exploration.new_member: Small change: a published rate is a signal and taking less damages it, so the whole lower market of work is reachable only by the chair whose rate is low, as the star who cannot play weddings or the former executive whom the shop calls overqualified; carried in the price attached to your name, it is lost at the first published high price, which is why a fall from a high chair goes past the floor rather than onto it; keepable by keeping the rate low, that is by refusing the income the rise offered; not favours and not help, but paid work.

priorities.item: Small change: a published rate is a signal and taking less damages it, so the whole lower market of work is reachable only by the chair whose rate is low, as the star who cannot play weddings or the former executive whom the shop calls overqualified; carried in the price attached to your name, it is lost at the first published high price, which is why a fall from a high chair goes past the floor rather than onto it; keepable by keeping the rate low, that is by refusing the income the rise offered; not favours and not help, but paid work.
priorities.why: It is the survival mechanism the map's first framing could not see at all, since it lives in a labour market's price signals rather than in anyone's regard, and it predicts something checkable: that a fall from a high chair overshoots the floor.
priorities.next_question: For one trade with a public rate ladder, session and touring musicians, list twenty players with their published rate and ask each whether they can be booked at the wedding rate under their own name; the prediction is that above some published rate no wedding booking exists at any price, and that the players who still reach that market do so under a second name or through a fixer who hides the rate.

priorities.item: Second chair: a riser keeps the advantages that live in others' beliefs only by holding a genuinely low seat in a separate order, the white belt, the church basement, the amateur choir, where the discount, the harmlessness, and the cheap question can form again; not disguise, which fails once known, since the second chair really is low; lost the day the two orders touch and the dojo learns what you do on weekdays; the map's own proposal, and the one member that is a mechanism for keeping rather than for having.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that it works as cleanly as written, high generative promise: it is the only member that answers the live question for the belief-borne class without deception, and it makes a testable claim about what happens when two status orders touch.
priorities.next_question: Find three risers who hold a known low seat in a separate order, a chief who is a white belt, a surgeon in an amateur orchestra, a bishop in a church-basement meeting, and record whether people in the second room say to them what nobody at work would; then find the day the room learned their weekday chair and ask whether the advantages died that day or survived because the low seat had been earned before the discovery.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after repairing three items (a civil-only shield in Stone's blood, a cash case moved out of Ladder credit, a summit discriminator added to Beggar's mouth) and three edge labels (subject-relative dumb question, floor-enforced credit in any currency, anonymity named as the alternative to a second chair); the 'work-borne' block's loss moment is noted as mislabeled for two of its four members. The fourth seriation block is relabeled floor-borne with its split loss moment; no items cut; order unchanged.

neighbors.left: Fool's license: words that arrive pre-discounted cannot be a challenge, so a truth passes from the fool that from a peer would have to be answered, as Lear's fool, or the junior on a trading desk who says the position is insane, is laughed at, and watches the desk quietly re-hedge; carried in the discount others apply, it ends the first time anyone acts on the words in the open, and a riser keeps it only by staying unheard; not credited sincerity, which works by being relied on, but a truth that works by needing no reply.
neighbors.right: Word without a move: talk from someone who can gain nothing by it is read as information rather than positioning, so the junior's memo is read as analysis and the chief's as a move, as the Rule of Benedict sends the abbot to hear the youngest, or the shop assistant who says she would not buy it; carried in others' estimate of your stake, it is lost at the first stake, real or suspected; not the fool's license, which works by needing no reply, but credit, which works by being relied on.
neighbors.separating_case: The junior on the desk who says the position is insane. If the desk laughs and re-hedges without saying so, the words worked by discount, nobody had to answer them, and the junior's chair is intact for next time: Fool's license. If the head trader says in the meeting that she is right, the words worked by credit, they were relied on because she had nothing to gain, and she is now a source: Word without a move. Same words, and the difference is whether anyone had to reply; and once relied on, the next thing she says is a move, so both licenses are gone together.

checks.boundary_case: Fresh eyes are out: the newcomer's not-yet-habituated perception is carried by novelty, not by the chair, since a new chief has fresh eyes too and pays full price for the obvious question the moment the honeymoon ends. Dumb question's price is in on exactly that contrast, since what the low chair confers is not the seeing but the cheapness of confessing.
checks.form_inference: The map shows an incompatibility the sequence conceals: Fool's license and Word without a move sit as neighbours on the itinerary, but the edge between them says the same words cannot be both unanswerable and relied on, so one open act on the fool's words converts the license into credit and ends it. It shows a dependency, Dumb question's price → Bosun's knowledge, where the question is dear over whatever your chair is supposed to hold and the floor's knowledge is exactly what the floor chair holds, so the bosun asks cheaply about the chart and dearly about the valve, and a riser who keeps a shift regains the knowledge while the question about it grows dearer. It shows a passage between levels at Servant's eye → Barber's chair, overhearing becoming being told at the price of a bond, and a second passage at Beggar's mouth → Second chair, out of this order altogether. It shows a loop the line cannot express, Stone's blood → Ladder credit → Many seats → Stone's blood, in which being uncollectible leaves only credit the floor enforces, in favours or in a susu's cash rounds, that credit recruits the floor to enforce it, and the floor holds you at the floor, so a rise breaks the loop at every point at once. And it shows a fork at No hostages → Expendable scout, where the same frontier knowledge comes back with different debts depending on who paid the fare.
checks.target_preserved: Judged by the Fable critic in a fresh context: the item type is real, the closest pairs separate under pressure (Fool's license against Word without a move on whether anyone had to reply; Dumb question's price against Beggar's mouth on whether the confession can be re-worn at the summit; Stone's blood against No hostages on a 2x2 of passive immunity against active freedom), and the strange members (a credit line that cash sterilises, a rate that makes a fall overshoot the floor, an ask that dies before the need does, a seat held in another order on purpose) survive as mechanisms; three items were repaired for a false generality, a self-contradicting case, and a misplaced case, and three edges relabeled where an 'only' or a 'must' had a counterexample, with no strange mechanism replaced by a respectable one.

name: runway-illusions
of: Mechanisms by which a person's or a firm's real time until it must stop, or what that time is worth, or how it answers to the operator's own moves, differs from what its cash balance over its burn predicts, each named with the carrier that holds the difference, what the cash figure misreads, and whether a better count corrects it or only a change in what is counted.
items: Date bomb: an obligation that arrives as a step rather than a slope, as the lease that renews in September, the annual premium, the tax bill in April, the tuition due before the school year, so the death is at the first step the balance cannot clear and not at the month the average burn predicts; the carrier is the calendar, the cash figure misreads a staircase as a ramp, and a better count corrects it, since the schedule was always on paper; the seasonal case, the fisherman's winter or the nine-month salary, is the same staircase repeated.

Reach the cliff: an asset that arrives as a step, as the vesting date, the pension's twentieth year, the bonus paid in March, the tranche released on a milestone, so the runway's worth is a step in its length, a race whose prize is a jump, and the whole loss is quitting three weeks early; the carrier is the payer's schedule, the cash figure misreads a binary as a slope, since the months before the cliff are worth nothing on their own and everything as a bridge; the same calendar as Date bomb read upward, and distinct in what it makes the operator do, since a step down is cleared by having the cash at the date while a step up is raced for by spending whatever reaches the date, so a cut that lengthens the months and misses the date is a loss and not a gain; a permission that arrives on a date, as naturalization at year five, is Stamp's clock read upward and not this.

Cash behind glass: money that is owned but cannot be reached in time, as deposits at a bank taken into receivership on a Friday, a retirement account behind a penalty, a receivable held in escrow, savings in a currency that cannot leave its country, so the runway runs on the reachable balance and the pipe's delay rather than on the owned one; the carrier is the pipe between the account and the payroll, the cash figure counts ownership where the clock runs on access, and a better count corrects it once the ledger has an access column, which it usually does not.

Burn you cannot put down: burn divides into what stops when you stop it and what stops only after notice, severance, or a lease's remaining term, so two firms with equal burn have unequal runways under cuts, and the first cut costs a step before it saves a slope; the carrier is the stack of commitments, the cash figure misreads one number for what is a floor and a ceiling, and a better count corrects it, since each commitment carries its notice period on paper; not Date bomb, which is one step on the calendar, since this is the shape of the whole burn under the operator's own hand.

Cost of the coffin: dying costs money, as the final payroll, the accrued leave, the lease break, the deposits returned, the accountant who closes the books, so the line at which a firm must stop is not zero but zero plus the cost of stopping cleanly, and the founder who runs the balance to nothing has already crossed it; the carrier is the wind-down bill, the cash figure misreads zero for the floor, and a better count corrects it; the creditor's covenant that calls the loan at a minimum balance draws the same line from outside, and sits here rather than under Watched burn because it is a written number, not an inference.

Near the pole: runway is cash over net burn, and net burn is the difference of two large flows, so two operators with identical months differ by how close their burn sits to the pole where income covers it, as a shop taking in ninety and spending a hundred has the same three months as a startup taking in nothing and spending ten, and only the shop can multiply its runway by a ten-percent cut; the carrier is the ratio of the gross flows to their difference, the cash figure misreads a point for the steepness of the curve the point sits on, and counting corrects it, but only if the gross flows are counted and not the net.

Hurry discount: assets counted at what they would fetch with time to sell fetch less the less time there is, as the inventory, the machinery, the house, the domain name, so the runway sets the pile's price and the pile's price sets the runway, and a first shortening of the clock shortens it again through the pile; the carrier is the depth of the market for a seller in a hurry, the cash figure misreads a stock as if its price stood still while the clock ran, and a count corrects it only by putting the clock inside the price and solving for the point where the two agree.

Watched burn: a burn that counterparties can see is repriced as they see it, as the landlord who asks for a larger deposit, the supplier who moves to cash on delivery, the investor who reads the bank statement, the buyer whose diligence finds the runway and waits for the price to fall, so terms tighten as the clock shortens and shorten it further; the carrier is the counterparties' inference from what they can observe, the cash figure misreads terms as fixed when they are a function of the perceived clock, and the correction is not a better count of the ledger but a count of what others can see of it.

The front: a runway that runs on the belief that it is long, as the house with no cash behind it, the firm that pays every vendor late but on an exact schedule, the officer's mess bill, so credit flows as long as the belief does and the death arrives on the day of the discovery rather than the day of the zero; the carrier is others' belief used as collateral, the cash figure misreads the clock as continuous when it ends at a step set by an exposure, and no count corrects it, since the quantity is a belief; Watched burn with the sign reversed: there, being seen shortens, here, not being seen lengthens.

Receivable from the dying: money owed to you by a customer whose own clock runs on your weather, as the subcontractor owed by a builder in a housing bust or the freelancer owed by the agency that lost the same client, so the receivable is a loan to someone whose death is correlated with yours, and it arrives as cash when least needed and as a loss when most; the carrier is the customer's balance sheet, the cash figure misreads a dated claim for cash to come, and a better count corrects the ageing but not the correlation, which appears only when the customer's runway is counted too.

Forbearance clock: a debt with no schedule, as the family loan, the supplier who lets the invoice slide, the tax authority that has not yet noticed, the credit line uncalled, is due at the creditor's discretion, and the creditor's discretion runs on the creditor's own runway, so the debt is patient exactly until the creditor is in trouble, which need not be when you are, and is when you are whenever the two of you share weather; the carrier is the creditor's clock, the cash figure misreads an uncalled debt as not due, and no count of your own ledger corrects it, since the due date lives in someone else's; Receivable from the dying on the other side of the sheet.

Too expensive to let die: a runway carried by the cost of your death to others, as the only doctor in the district, the engineer who alone knows the plant, the tenant whose leaving would empty a building in a bad market, so counterparties who could call the debt do not, because replacing you costs more than carrying you; the carrier is their replacement cost, the cash figure misreads your clock as yours when it is theirs, and it is corrected only by counting what your death costs someone else; not Forbearance clock, which runs on the creditor's health, since a creditor in trouble who cannot replace you keeps you alive for as long as it expects a future in which to need you, though a creditor in receivership has no replacement cost, since it has no future to replace you in, and its receiver calls the debt; and not a leverage, since nothing is exercised.

Lien of blood: savings that are yours on the statement and a family's in fact, as the immigrant whose balance is also a sibling's tuition and a parent's surgery, the couple whose joint account is one partner's runway and the other's veto, so the disposable balance is the statement minus every claim that will be made before the death and enforced by no one but you; the carrier is kinship claims on no ledger, the cash figure misreads ownership for disposability, and counting the claims corrects it, which most people can do and do not; the parents' spare room, on no ledger and lengthening the clock at a price in standing, is the same carrier with the sign flipped, and its price belongs to the status maps.

Weakest wallet: a group's runway is not the pooled cash but the shortest private clock among members who can leave, as the band that ends when the drummer's savings do, the founding team whose firm has eighteen months while a founder's own rent has four, so the group dies at the first departure and not at the pooled zero; the carrier is the members' separate accounts joined to their exit option, the cash figure misreads the pooled balance for the group's time, and counting each wallet corrects it; the monastery, one purse and no private clock, is the case where the pooled count is right, and shows that the illusion is the exit option and not the pooling.

Any-town skill: a skill that is cash in any town lengthens the runway to the time it takes to move, while a skill that is cash only here shortens it to the cash, as the nurse or the welder against the fixer who knows this council, the session player known in this scene, the courtier; the carrier is the geography of the market for the skill, the cash figure misreads the pile for the pump, and it is corrected only by counting where the skill sells and at what discount, which is a count of a market you are not yet in; not a floor under income, which is what the skill fetches, since here only where it fetches it matters, and the location of the floor is what sets the clock.

The back: the body is the asset that produces the income and is drawn down by producing it, as the carpenter's back, the nurse's nights, the surgeon's hands, the drummer's hearing, so the double shift that lengthens the cash runway spends the body's, and the two clocks run in opposite directions; the carrier is work capacity, the cash figure misreads the income as free of depreciation, and no count corrects it without a second ledger in a second unit, which is a change of what is counted; the ship's hull kept afloat by deferred repair is the firm's back, and comes due as a Date bomb with no date printed.

Stamp's clock: a permission that expires on a date no cash extends, as the visa's sixty-day grace, the enlistment, the student's enrolment, the parole, the license that lapses without hours logged, so the death is the stamp's date whenever it falls before the cash's, and every month of cash past it is worth nothing here; the carrier is the issuing authority's calendar, the cash figure misreads money for time where the two do not convert, and no count of money corrects it, since the clock is in a unit money does not buy; not Date bomb, whose step is cleared by paying.

Runway in shots: for anyone who must find a thing before the cash ends, a founder's product, a scientist's result, an actor's part, a prospector's seam, the runway is not months but trials, so halving the burn doubles the months and may leave the shots unchanged if the cut removed the trial capacity, and the same firm with three months is short at one shot a month and long at ten; the carrier is the trial rate, the cash figure misreads time for attempts, and the correction is a change of unit, not a better count; here the clock is not time at all, so no count in months, however good, touches it.

source.register: Operator-grade and concrete: leases, vesting dates, receivership weekends, severance, fire sales, subcontractors, mess bills, visas, district doctors, bands, immigrants, carpenters, a monastery; mechanisms with the misread quantity named, not advice.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism. Two loop claims (the pile's price depends on the clock; terms depend on the perceived clock) are analytical and marked in the limits. Runway in shots is analytical in its cases and speculative in its generality, and the limits say where its contrast disappears. No invented worlds.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a taxonomy of insolvency or a model of it; a real case runs several of these at once, and the list claims no coverage.

The seriation is an itinerary of how far the real clock lies from the cash ledger, not a ranking of danger, size, or frequency; map edges are conditional authored claims, and the two loops (Watched burn with Hurry discount, and the front's belief) are analytical, not measured.

The illustrative cases (a bank receivership weekend, a visa grace period, a subcontractor in a housing bust, an officer's mess bill, a district doctor) are simplified to one mechanism each and are not claims about specific histories, firms, or jurisdictions.

Runway in shots assumes the search has a trial rate that a burn cut can remove; where trials are nearly free, as a writer's drafts, the contrast with months disappears, so the item's generality is speculative and its cases are the ones where trials cost money.

Floors under income belong to the sibling map survival-floors and the price of a fall in standing to the status maps; here only the clock. The operator's nerve, the panicked exit that arrives before zero, was left as an unresolved seed rather than admitted, since its mechanism is not yet separable from mood. Adjacent to clocks-that-are-not-clocks, which reads durations off states; every item here is a clock read against the cash figure, and adds what the figure misreads.

seriation.axis: How far the real clock lies from the cash ledger: from arithmetic the ledger could have done itself (a calendar, a floor under burn, an access column, a fixed point for the pile), through counterparties who hold part of your clock in their ledgers or their beliefs, through the household, the coalition, and a market you are not yet in, to quantities in no monetary unit at all (the body, a stamp, a count of trials).
seriation.note: An authored itinerary, not a scale of severity or of how often each occurs. Date bomb opens it because the correction is a calendar the operator already owns; Runway in shots closes it because there the clock is not time. The route answers the live question in three grades rather than two: items from Date bomb through Hurry discount are corrected by counting better inside one ledger; Watched burn through Any-town skill are corrected by counting someone else's ledger, belief, or market, which is still counting but not yours; The back through Runway in shots are corrected only by changing the unit. The hinge is Hurry discount → Watched burn: the discount is the last illusion solvable inside your own books, a fixed point where the clock and the pile's price agree, and it is also the mechanism by which your books become visible, since the hurried sale is what the counterparty sees, so counting better tips into counting what others count. The second turn is Any-town skill → The back: the skill's correction is a count of wages in another town, so it is the last carrier priced in money, and the body is the first that money does not buy; the critic moved Any-town skill here from the non-monetary grade, where the author had filed it, since its own correction is priced. Reach the cliff sits beside Date bomb because the two are the same calendar read up and down, and the adjacency teaches that a step down is cleared by having the cash at the date while a step up is raced for by spending whatever reaches it, so the same cut is a cure for one and a loss for the other. Too expensive to let die sits between Forbearance clock and Lien of blood because it is the last runway held by a stranger before the route enters the family.

relations.from: Date bomb: an obligation that arrives as a step rather than a slope, as the lease that renews in September, the annual premium, the tax bill in April, the tuition due before the school year, so the death is at the first step the balance cannot clear and not at the month the average burn predicts; the carrier is the calendar, the cash figure misreads a staircase as a ramp, and a better count corrects it, since the schedule was always on paper; the seasonal case, the fisherman's winter or the nine-month salary, is the same staircase repeated.
relations.to: Stamp's clock: a permission that expires on a date no cash extends, as the visa's sixty-day grace, the enlistment, the student's enrolment, the parole, the license that lapses without hours logged, so the death is the stamp's date whenever it falls before the cash's, and every month of cash past it is worth nothing here; the carrier is the issuing authority's calendar, the cash figure misreads money for time where the two do not convert, and no count of money corrects it, since the clock is in a unit money does not buy; not Date bomb, whose step is cleared by paying.
relations.label: If the step at the date cannot be cleared by any payment, the Date bomb is a Stamp's clock and the calendar stops being the ledger's; the fork at every dated death is whether cash converts to time, and the visa that a fee could extend sits on the bomb side while the grace period no fee extends sits on the stamp side.

relations.from: Lien of blood: savings that are yours on the statement and a family's in fact, as the immigrant whose balance is also a sibling's tuition and a parent's surgery, the couple whose joint account is one partner's runway and the other's veto, so the disposable balance is the statement minus every claim that will be made before the death and enforced by no one but you; the carrier is kinship claims on no ledger, the cash figure misreads ownership for disposability, and counting the claims corrects it, which most people can do and do not; the parents' spare room, on no ledger and lengthening the clock at a price in standing, is the same carrier with the sign flipped, and its price belongs to the status maps.
relations.to: Weakest wallet: a group's runway is not the pooled cash but the shortest private clock among members who can leave, as the band that ends when the drummer's savings do, the founding team whose firm has eighteen months while a founder's own rent has four, so the group dies at the first departure and not at the pooled zero; the carrier is the members' separate accounts joined to their exit option, the cash figure misreads the pooled balance for the group's time, and counting each wallet corrects it; the monastery, one purse and no private clock, is the case where the pooled count is right, and shows that the illusion is the exit option and not the pooling.
relations.label: If each member's statement is corrected for the claims on it, the private clocks shorten below what any member admits, and the group's clock is the minimum of the corrected clocks; the lien passes from a person's ledger to the coalition's, so a team that counts only the firm's cash is wrong twice, once per wallet and once at the minimum.

relations.from: Receivable from the dying: money owed to you by a customer whose own clock runs on your weather, as the subcontractor owed by a builder in a housing bust or the freelancer owed by the agency that lost the same client, so the receivable is a loan to someone whose death is correlated with yours, and it arrives as cash when least needed and as a loss when most; the carrier is the customer's balance sheet, the cash figure misreads a dated claim for cash to come, and a better count corrects the ageing but not the correlation, which appears only when the customer's runway is counted too.
relations.to: Forbearance clock: a debt with no schedule, as the family loan, the supplier who lets the invoice slide, the tax authority that has not yet noticed, the credit line uncalled, is due at the creditor's discretion, and the creditor's discretion runs on the creditor's own runway, so the debt is patient exactly until the creditor is in trouble, which need not be when you are, and is when you are whenever the two of you share weather; the carrier is the creditor's clock, the cash figure misreads an uncalled debt as not due, and no count of your own ledger corrects it, since the due date lives in someone else's; Receivable from the dying on the other side of the sheet.
relations.label: If the customer who owes you and the creditor who carries you share your weather, then the receivable fails and the forbearance ends in the same month, and the two sides of the sheet, counted separately as an asset ageing and a debt not yet due, fail as one event; the correlation is between the counterparties, not within either column.

relations.from: Forbearance clock: a debt with no schedule, as the family loan, the supplier who lets the invoice slide, the tax authority that has not yet noticed, the credit line uncalled, is due at the creditor's discretion, and the creditor's discretion runs on the creditor's own runway, so the debt is patient exactly until the creditor is in trouble, which need not be when you are, and is when you are whenever the two of you share weather; the carrier is the creditor's clock, the cash figure misreads an uncalled debt as not due, and no count of your own ledger corrects it, since the due date lives in someone else's; Receivable from the dying on the other side of the sheet.
relations.to: Too expensive to let die: a runway carried by the cost of your death to others, as the only doctor in the district, the engineer who alone knows the plant, the tenant whose leaving would empty a building in a bad market, so counterparties who could call the debt do not, because replacing you costs more than carrying you; the carrier is their replacement cost, the cash figure misreads your clock as yours when it is theirs, and it is corrected only by counting what your death costs someone else; not Forbearance clock, which runs on the creditor's health, since a creditor in trouble who cannot replace you keeps you alive for as long as it expects a future in which to need you, though a creditor in receivership has no replacement cost, since it has no future to replace you in, and its receiver calls the debt; and not a leverage, since nothing is exercised.
relations.label: If the creditor's own clock is short but not out and you cannot be replaced, the forbearance outlives the creditor's trouble, since replacement cost overrides the creditor's health for as long as the creditor expects a future in which to need you; past the creditor's own death the override fails, a receiver has no replacement cost, and the runway that had moved from the creditor's ledger to the creditor's dependence ends with the creditor, so the operator who raises the cost of their own death has bought time bounded by the creditor's.

relations.from: Near the pole: runway is cash over net burn, and net burn is the difference of two large flows, so two operators with identical months differ by how close their burn sits to the pole where income covers it, as a shop taking in ninety and spending a hundred has the same three months as a startup taking in nothing and spending ten, and only the shop can multiply its runway by a ten-percent cut; the carrier is the ratio of the gross flows to their difference, the cash figure misreads a point for the steepness of the curve the point sits on, and counting corrects it, but only if the gross flows are counted and not the net.
relations.to: Runway in shots: for anyone who must find a thing before the cash ends, a founder's product, a scientist's result, an actor's part, a prospector's seam, the runway is not months but trials, so halving the burn doubles the months and may leave the shots unchanged if the cut removed the trial capacity, and the same firm with three months is short at one shot a month and long at ten; the carrier is the trial rate, the cash figure misreads time for attempts, and the correction is a change of unit, not a better count; here the clock is not time at all, so no count in months, however good, touches it.
relations.label: If the burn that can be cut is the burn that buys trials, then a cut that moves the firm toward the pole lengthens the runway in months and shortens it in shots; the two units disagree about whether the cut helped, and the pole is a pole in months only, since a firm at breakeven with no trials has an infinite runway and no way to arrive.

exploration.first_question: Where does a person's or a firm's real time-to-death differ from what its cash over its burn says: which mechanism holds the difference, what carries it, and what does the cash figure misread?
exploration.changed_question: Is the clock cash at all, and which runways change length when they are counted? The first breath assumed death was the cash reaching zero and looked for mis-scheduled steps and mis-counted counterparties. Sharpening Watched burn against The front showed a runway whose length is a function of its own reading, sharpening Cost of the coffin showed the death line is above zero, and both together asked whether the answer must be a number of months. The second breath found the loop through the pile (Hurry discount), the clocks held by others (Too expensive to let die, Weakest wallet), and two runways in units money does not convert to (Stamp's clock, Runway in shots).

priorities.why: It can be run on public numbers, it separates operators the months figure calls identical, and it is the cleanest test of the map's first grade, that some illusions vanish under a better count of the same ledger.
priorities.next_question: Take ten small firms with the same reported months of runway and write each one's gross inflow and gross outflow beside the net; recompute the months after a ten-percent cut to outflow for each; the spread of the recomputed months across firms that started equal is the size of the illusion, and the firm whose months go to infinity is the one sitting on the pole.
