relations.to: Advance against the crop: a debt that converts into a claim on future labour, as the sharecropper's advance of seed and food against the harvest, the company store's tab, the boat-owner who advances the fisherman's season, the kiln-owner's loan against the season's bricks; the floor conserves calories now, is paid by the future, and standing on it costs the future, since the creditor profits from the debt continuing and keeps the books, so the floor deepens with each use and inverts into a keeper; the oldest floor on the map; not Creditor's chair, where the creditor's interest turned to your success, and not the indenture, whose term is fixed and clears, since a debt with a date is a price and this floor has none.
relations.label: If the unpaid debt converts into a share of the upside, the creditor's interest turns to your success; if it converts into a claim on your labour, the creditor's interest is that the debt never clears, so one floor, the debt you cannot pay, forks at the conversion into an ally and a keeper, and which branch you are on is decided by what the creditor is able to take.

relations.from: Kept on call: a retainer that pays to keep you available is a floor that is really an option someone else holds, as the client who pays a monthly fee for first call on a lawyer, a plumber, a designer; the floor conserves a monthly minimum, is paid by the client as the premium on your time, and standing on it costs the better work, since the option can be exercised at the moment you are busiest and takes no account of it, and the floor holds only under light use: never called, it is cancelled at renewal as waste, always called, it is a job at their rate; not a salary, since nothing is owed for the hours, and not a job, since the trigger is in another hand.
relations.to: Uncalled favour: a specific debt owed to you and never called, as the old boss's referral, the mentor's phone call, the client who said anytime, is worth the largest thing it could be asked for, and calling it collapses it to the thing asked; the floor conserves one full draw, is paid by the one who owes, and standing on it costs the account, since the first call closes it and the caller is now the one who asked; adds to exchange-ontologies' Obligation futures and pivot-invariants' war chest of favours the collapse rule, that the favour is sized only at the call and sized once; the map's far pole, consumed entirely by the first step.
relations.label: If the retainer lapses for want of calls and is let go with an 'anytime' rather than a rupture, what remains is the client's sense of having been kept, an uncalled favour of unknown size held by the one who was on call, so the floor that lived by light use decays into the floor that dies by the first call; the passage runs one way, since a called favour does not become a retainer, and it fails where the client leaves feeling they paid for nothing, since then the favour is owed the other way.

relations.from: Plot that must be tended: a right to feed oneself outside any wage, as the allotment, the grazing right on the common, the village fishing berth, the squatter's occupation, keeps a floor under food that no employer can remove, and lapses with non-use, since the allotment tenancy is ended for non-cultivation, the customary right is presumed abandoned after long disuse, and the squatter's claim exists only while in possession, and once that claim ripens into title it is property and leaves the map; the floor conserves calories and a place, is paid for in fair-weather labour the wage could have bought better, and standing on it costs mobility, since the plot cannot come with you; not property, which keeps while unused, but a floor that exists only by being stood on.
relations.to: Advance against the crop: a debt that converts into a claim on future labour, as the sharecropper's advance of seed and food against the harvest, the company store's tab, the boat-owner who advances the fisherman's season, the kiln-owner's loan against the season's bricks; the floor conserves calories now, is paid by the future, and standing on it costs the future, since the creditor profits from the debt continuing and keeps the books, so the floor deepens with each use and inverts into a keeper; the oldest floor on the map; not Creditor's chair, where the creditor's interest turned to your success, and not the indenture, whose term is fixed and clears, since a debt with a date is a price and this floor has none.
relations.label: If the tended plot's harvest fails, the advance against the next crop is the only floor left and its terms are the landlord's, and the advance keeps the plot tended, since the crop is the collateral; the loop closes, and the tenant tends the plot to pay the advance taken because the plot failed, which the route shows as two distant items.

relations.from: Sponsor's promise: a floor under future income promised by the party whose failure is the risk it insures, as the company pension, the founder's promise of back pay, the firm's severance policy; the floor conserves a future income, is paid by the sponsor's future, and standing on it costs the cliff, the years to vesting, and the correlation, since the promise fails in the very weather it was for, as the Studebaker pensioners learned when the plant closed; not insurance, which is the same promise from a stranger whose weather is not yours, and the worst-shaped floor on the map.
relations.to: Accident only: a priced floor from a stranger, as the disability policy, the income-protection policy, the crop insurance, pays in cash and leaves no debt in standing, because the premium was paid before the fall; the floor conserves cash, is paid by the premium and by the other policyholders whose falls did not come, and standing on it costs the exclusions and the repricing, since the stranger covers what happened to you and refuses what you did, the quit, the risk you chose, the pre-existing, and raises the premium after the claim; not Prove the fall, which covers the chosen fall after proof and a wait, and not kin, who cover both at a price in rank.
relations.label: If the sponsor is the employer, the promise fails in the weather it insures and becomes a floor only when a stranger takes it, an insurer or a guarantee fund, so the sponsor's floor depends on a second hand whose weather is not yours; can recruit: if the sponsor is solvent enough to buy the stranger's policy, which is when the floor was least needed.

relations.from: Kin policy, premium after the claim: family insures against failure and pays in kind, a bed, a meal, a room over the shop, as the adult child who moves back, the cousin taken into the business, the widow at her brother's table; the floor conserves bed and food, is paid by kin in kind and enforced by no ledger, and standing on it costs a premium paid after the claim, in obligation and in rank, since the returning child is a child again and the claim is never settled, because kin refuse the cash that would settle it; the reverse policy, children as their parents' pension, is the same policy with the premium paid before; adds to runway-illusions' Lien of blood, which counts the claims on your savings, the payout side and its price in rank.
relations.to: Prove the fall: a means-tested floor is reachable only by proving no other floor exists, as unemployment assistance with an asset test, the parish relief, the hardship fund; the floor conserves a cash minimum, is paid by the taxpayer or the pool, and standing on it costs the other floors first, since the test counts the savings, and where its rule reaches them the roof's equity and the family's bed and board, and demands they be spent, and then the record of having stood there; a floor that is a wall in front of the others, whose height is set by what the test can see; not insurance, since the claim is not a premium paid but a state proven; invisible while floors were counted side by side.
relations.label: If the test reads only cash and kin pay in kind, the test sees nothing and both floors hold; if kin pay in cash, or the test reckons a bed and a meal as income, as a rule that counts in-kind support does, the state's floor closes; so whether the two floors can be stood on together is decided by the unit the family pays in set against the unit the test reads, and not by how much is given.

exploration.first_question: What keeps a floor under a person's or a small firm's income or standing when the main source fails, beyond a pile of cash: which institutions, claims, rights, and debts catch the fall, what does each conserve, who pays for it, and what does standing on it cost later?
exploration.changed_question: What does standing on a floor do to the floor, and to the other floors: which are kept only by being used, which are consumed by the first step, and which are walls in front of the rest? The first breath treated floors as reserves held side by side; sharpening the retainer, cancelled when never called and absorbed when always called, against the family bed, never settled once claimed, produced an axis of use rather than of size, and asking what a means test counts produced a floor that requires the others' destruction.
exploration.new_member: Prove the fall: a means-tested floor is reachable only by proving no other floor exists, as unemployment assistance with an asset test, the parish relief, the hardship fund; the floor conserves a cash minimum, is paid by the taxpayer or the pool, and standing on it costs the other floors first, since the test counts the savings, and where its rule reaches them the roof's equity and the family's bed and board, and demands they be spent, and then the record of having stood there; a floor that is a wall in front of the others, whose height is set by what the test can see; not insurance, since the claim is not a premium paid but a state proven; invisible while floors were counted side by side.

priorities.item: Kept on call: a retainer that pays to keep you available is a floor that is really an option someone else holds, as the client who pays a monthly fee for first call on a lawyer, a plumber, a designer; the floor conserves a monthly minimum, is paid by the client as the premium on your time, and standing on it costs the better work, since the option can be exercised at the moment you are busiest and takes no account of it, and the floor holds only under light use: never called, it is cancelled at renewal as waste, always called, it is a job at their rate; not a salary, since nothing is owed for the hours, and not a job, since the trigger is in another hand.
priorities.why: It is an arrangement of incentives that can be varied on paper, and its two-sided erosion is a prediction rather than a description: renewal should peak in a band of light use and fail at both ends, which a freelancer's own books can test.
priorities.next_question: From a freelancer's or a small firm's books, or a fictional set of twenty retainers, record for each month the calls made and the fee, and at each renewal whether the retainer was renewed, cancelled, or converted into a scoped job; the prediction is that renewals cluster in a band of light use, that zero-call retainers are cancelled and saturated ones converted, and the probe is to find the band's edges and whether one small call a month keeps a retainer alive.

priorities.item: Roost ledger: a floor sized by one's own giving history, as vampire bats that fail to feed for two nights are fed by roost-mates who regurgitate blood, and are fed most by those they themselves fed when fat, the ledger living in the recipients' memory; the floor conserves a night's meal, is paid by past recipients who remember, and standing on it costs the ledger itself, since a meal taken is a meal owed and the balance that sized the floor is drawn down by the draw, so this floor is fed by giving and spent by taking and is only there for those who paid out when they could, and the stingy have none; observed in bats, analytical in people, as the freelancer fed by those she once passed work to; not Burial club, whose contributions are fixed and whose ledger is a book, since here the floor strengthens with giving.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that a human institution can keep its ledger in recipients' memory at any scale, high generative promise: it is the only floor on the map that gets stronger the more is given into it, and the only one both fed and spent by use, and no human mutual-aid rule is built on giving history alone rather than on dues.
priorities.next_question: Run a tabletop with eight players, each with a private random schedule of failed months and tokens to give, under two rules in turn: fixed dues with fixed payouts (the club), and payouts sized by what each recipient remembers receiving from the claimant (the roost); count how many players survive under each rule when failures are independent and when they are correlated, and whether the roost rule starves anyone who was merely unlucky early.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after repairing nine items whose illustrative cases broke their own discriminators or misstated a price, moving Countercyclical hand among the floors kept by use, and relabeling three edges: two whose antecedents held only for means tests that read cash alone, and one whose residual favour needed a holder and a condition under which it fails.

neighbors.left: Burial club: a pool of peers whose failures are uncorrelated, as the burial society, the rotating credit circle, the friendly society, the crew's kitty, keeps a floor under a lump at one's turn; the floor conserves the lump, is paid by members in advance and enforced by shame among equals, and standing on it costs the obligation to keep paying at others' turns after one's own failure, and the pool dies in the weather that fails everyone at once, as the village whose harvest is one harvest; adds to cooperation-mechanisms' insurance pools and joint liability the correlation condition and the premium that continues after the claim; not kin, whose premium comes after and whose enforcement is rank.
neighbors.right: Roost ledger: a floor sized by one's own giving history, as vampire bats that fail to feed for two nights are fed by roost-mates who regurgitate blood, and are fed most by those they themselves fed when fat, the ledger living in the recipients' memory; the floor conserves a night's meal, is paid by past recipients who remember, and standing on it costs the ledger itself, since a meal taken is a meal owed and the balance that sized the floor is drawn down by the draw, so this floor is fed by giving and spent by taking and is only there for those who paid out when they could, and the stingy have none; observed in bats, analytical in people, as the freelancer fed by those she once passed work to; not Burial club, whose contributions are fixed and whose ledger is a book, since here the floor strengthens with giving.
neighbors.separating_case: Two members of a fishing crew's kitty, one who paid dues every month and never once covered a mate's share, and one who paid dues and also covered three mates in their bad seasons, both lose a season: the kitty pays each the same fixed sum, since the club's ledger is dues, and would pay neither if the whole fleet's season failed; the roost would feed the second and starve the first, since its ledger is what each gave beyond the rule. The club floors the contributor and the roost floors the giver, and a fleet-wide failure kills the club while leaving the roost's ledger intact but unpayable.

checks.boundary_case: The emergency fund is out: cash under the mattress is what the floors conserve, has no second hand on it and no use-rule, and the map sees it only as the thing Prove the fall counts and makes you spend. A second job is out on the same ground unless its demand runs against the first's, which is exactly the contrast Countercyclical hand is in on: a second source that fails with the first is a second exposure, not a floor.
checks.form_inference: The map shows an incompatibility the route conceals: Roof as piggy bank and Prove the fall sit far apart on the itinerary, but the edge between them says that a means test which counts the roof's equity makes the two floors exclusive, since reaching one requires spending the other. It shows a fork at Creditor's chair → Advance against the crop, where one floor, the debt you cannot pay, becomes an ally or a keeper depending on what the creditor can take. It shows a loop at Plot that must be tended → Advance against the crop, where the failed plot recruits the advance and the advance keeps the plot tended, a circle the sharecropper never leaves. It shows a passage between the two poles at Kept on call → Uncalled favour, where a floor kept by light use decays into a floor spent by the first call. And it shows two dependencies the sequence cannot state: Sponsor's promise is a floor only if a stranger's hand takes the promise, and whether Kin policy and Prove the fall can be stood on together is decided by the unit the family pays in set against the unit the test reads.
checks.target_preserved: Judged by the Fable critic in a fresh context: the item type and the axis of use survived every case the critic threw at them; the strange members (a retainer that is the client's option, a roost ledger kept in recipients' memory and now read as fed by giving and spent by taking, a legislated list of what a bailiff may not take, a state floor that is a wall in front of the others whose height is what the test can see) are kept as mechanisms rather than softened into advice about diversifying income; nine items were repaired where a case in the author's own list broke the item's discriminator (the medallion that is property, the cook without a registry, the funeral player whose weather is merely different, the prison that takes the exit right, the indenture that clears, the squatter whose claim ripens into property) or where a price or a correlation was asserted beyond what the mechanism supplies, and three edges were relabeled where an antecedent held only for one kind of means test or left the favour's holder unstated, with no strange mechanism replaced by a respectable one.

name: who-can-be-bound
of: A mechanism by which a party becomes bindable, so that a promise to or from it can carry weight, named with the hold (what of the party's can be reached, kept, cut, or lost), the carrier that keeps the hold in someone's hand, a market that exists only because of that hold and one that fails without it, the escape from the hold, and how long a stranger needs to acquire it: walked in with, bought at the door, imported from a stay done elsewhere, or accrued only by staying here.
items: Body that can be brought: a party with nothing else is bindable because it can be found, held, and made to appear, so the assetless are bound by custody where the propertied are bound by money, as a fine unpaid becomes a night in jail and a summons ignored becomes a warrant; the bail bond is a market that exists only because a body can be retrieved, since the bondsman prices the recoverability of a body, and no small claim can be brought against a body the court cannot reach; escaped by flight past the reach of whoever must bring it; the hold everyone walks in with, and therefore the hold on the poor.

Kneecap: a party the courts cannot reach is bindable by anyone who can hurt it, so lending to the judgment-proof exists outside the law wherever the lender can reach the borrower's body, as the loan shark and the protection racket lend and insure at rates no court would enforce; not custody, which needs a state to hold the body, but harm, which needs only an asymmetry of force, so it is escaped by acquiring protection or force of one's own, and the market fails the moment the borrower can hit back; walked in with, needing no institution, and for that reason the hold that fills every gap the other holds leave.

Tap: a party becomes bindable the moment it depends on a flow the other side can cut, as the postpaid electricity account, the cloud tenancy, the payment processor, the app store, each of which binds its customer by disconnection rather than by any court; postpaid utility service to strangers exists only because the tap can be shut, and where winter moratoria forbid the cutoff the utility demands a deposit instead; escaped by multi-homing or by becoming too important to cut, as a hospital is; not a license, which a third party revokes to protect others, but a flow the creditor itself withholds, in either direction, the supply a seller can cut or the custom a buyer can withdraw, so the supplier who tooled a line for one customer is bound by that customer's orders; the one hold a stranger acquires within the hour, by needing.

Deposit at the door: a party posts value into the other's hand before anything is owed, forfeited on breach, as the security deposit, the earnest money, the training bond a new pilot signs, the margin at a clearinghouse; rental housing to strangers exists only because of it, and a stranger with nothing to post is not unbindable but unhoused; escaped by breaching for more than the deposit, since the hold is capped at its amount, and undone by the holder's own temptation to keep it wrongly, which is why a large deposit needs a custodian neither party controls; bought in a day at the price of liquidity, so it is the binding of the newly arrived who have cash and a toll on those who do not.

Ugly hostage: a party hands over a token worth much to it and nothing to the holder, as the car title in a title loan, the diploma a school keeps until fees are paid, the passport an employer holds under kafala, the arrangement Williamson called an ugly hostage; title lending exists only because the paper is useless to the lender and indispensable to the borrower, so the holder is never tempted to keep it wrongly and no custodian is needed, which the same loan against cash could not say; escaped by reissue, since a passport reported lost or a duplicate title unmakes the hold, so it lasts exactly as long as the token cannot be replaced; adjacent to cooperation-ignitions' Hostage before the ask, which is a first move, this is the standing hold and its failure by duplication; handed over in a day.

Rented door: a party becomes bindable on paper by naming a place at which it agrees to be deemed found, so that a summons left there counts as received whether or not anyone read it, as a Delaware company buys a registered agent's address for a small annual fee and a tenant gives an address the landlord can nail a notice to; what is held is the party's plea of ignorance, since silence at the door becomes a default judgment, and contracting with an entity nobody will ever visit exists only because it can be served, while a person of no fixed abode cannot rent, bank, or be sued, which leaves them bindable only by body; not escaped by letting the door lapse, since a resigned agent is replaced by the Secretary of State and returned mail by a notice posted on the door, so that lapse only speeds the default, but only by never renting one, which forfeits every paper market at once; not a body, which must be brought, but a place where ignorance can no longer be claimed, bought in a day for the cost of the rent.

Keep the car: the hold arises from the shape of the trade itself when the thing worked on sits in the worker's hands, as the garage keeps the car, the tailor the suit, the innkeeper the luggage, the warehouse the grain, until the bill is paid; repair to strangers exists only because the object can be held, and the same trade on an object that cannot be held, a roof, a field, a standing crop, fails until statute invents a registered lien on the house in the garage's place, while the ship repaired and gone to sea is held by no registry but by arrest in the next port, which is the crossing's hold; escaped by abandoning the thing when it is worth less than the bill, so a hold on a wreck holds nothing; acquired the moment the thing is handed over, needing no deposit, no court, no name.

Held-back pay: the party is owed a stream the other side has not yet paid, and the unpaid remainder is the hold, as retainage keeps a tenth of every construction invoice until the defects are fixed, the sharecropper's share waits for harvest, the commission waits out the return window; hiring a stranger to build exists only because the last tenth can be withheld, and the prepaid builder who vanishes is the market that fails without it; not a deposit, which is the party's own cash posted before work and costs it liquidity, but the counterparty's money not yet paid, binding from the first invoice and costing nothing up front; escaped in the last period, since a party owed nothing further is bound by nothing further, which is why final payments are disputed and warranties are bonded; acquired by beginning the work.

Someone to sue: a promise can be enforced only against a thing the law recognizes as able to bear an obligation, so a market wanting a side that cannot be bound, a town before incorporation, a club, a protocol without a wrapper, a river, the unborn party to a hundred-year carbon contract, is born only when a proxy is deputized to stand for that side, and the proxy's own holds then govern the market; municipal bonds exist only because a city is a person that can be sued, and a club that is no person borrows only on its treasurer's own name, which is Cosigner and stops the day the treasurer will not sign; the trading twin of witness-architectures' Deputized injury, which names who may bring a harm, and the two come apart, since a river with a guardian can sue but nobody lends to a river, because no hold reaches the guardian's purse; escaped by dissolving the person or by immunity; bought in a day for a company, never for a river.

Seizable title: a party is bindable through property only if a registry ties the property to its name so that a creditor can find it and take it, as the land registry, the vehicle title, the filed lien; the mortgage exists only because of the registry, and, on de Soto's contested reading, lending against unregistered land fails wherever the deed cannot be searched, so the same house is collateral in one country and dead weight in the next; escaped by moving the asset past the registry's reach or into an exempt class, the homestead, the pension, the tools; adjacent to survival-floors' Tools the bailiff cannot take, which names the exemptions as a floor, this names what the exemptions are carved from; acquired only by owning something registered, which takes a purchase and a registry, not a day.

Hold at the crossing: a party immune where it stays is bindable through whatever it must send across a border, as a creditor had an Argentine naval training ship detained in a Ghanaian port in 2012, as an airline's aircraft can be repossessed wherever it lands under the Cape Town registry, as a payment in dollars must clear through New York; aircraft leasing to airlines in states whose courts will not enforce exists only because the plane travels, and sovereign lending fails wherever the sovereign keeps everything at home; escaped by not crossing, or by routing through friendly ports; not a seizable title, which sits still under one registry, but a hold that exists only during transit, so the immune are bound exactly as much as they need to move.

Cosigner: a party bound by nothing the creditor can reach borrows the bindability of someone who is, as the parent cosigns the lease, the sponsor signs the affidavit of support, the village group underwrites each member's microloan, the bank issues the letter of credit; renting to a student exists only because of it, and the immigrant with no cosigner meets the deposit instead; the mechanism is an arbitrage of holds, since the guarantor holds on the principal something the creditor lacks, shame, kinship, employment, and sells it priced in the cash the creditor can hold, so it binds only if the guarantor is bindable by another hold on this map and the principal is bindable by the guarantor; escaped when either link fails, the judgment-proof guarantor or the child past shaming; adjacent to exchange-ontologies' Vouching, which names the good, this names the conversion; imported in a day from a stay done elsewhere, by someone else.

Portable file: a stay done elsewhere binds here only if a registry carries its record out, as the credit bureau's file lets a lender bind a stranger it never met, a licensing board's record lets a nurse be hired in a town where nobody knows her, a passport carries a state's vouching across a border; unsecured lending to strangers exists only because of the file, and the credit-invisible newcomer, with a clean past and no record of it, is bound by deposit until a file accrues, as the secured card takes a deposit and returns it once a year of payments has been written; escaped by forging the file, the synthetic identity, or by moving past the registry's reach; not a small world, where the hold is remembered faces, but its export, which loses the face and gains the road; imported in a day from one's own stay elsewhere.

Rent as leash: a party is bound by a revocable permission exactly in proportion to what the permission is worth, so a license binds only through its scarcity, as a medical license is worth more than any single bribe and a taxi medallion at a million dollars bound its owner while the same medallion at a tenth of that bound nobody; surgery by a stranger exists only because the license can be pulled, and the unlicensed trades, the handyman, the mover, run on deposits and small worlds instead; escaped by being the marginal licensee to whom the license is worth little, or by practicing without one; adjacent to cooperation-mechanisms' sunsetting of privileges, which names the sanction, this names the leash's length as the rent, so that a licensor makes its licensees bindable by restricting entry; earned over years, and held by the licensor.

Name worth keeping: a judgment attaches to a name, so a party is bindable through its name only when the name is worth more to it than any single default, as a firm with a brand, a family with a name in the village, a person whose identity is the one thing it cannot replace; the warranty, the prepaid subscription, the long-dated contract exist only because the name will be there to answer, and the gift card from a pop-up fails with the pop-up; escaped by the phoenix, the company dissolved and re-formed under a new name with the old debts left on the corpse, and by the synthetic identity, which is the phoenix for persons; not reputation, which is what a name carries, but the persistence to which anything can attach at all; accrued by staying under one name, which is why a stranger's name binds nothing.

Small world: a party is bindable by memory alone when the set of its future counterparties is small enough that all of them will hear of a default by next week, as the diamond bourses trade parcels on a word and settle disputes by arbitration and expulsion, and, on one historian's reading, the medieval Maghribi traders bound agents across the Mediterranean by a coalition's shared memory; the handshake trade in stones exists only because the world is small, and the same handshake among strangers at a gem show fails, the parcel paid before it leaves the table; escaped by exit, which is why such worlds close their doors, since closure is the binding's carrier and not merely its prejudice; adjacent to cooperation-mechanisms' reputation legible to future partners, this names the bound on the world's size that makes the legibility bind; the denominator is the hold, and it is accrued only by staying long enough to be a face.

Place in line: a party is bound by an ordering it cannot transfer and would lose by leaving, as the pilot's seniority number, the union hall's out-of-work book, the tenure line, the resting order's time priority in an exchange's book, lost by cancelling and re-entering; the airline's investment in a pilot's training exists only because the pilot cannot take the number to another carrier, and the same airline binds the newcomer, whose number is worth nothing yet, by a training bond, a deposit, until the list takes over; not held-back pay, which is what the pension that vests at ten years and the equity that vests over four really are, since those are the counterparty's own money released by time, but a rank among peers that nobody owes and that every other list starts at the bottom; escaped only by the institution's own death, since a bankruptcy wipes the list, so the hold is only as good as the institution's name; adjacent to exchange-ontologies' Priority, which names the good, and survival-floors' Hiring hall, which names the floor, this names the hold the institution gets in return; accrued only by staying, and the purest such hold, since the wait itself is the deposit.

source.register: Mechanistic and concrete: bail, retainage, registered agents, title loans, seniority lists, credit files, port seizures; drawn from tenancy, construction, consumer credit, aviation finance, sovereign debt, licensing, and the diamond trade.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism; the day-or-stay reading of each hold is an authored simplification, one historical case is marked as contested, and no item is speculative.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not an empirical taxonomy or a partition; a real contract usually runs on several of these holds at once, and the list makes no claim to cover every kind.

The seriation is an itinerary by what the party must have done for the hold to exist, not a ranking of strength, legitimacy, or cost; the day-or-stay readings are authored simplifications, since a company is a day and a river never, and map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (bail bonding, title lending, kafala, retainage, the 2012 ship detention, the Cape Town registry, the diamond bourses, pilot seniority, the secured card) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about the full histories; the Maghribi coalition and de Soto's reading of unregistered land are contested readings and are marked so.

Whether a hold should exist is outside the list; Kneecap and Ugly hostage describe what a cruel hold does to a market's shape, not whether the cruelty is tolerable, and the map does not rank the holds by justice.

cooperation-mechanisms lists several of these holds as bare noun phrases (slashable collateral, hostages, exclusion from vital networks, legible reputation); this map is not a restatement, since its item is the hold with its carrier, its born and failing markets, its escape, and its time-to-acquire, and the walk and edges are what the bare phrases could not show. Holds that live in nobody's hand but the party's own, honor, oath, conscience, are outside, as the boundary case says.

seriation.axis: What the party must have done for the hold to exist: from holds everyone walks in with (a body that can be brought, a body that can be hurt), through holds bought at the door in an hour or a day (dependence on a tap, a deposit, a token handed over, a rented address, a thing left in the worker's hands, work begun), through holds that need an institution outside the two parties (a legal person, a registered title, a border crossed, a guarantor, a file carried out of a stay elsewhere), to holds that accrue only by staying here (a license worth its rent, a name with things attached, a face in a small world, a place in line).
seriation.note: An authored walk, not a scale of strength or a construction order. Body that can be brought opens it because nobody has to do anything for the hold to exist, which is why it is the hold on the poor; Place in line closes it because nothing but time can make it, which is why it is the hold on the loyal. The consequential adjacency is Cosigner → Portable file: both are imports of a stay done elsewhere, the cosigner imports someone else's and the file imports one's own, and the pair teaches that a stranger's day-one bindability is always somebody's staying, exported, so that the registry is the difference between needing a mother and needing a file. Deposit at the door → Ugly hostage is a second lesson, since the two are the same act, handing something over, and differ only in whether the holder could use it. The walk also crosses a second axis twice: the holds that need no judgment against the party itself (harm, tap, deposit, hostage, possession, held-back pay, name, small world, place in line) sit at both ends, and the holds that need one (a legal person, a registered title, a border crossed) occupy the middle, so that the stranger of a day and the villager of forty years are both bound without judgments, and judgments bind the party in between, who has stayed long enough to be registered and not long enough to be known. Body that can be brought opens the walk on the declared axis, since nothing must be done for it, but it is not court-free, since custody needs a state, a sheriff, and a jail; Kneecap is the court-free hold at the opening. Two placements are authored rather than derived: the middle segment (Someone to sue, Seizable title, Hold at the crossing) is sorted by the second axis, institution needed, though by time-to-acquire a company bought in a day would sit beside Rented door; and Rent as leash sits at the accrued end on the strength of the years a license takes to earn, though the rent binds from the day of issue and a license moves by endorsement, which is import.

relations.from: Body that can be brought: a party with nothing else is bindable because it can be found, held, and made to appear, so the assetless are bound by custody where the propertied are bound by money, as a fine unpaid becomes a night in jail and a summons ignored becomes a warrant; the bail bond is a market that exists only because a body can be retrieved, since the bondsman prices the recoverability of a body, and no small claim can be brought against a body the court cannot reach; escaped by flight past the reach of whoever must bring it; the hold everyone walks in with, and therefore the hold on the poor.
relations.to: Deposit at the door: a party posts value into the other's hand before anything is owed, forfeited on breach, as the security deposit, the earnest money, the training bond a new pilot signs, the margin at a clearinghouse; rental housing to strangers exists only because of it, and a stranger with nothing to post is not unbindable but unhoused; escaped by breaching for more than the deposit, since the hold is capped at its amount, and undone by the holder's own temptation to keep it wrongly, which is why a large deposit needs a custodian neither party controls; bought in a day at the price of liquidity, so it is the binding of the newly arrived who have cash and a toll on those who do not.
relations.label: If the party can post cash, the custody hold converts into a deposit and the body may leave, as bail does; if it cannot, the body stays, so the conversion out of the hold everyone walks in with is available only to those who already have the next hold.

relations.from: Deposit at the door: a party posts value into the other's hand before anything is owed, forfeited on breach, as the security deposit, the earnest money, the training bond a new pilot signs, the margin at a clearinghouse; rental housing to strangers exists only because of it, and a stranger with nothing to post is not unbindable but unhoused; escaped by breaching for more than the deposit, since the hold is capped at its amount, and undone by the holder's own temptation to keep it wrongly, which is why a large deposit needs a custodian neither party controls; bought in a day at the price of liquidity, so it is the binding of the newly arrived who have cash and a toll on those who do not.
relations.to: Portable file: a stay done elsewhere binds here only if a registry carries its record out, as the credit bureau's file lets a lender bind a stranger it never met, a licensing board's record lets a nurse be hired in a town where nobody knows her, a passport carries a state's vouching across a border; unsecured lending to strangers exists only because of the file, and the credit-invisible newcomer, with a clean past and no record of it, is bound by deposit until a file accrues, as the secured card takes a deposit and returns it once a year of payments has been written; escaped by forging the file, the synthetic identity, or by moving past the registry's reach; not a small world, where the hold is remembered faces, but its export, which loses the face and gains the road; imported in a day from one's own stay elsewhere.
relations.label: If the deposit is held long enough for a record of performance to be written against the party's name, the registry can return the cash and keep the file, as the secured card becomes an unsecured one; the hold passes from what the stranger posted to what the stranger did, a passage from a bought hold to an accrued one.

relations.label: If the file can be forged, as the synthetic identity forges it, the registry trusts a file only after anchoring its name to papers the state will prosecute a body for faking, so know-your-customer is the fraud statute reaching through the document to the body; the walk that left the body through bail returns to it through the criminal court, and no hold on this map escapes the loop except by staying.

relations.from: Keep the car: the hold arises from the shape of the trade itself when the thing worked on sits in the worker's hands, as the garage keeps the car, the tailor the suit, the innkeeper the luggage, the warehouse the grain, until the bill is paid; repair to strangers exists only because the object can be held, and the same trade on an object that cannot be held, a roof, a field, a standing crop, fails until statute invents a registered lien on the house in the garage's place, while the ship repaired and gone to sea is held by no registry but by arrest in the next port, which is the crossing's hold; escaped by abandoning the thing when it is worth less than the bill, so a hold on a wreck holds nothing; acquired the moment the thing is handed over, needing no deposit, no court, no name.
relations.to: Seizable title: a party is bindable through property only if a registry ties the property to its name so that a creditor can find it and take it, as the land registry, the vehicle title, the filed lien; the mortgage exists only because of the registry, and, on de Soto's contested reading, lending against unregistered land fails wherever the deed cannot be searched, so the same house is collateral in one country and dead weight in the next; escaped by moving the asset past the registry's reach or into an exempt class, the homestead, the pension, the tools; adjacent to survival-floors' Tools the bailiff cannot take, which names the exemptions as a floor, this names what the exemptions are carved from; acquired only by owning something registered, which takes a purchase and a registry, not a day.
relations.label: If the thing worked on cannot be held, a roof, a field, a standing crop, the possessory hold fails and must be re-created as a registered lien on the thing, which needs a registry and a court; where it can be held no court is needed, so the same trade forks by whether the object fits in a garage.

relations.from: Ugly hostage: a party hands over a token worth much to it and nothing to the holder, as the car title in a title loan, the diploma a school keeps until fees are paid, the passport an employer holds under kafala, the arrangement Williamson called an ugly hostage; title lending exists only because the paper is useless to the lender and indispensable to the borrower, so the holder is never tempted to keep it wrongly and no custodian is needed, which the same loan against cash could not say; escaped by reissue, since a passport reported lost or a duplicate title unmakes the hold, so it lasts exactly as long as the token cannot be replaced; adjacent to cooperation-ignitions' Hostage before the ask, which is a first move, this is the standing hold and its failure by duplication; handed over in a day.
relations.to: Deposit at the door: a party posts value into the other's hand before anything is owed, forfeited on breach, as the security deposit, the earnest money, the training bond a new pilot signs, the margin at a clearinghouse; rental housing to strangers exists only because of it, and a stranger with nothing to post is not unbindable but unhoused; escaped by breaching for more than the deposit, since the hold is capped at its amount, and undone by the holder's own temptation to keep it wrongly, which is why a large deposit needs a custodian neither party controls; bought in a day at the price of liquidity, so it is the binding of the newly arrived who have cash and a toll on those who do not.
relations.label: If the pledged thing is worth something to the holder, the holder is tempted to keep it wrongly and a custodian is needed; if it is worth nothing to the holder, no custodian is needed but no loss can be recovered from it either; a pledge cannot be both liquid to the holder and untempting, so escrow and the ugly hostage are alternatives, not degrees of one hold.

relations.from: Held-back pay: the party is owed a stream the other side has not yet paid, and the unpaid remainder is the hold, as retainage keeps a tenth of every construction invoice until the defects are fixed, the sharecropper's share waits for harvest, the commission waits out the return window; hiring a stranger to build exists only because the last tenth can be withheld, and the prepaid builder who vanishes is the market that fails without it; not a deposit, which is the party's own cash posted before work and costs it liquidity, but the counterparty's money not yet paid, binding from the first invoice and costing nothing up front; escaped in the last period, since a party owed nothing further is bound by nothing further, which is why final payments are disputed and warranties are bonded; acquired by beginning the work.
relations.to: Name worth keeping: a judgment attaches to a name, so a party is bindable through its name only when the name is worth more to it than any single default, as a firm with a brand, a family with a name in the village, a person whose identity is the one thing it cannot replace; the warranty, the prepaid subscription, the long-dated contract exist only because the name will be there to answer, and the gift card from a pop-up fails with the pop-up; escaped by the phoenix, the company dissolved and re-formed under a new name with the old debts left on the corpse, and by the synthetic identity, which is the phoenix for persons; not reputation, which is what a name carries, but the persistence to which anything can attach at all; accrued by staying under one name, which is why a stranger's name binds nothing.
relations.label: If the last payment is made, the held-back hold is gone and the final period is unbound; a contract whose end must still bind recruits either a name that will be there next year or a deposit posted for the warranty period, and which it recruits depends on whether the party has stayed long enough to have a name.

relations.from: Someone to sue: a promise can be enforced only against a thing the law recognizes as able to bear an obligation, so a market wanting a side that cannot be bound, a town before incorporation, a club, a protocol without a wrapper, a river, the unborn party to a hundred-year carbon contract, is born only when a proxy is deputized to stand for that side, and the proxy's own holds then govern the market; municipal bonds exist only because a city is a person that can be sued, and a club that is no person borrows only on its treasurer's own name, which is Cosigner and stops the day the treasurer will not sign; the trading twin of witness-architectures' Deputized injury, which names who may bring a harm, and the two come apart, since a river with a guardian can sue but nobody lends to a river, because no hold reaches the guardian's purse; escaped by dissolving the person or by immunity; bought in a day for a company, never for a river.
relations.to: Seizable title: a party is bindable through property only if a registry ties the property to its name so that a creditor can find it and take it, as the land registry, the vehicle title, the filed lien; the mortgage exists only because of the registry, and, on de Soto's contested reading, lending against unregistered land fails wherever the deed cannot be searched, so the same house is collateral in one country and dead weight in the next; escaped by moving the asset past the registry's reach or into an exempt class, the homestead, the pension, the tools; adjacent to survival-floors' Tools the bailiff cannot take, which names the exemptions as a floor, this names what the exemptions are carved from; acquired only by owning something registered, which takes a purchase and a registry, not a day.
relations.label: If the party is not a legal person, no judgment can enter against it, so the holds that need a judgment against the party itself, title, door, and the crossing, fall away, and what remains is what needs none: the tap, the deposit, the hostage, possession, held-back pay, the name, the small world, the place in line, and, on its members rather than itself, custody, harm, and the cosigner's name; a protocol with no wrapper can be cut off and disgraced but never seized, which is why every counterparty can bind it and nobody will lend to it.

exploration.first_question: What must be true of a party, in someone else's hands, for a promise to or from it to carry weight, and which market exists only because that hold exists?
exploration.changed_question: Which holds does a stranger walk in with, which can be bought at the door, which are imports of staying done elsewhere, and which accrue only by staying here; and when a hold is escaped, which next hold does the escape recruit? The first breath sorted holds by what is held, an asset, a body, a name; testing the live question against Deposit at the door and Small world showed that the sorting a stranger cares about is time-to-hold, and that holds convert into one another, bail turning custody into cash and the secured card turning cash into a file.

priorities.item: Portable file: a stay done elsewhere binds here only if a registry carries its record out, as the credit bureau's file lets a lender bind a stranger it never met, a licensing board's record lets a nurse be hired in a town where nobody knows her, a passport carries a state's vouching across a border; unsecured lending to strangers exists only because of the file, and the credit-invisible newcomer, with a clean past and no record of it, is bound by deposit until a file accrues, as the secured card takes a deposit and returns it once a year of payments has been written; escaped by forging the file, the synthetic identity, or by moving past the registry's reach; not a small world, where the hold is remembered faces, but its export, which loses the face and gains the road; imported in a day from one's own stay elsewhere.
priorities.why: The passage from a bought hold to an accrued one is where a stranger stops paying tolls and starts being trusted, and it can be checked on paper: an institution either has a rule for converting a deposit into a record and returning the cash, or it does not.
priorities.next_question: Take three holds a stranger buys at the door (a security deposit, a training bond, a secured card's deposit) and find, for each, the institution's written rule for when the record accrued replaces the cash posted and the cash comes back; where no such rule exists, the deposit is a toll rather than a binding, and the operator can predict which newcomers leave.

priorities.item: Someone to sue: a promise can be enforced only against a thing the law recognizes as able to bear an obligation, so a market wanting a side that cannot be bound, a town before incorporation, a club, a protocol without a wrapper, a river, the unborn party to a hundred-year carbon contract, is born only when a proxy is deputized to stand for that side, and the proxy's own holds then govern the market; municipal bonds exist only because a city is a person that can be sued, and a club that is no person borrows only on its treasurer's own name, which is Cosigner and stops the day the treasurer will not sign; the trading twin of witness-architectures' Deputized injury, which names who may bring a harm, and the two come apart, since a river with a guardian can sue but nobody lends to a river, because no hold reaches the guardian's purse; escaped by dissolving the person or by immunity; bought in a day for a company, never for a river.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that any existing wrapper solves it, high generative promise: every long-dated promise has a side that cannot yet be sued, and the map says such a market runs on the proxy's holds, which nobody has listed.
priorities.next_question: Write the proxy for the unborn side of a hundred-year contract (a trustee, a fund, a guardian) and name, from this map, each hold the living side has on that proxy; then check one existing long-dated instrument, a perpetual trust or a sovereign wealth fund's rule, for which of those holds it actually carries, and whether a market with one bindable side behaves like a market at all.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after relabeling the dependency and loop edges, whose partitions misfiled custody, name, and license, repairing Rented door's inverted escape and three false illustrative claims, moving vesting out of Place in line into Held-back pay, and cutting nothing.

neighbors.left: Deposit at the door: a party posts value into the other's hand before anything is owed, forfeited on breach, as the security deposit, the earnest money, the training bond a new pilot signs, the margin at a clearinghouse; rental housing to strangers exists only because of it, and a stranger with nothing to post is not unbindable but unhoused; escaped by breaching for more than the deposit, since the hold is capped at its amount, and undone by the holder's own temptation to keep it wrongly, which is why a large deposit needs a custodian neither party controls; bought in a day at the price of liquidity, so it is the binding of the newly arrived who have cash and a toll on those who do not.
neighbors.right: Held-back pay: the party is owed a stream the other side has not yet paid, and the unpaid remainder is the hold, as retainage keeps a tenth of every construction invoice until the defects are fixed, the sharecropper's share waits for harvest, the commission waits out the return window; hiring a stranger to build exists only because the last tenth can be withheld, and the prepaid builder who vanishes is the market that fails without it; not a deposit, which is the party's own cash posted before work and costs it liquidity, but the counterparty's money not yet paid, binding from the first invoice and costing nothing up front; escaped in the last period, since a party owed nothing further is bound by nothing further, which is why final payments are disputed and warranties are bonded; acquired by beginning the work.
neighbors.separating_case: A contractor with no cash on a job that fails on its first day: retainage holds nothing, since nothing has been invoiced, and a deposit could not have been posted, so the two holds differ in who must have liquidity and in when the hold begins. The same contractor on a job that fails on its last day: the retainage holds the final tenth and the deposit, returned at substantial completion, holds nothing. One is the party's own cash posted before work and capped at its amount; the other is the counterparty's money not yet paid, growing with the work and dying at the last payment.

checks.boundary_case: A man of his word is out: honor binds, but the hold is in nobody's hand but his own, a stranger cannot see it, and no market to strangers has ever been born on it. It enters the map only when the word is spoken before a world small enough to remember it (Small world) or sworn under a penalty that reaches the body (Body that can be brought), and the contract paper itself is out for the same reason, since paper binds only through whichever hold it names.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a loop the sequence conceals: Body that can be brought → Deposit at the door → Portable file → Body that can be brought, where bail converts custody into cash, the secured card converts cash into a file, and know-your-customer, which is the fraud statute reaching through the identity papers to whoever faked them, sends the forged file back to the body through the criminal court, so that no hold on this map escapes the loop except by staying. It shows a passage between levels at Deposit at the door → Portable file, from a bought hold to an accrued one. It shows a fork at Keep the car → Seizable title, where one trade splits by whether the object can be held into a hold needing no court and a hold needing a registry, with a third tine, the ship arrested in the next port, going to the crossing. It shows an incompatibility at Ugly hostage → Deposit at the door, on the axis of value to the holder, where a pledge cannot be both liquid and untempting. And it shows a dependency at Someone to sue → Seizable title, which splits the whole map into holds that need a judgment against the party itself (title, door, the crossing) and holds that need none (tap, deposit, hostage, possession, held-back pay, name, small world, place in line, and custody, harm, and the cosigner's name on the party's members); the judgment-free holds sit at both ends of the walk, since Kneecap opens it and Place in line closes it.
checks.target_preserved: Judged by the Fable critic in a fresh context: each item names a distinct hold, carrier, born and failing market, and escape, and the strange members (a hold acquired by needing, a hold worthless to its holder, a hold that exists only in transit, a leash whose length is its rent, a river that can sue but cannot borrow) survive as mechanisms; the critic tried to break the loop and the fork and could not, and the dependency holds once read as a claim about judgments rather than courts.

name: domain-entry-keys
of: A mechanism by which a stranger gains working orientation in an unfamiliar important domain in one move, named with the key, its carrier (a distinction, a unit, a chair, a document, a question, a word, a failure, a habit), one domain where it opens the door, and the domain where the same key opens the wrong door; sorted by how much of the key survives a crossing between domains, from keys that are the same in every lock to keys the domain re-cuts as soon as they are copied.
items: Prey question: in every domain the stranger's first instinct is the outcome question, is it serious, will I win, how much, is this a good buy, and asking it hands the native the frame, since an outcome question is answered by whatever the native decides to say; the key is the question's shape, held so as not to ask it, and the shape is the same in a clinic, a law office, a car lot, and a garage, which is why it is the one key here that needs no re-cutting; it opens the wrong door where the outcome is the domain's whole product, as with a bookmaker, since there the outcome question is the peer question and the withheld one reads as a bluff.

Magic word: an institution keeps an exception path where its real machinery is reachable, and a stranger enters it with a protocol token rather than a reason, in writing, for the record, I'd like the attending to see this, the form number said aloud at the counter; the form of the token travels between domains (ask for a writing, ask for a record, ask for the senior) while the phrase is local; it opens the wrong door where the token is also the marker of trouble, so the patient who asks for the attending is charted as difficult and the litigant who cites the form number is flagged as the kind who reads forms, and the exception path routes to the domain's defenses rather than its machinery.

Switchboard chair: the person whose job is to know who knows sits in a low chair with the whole map, the ward clerk, the court clerk, the department administrator, the crew's fixer, the sysadmin, and the key is the chair rather than the person, since it is nearly the same chair in every institution and can be found from outside; not low-chair-advantages' account of what the chair confers on its occupant, but the stranger's one use of it, a routing; it opens the wrong door in craft and small domains, where the knower is the master and there is no switchboard, and in domains whose front desk is built to deflect, where the chair is a gate and the map is withheld.

Native gripe: what natives complain about without expecting change is the negative image of the domain's control surface, since people gripe about what they cannot move, nurses about staffing, academics about grant cycles, farmers about weather and the price, pilots about the roster, so an hour in the break room lists the binding constraints; the reading rule travels, the list does not; it opens the wrong door where the gripe is ritual, a bonding complaint whose object nobody would change, as with an orchestra and its conductor, and where the true constraint is a person in the room and therefore never said.

Read sheet: the document everyone in the domain actually reads is the one that binds today's action, the judge's standing order and not the code, the handoff sheet and not the textbook, the on-call rota and not the org chart, the drawing's revision log, the prep list, the docket, the build config, and the key is that the read document is the domain's working interface while the taught document is its legitimation; the slot travels as one question, what binds today's action, while the answer is an accident of each domain's day and may not be a document at all; it opens the wrong door where the read sheet is oral and lives in the foreman's head, or where the domain keeps a public playbook as a decoy and the sheet it reads is the one it would never hand a stranger.

Confluence chore: the menial task that sits where every flow of the domain crosses, prep in a kitchen, retracting in surgery, document review in a lawsuit, on-call in a service, obituaries in a newsroom, teaches the domain's traffic in one shift because everything passes through it; the key is the task's position in the flow, not its lowliness, which is what it adds to low-chair-advantages, and it is held only by the stranger who enters as hands, since a patient or a litigant is never handed the retractor; it opens the wrong door where the chore has been outsourced or automated off the confluence, contract dishwashers, e-discovery, so the stranger who takes it learns the outsourced thing and nothing else.

Native period: every domain has a period inside which things can happen and outside which nothing moves, the court term, the fiscal quarter, the growing season, the academic year, the sprint, the liturgical year, and the stranger who learns it learns when to ask and when asking is noise; not the time a thing takes but the window in which it can be asked for at all, and not a clock read off a state but a calendar natives assume; it opens the wrong door where the visible calendar hides the operative one, the academic year seen and the grant cycle running, or where the domain performs continuity, markets and newsrooms, while running on a hidden period, the close and the deadline.

Stop-holder: every domain has a person or office whose no ends the matter regardless of rank, the pharmacist who will not fill, the building inspector, the completion-bond company on a film, the clerk who will not docket, the anaesthetist who will not put the patient under, and the key is to find the no rather than the yes, since a yes above a no is a wish; the slot travels, the office must be re-found; it opens the wrong door where the formal stop is not the real one, a board whose veto is ceremonial over a founder's mood, and in consensus cultures where the no is distributed and no one holds it, so the stranger who finds the stop-holder finds a chair with nobody in it.

Native unit: the unit natives count in compresses what the domain is short of, beds and patient-days, matters and billable hours, covers, acres and head, containers, seat-miles, person-years, points and picas, so learning the unit tells the stranger what the domain pays for before anyone explains it; not the unit that is priced, which pricing-unit-metamorphoses follows, but the unit said in the corridor; it opens the wrong door where the unit is a badge rather than a measure, kept from a time when it tracked the scarcity, the billable hour where the sale is now the outcome, the film crew's day where the cost is the setup, so the stranger reads a scarcity that is dead, a ghost-leverage worn as a count.

Native tolerance: the same unit at a different precision marks the domain, the bookkeeper to the cent and the CFO to the million, the framer to the eighth, the machinist to the thousandth, the surveyor to a millimetre over a kilometre, and a stranger who reports at the wrong precision is identified in one sentence, while the native tolerance tells what the domain can actually control; not what is counted but how finely, so two natives of one unit can be strangers to each other; it opens the wrong door where the stated tolerance is aspiration, a spec sheet the shop floor does not meet, or where precision is theatre, a forecast to three decimals, so the stranger matches a precision nobody works at.

Fatal class: every domain sorts its errors into a small class that cannot be undone and a large class that can, the missed filing deadline, the wrong-side operation, the jibe in a following sea, the dropped table, and a stranger can act at all only once they hold the short list, because slowness buys something only against the fatal class and native speed elsewhere looks reckless until the list is known; not the domain's famous failure but the shape of its error space; it opens the wrong door where the fatal class is unmarked because the domain is young enough that natives have not met it, or where the list is kept deliberately vague to keep juniors slow everywhere.

Founding wreck: a domain's rules are fossils of its failures, and the failure everyone can name, the bridge that galloped, the wrong-patient transfusion, the fund solvent on paper and dead on cash, is the key to which rules are load-bearing, since a rule with a wreck behind it is broken at one's peril and a rule without one is a habit; not the fatal class, since a wreck can stand behind a rule that guards a recoverable error; it opens the wrong door where the famous wreck is the domain's legend, a business-school case, and the shaping failures are hidden, classified, settled under seal, or filtered by survival, so the stranger reads the failure the domain wants seen.

Hinge distinction: the cut natives make before anything else, acute or chronic, civil or criminal, standing or none, income or capital, static or dynamic load, authentication or authorization, reorganizes the domain's whole pile around one binary, and a stranger who holds it can follow any native conversation because every sentence assumes it; not hinge-kinds' latent variable that decides between two advices, but the cut made before advice exists; it opens the wrong door when the stranger carries the last domain's hinge, the physician asking a lawyer whether the matter is acute and hearing time-barred, and where a domain's first cut is social, who is asking, so the technical hinge opens onto a room where nothing happens.

False friend list: the words a stranger already owns that mean something else inside the domain are a short list that does most of the damage, positive in medicine, conservative in surgery, consideration in contract, sanction in law, theory in science, aggressive in oncology against aggressive in finance, and the key is that the list is short and each carried meaning confidently wrong, at the worst reversed, so a stranger carrying the outside meaning is fluent and wrong in the same sentence; the carried word is the general failure of every key on this map caught at the size of one word; it opens the wrong door where the danger is an orphan rather than a false friend, a native term with no outside referent, a tort, a p-value, which the list cannot catch because there is nothing to carry.

Tourist key: a domain that must face many strangers manufactures a stranger-facing simplification that is stable, teachable, and false, the patient leaflet, the introductory course, the public standards page, the price list, and the stranger who learns it becomes fluent at the wrong level, since natives never say it and the tell that catches them is their fluency in it; observed as far as the unsaid simplification, speculative in the clause that natives make it because they cannot name their own keys; it opens the wrong door wherever it is offered, which is its point, and the right door only where no natives remain, a dead language, a defunct exchange's rulebook, and the tourist key is all that is left.

Peer question: the question that asks for a value inside the domain's decision structure, what is the differential, what is the standard of review, what is the cap rate, is it the alternator or the battery, shows that the asker holds the structure and lacks only the number, and is answered as a peer is answered; it must be re-found in every domain and is heard only if it is right, since a near miss is the prey question in costume; it opens the wrong door in that a peer is not taught, because instruction flows to declared novices, and in a competitive domain the peer answer is a competitor's answer, so the stranger who passes buys speed at the price of the domain's teaching.

Kept tell: the expert's tell that separates the real thing from its imitation is a cost the imitator will not pay or a habit the imitator cannot know to fake, the surgeon watching hands rather than words, the contractor who asks about drainage first, the engineer who reads the error path before the happy path, the sommelier who spits, and the key is to learn the tell before the vocabulary, since vocabulary is what the imitation has; it is the one key the domain re-cuts when copied; it opens the wrong door where the tell has leaked and been priced, the confidence man's textbook, the trained interviewee, the counterfeit with the right stitching, so the imitation carries the tell, natives move to a new one, and the stranger holds last year's key.

source.register: Concrete and institutional: ward clerks, standing orders, billable hours, wristbands, prep lists, patient leaflets, false-friend words, the galloping bridge; drawn from medicine, law, kitchens, construction, aviation, sailing, film sets, farming, software, and publishing.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism; one item (Tourist key) carries a marked speculative clause about why natives manufacture the decoy, and Native gripe's reading rule is analytical rather than observed.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not an empirical taxonomy or a partition; a real entry into a domain uses several keys at once, and the list makes no claim to cover every kind.
The seriation is an itinerary of how much of a key survives a crossing between domains, not a ranking of value, difficulty, or order of use; map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (ward clerks, standing orders, the galloping bridge, e-discovery, patient leaflets, the billable hour) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about particular institutions or histories.

Tourist key's clause that natives manufacture the decoy because they cannot name their own keys is speculative and marked as such; the item stands on the observed part, a stable, teachable, unsaid simplification.
Study methods, mentors, credentials, and the domain's own gates are outside: a key here is what a stranger can hold in one move, not a course of study or a status the domain confers.

seriation.axis: How much of the key survives the crossing between domains: from the key that is the same in every lock (the outcome question one must not ask), through keys whose slot travels and which can be used before the local value is known (ask for the senior, find the chair, sit in the break room, ask what binds today's action), to keys whose slot travels but which buy nothing until the local value has been re-cut (the chore, the period, the stop, the unit, the tolerance, the fatal list, the wreck, the hinge), to the word whose carried value is the wrong door itself (the false friend), to keys the domain cuts for you falsely (the tourist key), keys that must be found against the domain and are heard only if right (the peer question), and finally the key the domain re-cuts as soon as it is copied (the kept tell).
seriation.note: An authored walk, not a scale of value or a sequence of use. Prey question opens because it is the one key identical in every lock: the outcome question is the same everywhere and the key is not to ask it. Kept tell closes because it is the one key the lock re-cuts as soon as it has been copied. The middle was re-cut at the critic's showing: the authored tiers 'form travels, phrase or person local' and 'slot travels, value re-cut' were one tier under two names, since a form is a slot and a phrase is a value, and Read sheet's 'no slot' tier rested on a false clause. What separates the middle is whether the key is usable before the local value is known (Magic word, Switchboard chair, Native gripe, Read sheet, which is why Read sheet now sits beside Native gripe: the reading rule travels, the answer does not) or only after it (Confluence chore, which moved into this group because a chore is taken only once one knows which task is the confluence, then Native period, Stop-holder, Native unit, Native tolerance, Fatal class, Founding wreck, Hinge distinction). Hinge distinction → False friend list remains the hinge of the route: the hinge is the value that must be re-cut, and the false friend is what a carried value does, the same word with its load shifted or reversed, so the adjacency teaches that the failure clause of every item on this map is one mechanism, a value carried across a slot; this is what the live question about which keys transfer turned into, since what transfers is the slot and the transfer of a value is the wrong door. Then the three keys that involve the domain's own hand: Tourist key, which it cuts for you falsely, Peer question, which must be found against it, and Kept tell, which it withholds.

relations.from: Switchboard chair: the person whose job is to know who knows sits in a low chair with the whole map, the ward clerk, the court clerk, the department administrator, the crew's fixer, the sysadmin, and the key is the chair rather than the person, since it is nearly the same chair in every institution and can be found from outside; not low-chair-advantages' account of what the chair confers on its occupant, but the stranger's one use of it, a routing; it opens the wrong door in craft and small domains, where the knower is the master and there is no switchboard, and in domains whose front desk is built to deflect, where the chair is a gate and the map is withheld.
relations.to: Hinge distinction: the cut natives make before anything else, acute or chronic, civil or criminal, standing or none, income or capital, static or dynamic load, authentication or authorization, reorganizes the domain's whole pile around one binary, and a stranger who holds it can follow any native conversation because every sentence assumes it; not hinge-kinds' latent variable that decides between two advices, but the cut made before advice exists; it opens the wrong door when the stranger carries the last domain's hinge, the physician asking a lawyer whether the matter is acute and hearing time-barred, and where a domain's first cut is social, who is asking, so the technical hinge opens onto a room where nothing happens.
relations.label: If the stranger reaches the chair that routes, then the question the chair asks in order to route (how long has this been going on; is this civil or criminal) is the hinge distinction said aloud, so the routing hands over the hinge as a side effect; a passage from a person to a distinction.

relations.from: Prey question: in every domain the stranger's first instinct is the outcome question, is it serious, will I win, how much, is this a good buy, and asking it hands the native the frame, since an outcome question is answered by whatever the native decides to say; the key is the question's shape, held so as not to ask it, and the shape is the same in a clinic, a law office, a car lot, and a garage, which is why it is the one key here that needs no re-cutting; it opens the wrong door where the outcome is the domain's whole product, as with a bookmaker, since there the outcome question is the peer question and the withheld one reads as a bluff.

relations.label: If the stranger asks the outcome question, then the domain answers with the tourist key, since the outcome question is the tourist key's request form; and the tourist key yields better-sounding outcome questions, so the loop closes one level below the natives.
