relations.from: Reset with the trigger in the other hand: the Series A puts a founder's already-vested shares back on a schedule with a repurchase right at cost, so a founder three years in and three-quarters vested is a quarter vested again; agreed under the sentence 'we need you committed' and understood by both sides as a commitment device, but the board that can end her employment is, after the round, a board the investor sits on, and forfeited shares are retired, which lifts every remaining holder pro rata including the one who voted; a founder with thirty percent removed twelve months after the reset keeps under half of her shares, and the seventeen percent of the company that returns is spread over whoever remains; not vesting, which any hire accepts, but a forfeiture whose trigger sits with a board on which its beneficiaries vote.
relations.to: Ninety-day guillotine: vested options must be exercised within ninety days of leaving, paying the strike and the tax on the spread, or they lapse back to the pool, so the carrier of an employee's ownership back to the company is a purchase price on the exit door, due on the day she can least afford it; agreed in the plan document every hire signs unread, written by counsel under a tax rule; fifty thousand vested options at a two-dollar strike against a twenty-dollar appraisal is a hundred thousand in cash and a nine-hundred-thousand spread the tax bill can treat as income, so a departing engineer with a mortgage forfeits ownership she spent four years earning; not a vesting term, since the shares had vested, but a toll on keeping them, and what lapses returns to a pool the same board regrants, so the beneficiary is whoever is hired next and the founder whose next refill is smaller.
relations.label: If the reset puts a founder's shares on a clock held by a board the investor can move, then her removal retires the unvested shares and starts the ninety days on her vested options, so both carriers fire from one decision: the retired shares lift every remaining holder pro rata, the hand that made the decision among them, and the lapsed options refill a pool the same board grants.

relations.from: Stack that eats the common: each round's preferred takes its money back before common sees anything, so the founder's percentage is a share of the exit only above the price at which conversion beats preference, and below it a good price pays the common almost nothing; agreed round by round as 'one times non-participating, standard', understood by every investor as the whole point and read by the founder as a percentage; fifty million raised at one times, exit at sixty, the preferred take fifty and a founder with twenty percent takes two million from a sale the press reports at sixty million; not the round price, which set her percentage truly, but a floor under each round that becomes the entire payout when the exit lands near the raise, and the tell is the conversion price, above which the cap table becomes honest again.
relations.to: Carve-out at the door: when the exit price sits inside or barely above the stack, the preferred agree a management carve-out, a share of proceeds paid to named, still-employed executives before the waterfall, so the same founder is paid as a manager and nothing as a shareholder, and every common holder who left gets nothing; agreed at the exit, by the board, understood by the board and by no one who has already gone; a hundred-and-fifteen-million sale against a hundred and ten of preference would pay the common five million, and a ten-percent carve-out taken off the top pays eleven and a half million to the four managers named and zero to two hundred option holders and the departed co-founder, so the carve-out drains the common only in the band from the top of the stack up to that top divided by one minus the carve-out fraction, a hundred and twenty-two here, while inside the stack the same carve-out is paid from the preferred's own money and drains the common nothing; not the stack, which is the cause, but the exception bought from it, and it forks the founder from the people who built the thing with her.
relations.label: If the exit price falls inside the stack, then the preferred must choose between a management that will not close the sale and a carve-out that pays it, and the carve-out forks the common into those still employed, who are paid, and those who left, who are not.

relations.from: Ten votes a share: the founder's class carries ten votes, so control is conserved while economics drain, and the leak is in the sunset and the transfer clauses, since the class converts to common on sale, on death, on leaving, or on a date; agreed at incorporation or at the offering, understood by the founder as permanent and by counsel as a schedule; eleven percent of the economics with fifty-five percent of the vote, until a divorce transfers a two-point block that converts on transfer and the vote falls under half; not control as such but control on a clock the founder does not see as a clock, and the tell is that the class's conversion events are listed on a page she never turned to.
relations.to: Veto without votes: protective provisions give the preferred a class vote over a sale, a new round, debt, the budget, and the pool, so a twenty-percent holder can block anything while the cap table shows nothing, since the control lives in the charter and not in the count; agreed as 'standard protective provisions', understood by the investor as the deal and by the founder as boilerplate; the reverse of ten votes a share, economics intact and control gone, and a board seat granted to a two-percent seed holder is the same carrier held by a body instead of a class; not a majority but a list of things a majority may not do, and no arithmetic ever shows it.
relations.label: If the founder keeps the vote by class and the investors keep the veto by charter, then each drains the other's use, a majority that may not act and a veto that cannot initiate, and control sits with whichever party can wait longer.

exploration.first_question: By which routes other than the round price does ownership or control drain from a party, and which of those routes can be computed on the cap table at signing versus only at the exit?
exploration.changed_question: Whose hand holds the trigger, and does the same hand catch what falls? The first breath assumed every carrier moves ownership from the founder to the party across the table and is agreed before it bites. Sharpening the vesting reset against the liquidation stack showed a carrier whose forfeited shares go to nobody in particular, since retired shares lift every remaining holder pro rata, while the trigger sits with the board the beneficiary controls. That opened a class the first framing could not see: carriers that return ownership to the company (the reset, the ninety-day window), carriers agreed at the moment they bite rather than before it (the carve-out), and carriers that move a claim without moving a share (the secondary's reclassification).
exploration.new_member: Carve-out at the door: when the exit price sits inside or barely above the stack, the preferred agree a management carve-out, a share of proceeds paid to named, still-employed executives before the waterfall, so the same founder is paid as a manager and nothing as a shareholder, and every common holder who left gets nothing; agreed at the exit, by the board, understood by the board and by no one who has already gone; a hundred-and-fifteen-million sale against a hundred and ten of preference would pay the common five million, and a ten-percent carve-out taken off the top pays eleven and a half million to the four managers named and zero to two hundred option holders and the departed co-founder, so the carve-out drains the common only in the band from the top of the stack up to that top divided by one minus the carve-out fraction, a hundred and twenty-two here, while inside the stack the same carve-out is paid from the preferred's own money and drains the common nothing; not the stack, which is the cause, but the exception bought from it, and it forks the founder from the people who built the thing with her.

priorities.item: Additive slices: under the post-money SAFE each check buys a percentage fixed as of the moment before the priced round and immune to every later SAFE, so the slices add and the founders alone pay for each one; agreed one check at a time with investors who never see the others, understood by the form's author, who published the arithmetic, and not by the founder who reads 'post-money' as a valuation word; five hundred thousand at a five million cap, a million at ten, a million and a half at fifteen is ten, ten, and ten percent, thirty percent gone before the Series A prices a share; not stacking as such, which pre-money notes also do while diluting one another, but immunity, which makes each slice a fixed charge on the common.
priorities.why: It is the carrier with the simplest arithmetic and the largest typical gap between what was agreed and what was summed, and it can be tested with a single question asked before a spreadsheet is opened.
priorities.next_question: Take ten pre-Series-A cap tables built on post-money SAFEs, real or synthetic, and before showing the table ask the founder for the total percentage sold; count how many land within five points, and separately whether founders who raised in one batch do better than founders who raised one check at a time across a year.

priorities.item: Reset with the trigger in the other hand: the Series A puts a founder's already-vested shares back on a schedule with a repurchase right at cost, so a founder three years in and three-quarters vested is a quarter vested again; agreed under the sentence 'we need you committed' and understood by both sides as a commitment device, but the board that can end her employment is, after the round, a board the investor sits on, and forfeited shares are retired, which lifts every remaining holder pro rata including the one who voted; a founder with thirty percent removed twelve months after the reset keeps under half of her shares, and the seventeen percent of the company that returns is spread over whoever remains; not vesting, which any hire accepts, but a forfeiture whose trigger sits with a board on which its beneficiaries vote.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that anyone would ever price it, high generative promise: the reset is an option held by the party who controls the trigger, and if it can be written as an option it can be priced, refused, or bought back, which no term sheet today does.
priorities.next_question: Build a toy company with an investor who holds the board majority and a founder whose shares are reset to a quarter vested; vary the founder's vested fraction at reset from zero to full and her replacement cost from cheap to irreplaceable, and find the region where removing her is worth more to the investor's stake than her continued work; then ask whether a reset with the trigger given to an independent director changes the region at all.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after repairing eight items and two edge labels, chiefly one wrong vote-share number, a pro rata claim that belonged to the reset and not the guillotine, and a false mechanism for the warrant's invisibility; the Cap as option and Ratchet after the fact pair survived a collapse attempt.

neighbors.left: Stack that eats the common: each round's preferred takes its money back before common sees anything, so the founder's percentage is a share of the exit only above the price at which conversion beats preference, and below it a good price pays the common almost nothing; agreed round by round as 'one times non-participating, standard', understood by every investor as the whole point and read by the founder as a percentage; fifty million raised at one times, exit at sixty, the preferred take fifty and a founder with twenty percent takes two million from a sale the press reports at sixty million; not the round price, which set her percentage truly, but a floor under each round that becomes the entire payout when the exit lands near the raise, and the tell is the conversion price, above which the cap table becomes honest again.
neighbors.right: Dip twice: participating preferred takes its preference and then its pro-rata share of what is left, so there is no exit price at which the cap table's percentage becomes the holder's share of proceeds until the participation cap is reached; agreed as one word after 'preferred', understood by the investor as the term that makes the cap table lie at every price; ten million for a quarter, exit at forty, takes ten plus a quarter of thirty, seventeen and a half, forty-four percent of the exit for twenty-five percent of the company; not the stack, which vanishes at the conversion point, but a stack with no such point below the cap, so the arithmetic must be run at every exit price rather than once.
neighbors.separating_case: Fifty million raised, a founder holding twenty percent, and an exit at five hundred million. Under a one-times non-participating stack every series converts, the stack vanishes, and the founder's twenty percent is a hundred million, so above the conversion point the cap table told the truth. Under participating preferred with no cap the same investors take their fifty and a share of the four hundred and fifty besides, so the founder's twenty percent is a share of proceeds at no exit price at all. The existence of a price at which the cap table becomes honest separates them, and it is the number an operator should ask for.

checks.boundary_case: A low round price is out: the founder who sold forty percent at the seed because she had two months of cash was drained by the headline price, which everyone at the table computed on the day. A recapitalization is out for the same reason, since the pre-money set near zero against forty million of old preference is a price, and the drain runs through it and not around it. Cap as option is in on exactly that contrast, because the cap is read as the price and is not one.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a loop the itinerary conceals: Pool before the price → Below the threshold → Pool before the price, where grants drawn from a pool the pre-money holders paid for are refilled inside the next pre-money (the forward leg is drawn as an edge; the return leg is the claim of that edge's label, since the map is at its edge ceiling), and Ratchet after the fact → Pool before the price enters the same loop from the next-price stage, since a down round refills the pool as well. It shows a passage between levels at Interest that converts → Dividend nobody pays, where the same clock that accrued shares at the note level accrues preference at the exit level. It shows a fork at Stack that eats the common → Carve-out at the door, where one exit price splits the common into the paid and the unpaid along the line of who is still employed, which the cap table cannot express. It shows a same-hand coupling at Reset with the trigger in the other hand → Ninety-day guillotine, two carriers that the sequence places as neighbors and the edge shows firing from a single decision, with two destinations for what falls: the retired shares lift every remaining holder pro rata, the decision's maker among them, and the lapsed options refill a pool the same board grants. And it shows an incompatibility at Ten votes a share → Veto without votes, where the two control carriers, placed together at the end of the itinerary, cancel into a stalemate rather than adding.
checks.target_preserved: Judged by the Fable critic in a fresh context: the item type, the itinerary, and the edges' shapes hold, and the strange members (a reset whose trigger sits with a board on which its beneficiaries vote, a secondary that creates a claim without issuing a share, a carve-out agreed at the moment it bites) survive as mechanisms; eight items and two edge labels were repaired for arithmetic and mechanism (the dual-class vote share, lapsed options returning to the pool rather than pro rata, the warrant's invisibility, the carve-out's illustrative price, the six-fold win, the secondary's board consent), and the Cap as option and Ratchet after the fact pair survived a collapse attempt.

name: power-trades
of: A mechanism by which a power, a capacity to make another party do, refrain, or accept something in a named future state, passes between parties in exchange for something else, named with the power given, what is received, the carrier that makes the trade hold (a paper, a body, a registry, a repeated game), the shape of the exchange rate, and the moment the trade unwinds or is found to have been one-sided; sorted by what becomes of the given power, from powers lent that return by their own clock to powers consumed in the giving and powers the trade creates in a hand that was never a party to it.
items: Card for one meeting: holders lend their votes to an activist by proxy card, giving the exercise of the vote and receiving a campaign they did not have to run; the carrier is the card, good for one meeting and revoked by any later-dated card up to the hour of the vote, so the power returns by its own clock with nothing worn off; the rate is zero at the margin, since each lender gives a vote worth nothing alone and the borrower assembles a majority from votes nobody priced; found one-sided when the activist settles with the board for two seats before the vote and the lenders learn their votes were the borrower's bargaining chip and never their ballot; not a sale, since the vote never leaves the share.

Seat for the check: an investor gives capital and receives one director's vote of five and the information that comes with the room; the carrier is the investors' rights agreement, which conditions the seat on holding a threshold of shares and sunsets it at a listing, so the seat lapses back by the paper; the rate is lumpy, since the last dollar across the threshold buys the whole seat and every dollar after it buys nothing, which is why the lead fights over the threshold and not the price; not control, and the investor who thought it bought control discovers this at the first vote that goes four to one, while the founder discovers what a seat is at the first vote that goes three to two.

Fence around the process: a founder gives the power to run an auction for thirty days and receives a term sheet whose only binding clause is the fence; the carrier is the no-shop together with the other bidders' calendars, and the clause returns the power on its date, but the power was never in the clause, it lived in the bidders' heat, and bidders told to wait find other deals, so an auction paused does not resume at the temperature it was paused at; the rate is written as thirty days and paid as the auction, and the party inside the fence can lower its price in the last week knowing this; not a breakup fee, which prices the walk, since the fence prices nothing and consumes the alternative.

Leased strike: a union gives the strike for the term of the contract and receives binding arbitration of grievances, a procedure that makes the employer obey a third party's answer; the carrier is the agreement and the arbitrator; the rate is flat across the term though the strike's value peaks in the employer's busy season, and arbitration pays out at the pace of the docket; the power returns at expiry in law, but a strike not run in twenty years returns as a threat the employer no longer believes and the members no longer know how to run, so what is leased comes back lighter each term; not ghost leverage, an obsolete power still obeyed, but a live one atrophied by disuse, since an employer that tests it may find it still works.

Customs house: a state gives foreign creditors the power to collect its customs and receives a loan, as the Ottoman Public Debt Administration from 1881 and the Dominican receivership of 1905 put creditors' clerks at the revenue's source; the carrier is the receivership itself, an occupation of the place where the money enters; the rate is set by the lender's model of default and not by what the state thinks its sovereignty is worth, so the power is priced as a yield; the loan has a maturity and the receivership has none, so the power returns only by an act the carrier never wrote, a war, a repudiation, or a new treaty bought with a new pledge, as Lausanne in 1923 and the Trujillo-Hull treaty of 1940 did, which the debtor must some decade find the strength or the credit to perform; not conditionality, which binds by the next tranche and can be dropped by dropping the tranche.

Veto sold as an improbability: a founder gives an investor class consent rights over named future states, a sale below a price, a new financing, a change to the charter, and receives a higher valuation now; the carrier is the charter's protective provisions, held by class vote; the rate is set by the founder's estimate of how unlikely those states are, so the veto is sold at the price of an improbability and exercised at the price of a certainty, and the buyer, who has seen a hundred companies reach those states, knows the base rate better than the seller who has seen one; found one-sided the day the improbable arrives and the acqui-hire that would save the team needs a signature from a class that would receive nothing; not control, since a veto can keep a future from happening and cannot make one happen.

Drag for tag: a minority gives the majority the power to force its shares into a sale and receives the right to join any sale the majority makes; the carrier is the shareholders' agreement; the rate is symmetric in the text and asymmetric in frequency, since drags fire at nearly every exit and tags almost never, because majorities rarely sell in part, so a swap of two powers over two futures is priced as if the futures were equally likely and pays out as if only one existed; found one-sided when the drag fires at a price the majority's preference makes handsome and the minority's common makes nothing. Adds to impasse-inventions' swap of vetoes the shape of the rate: a power-for-power swap is priced by which future arrives, not by the powers' text.

First look that chills the room: a founder gives an investor the right to match or lead the next round and receives a better price now; the carrier is the clause; the rate is written as an option and paid as a chill, since outsiders will not spend a month of diligence on a round they can be matched out of, so what was given was not a first look but the outsiders' willingness to bid; found one-sided when the next process is run and the serious bidders decline to come, and returned only by a waiver the holder can sell a second time; not the fence, which consumes a process already running, since the first look keeps the next one from starting. Adds to impasse-inventions' right of first refusal the mechanism by which the right is worth more than its text.

Silence on the tab: a reporter or an analyst gives a source a veto over each story in exchange for access, and the veto outlives the story, since access is revocable at any moment and every story withheld is an investment in the relationship that the next disclosure would forfeit; the carrier is the repeated game and the reporter's own sunk stories, not any one item, so the source holds a standing power to make the reporter refrain that grows without ever being re-granted; the rate ratchets, because the price of the next disclosure rises with every one not made while the rent the source pays stays flat; found one-sided when the access yields only what cannot be printed and the power to publish has quietly become a power to know; not a bribe, an outcome bought once and priced fresh each time, since here the hold accumulates in what the reporter has already withheld, and not discretion sold as a good, a single sale, but a lease whose breaking fee rises with the tenancy.

Hostage returned as partisan: a party gives another a power to punish it through a body it values, and receives a hold or a confirmation back, as in the medieval exchange of sons between truce-makers, which ran both ways, and the hostages Rome took from client kings, which ran one way and paid in the king's throne; the carrier is the body together with the giver's continuing love for it, since a hostage the giver stops valuing holds nothing, so the rate is set by the givers' caring and not by the ranks of the persons given; the trade inverts, on the standard reading of Roman practice, when the hostage raised in the holder's house returns as its friend, so the giver gave a hold and got back a party of the other side; not the ugly hostage of who-can-be-bound, a token worth nothing to its holder, since here the holder comes to value the body too, and that is what lets it be turned.

Name on the door: a partner gives share and receives the name on the letterhead, and a founder gives the chief executive's chair and receives the chairman's; the power given is a share of decisions and profits, the thing received is a sign, and the carrier is the sign plus whoever routes through it; the rate is settled afterward by third parties, since a sign that captures a flow, the client who will deal only with the named partner, the press that calls the founder, regenerates the substance it was traded for, while a sign that captures no flow decays into a room where the meetings are held elsewhere; found one-sided on the day one learns which kind one holds; not a status conversion, which turns one standing into another in the same holder, since here the substance passes to a counterparty and outsiders set what the sign is worth.

Blame-bearer's fee: a principal gives the visible power, the signature on the filing, the name in the registry, the responsible person on the license, and receives invisibility, while a nominee gives its name and receives a fee; the carrier is the registry that names the nominee, so the summons goes where the registry points; the rate prices the ordinary year, and the liability that arrives in the rare one was never priced, since the fee is set as if the nominee's name were only a name; found one-sided when the liability arrives and the nominee learns that the decision was never theirs and the answer for it is; not the name on the door, whose sign draws clients, since this sign draws process servers.

Vote that dies in transit: the public gives its vote and receives the position, a share at a measured small discount, while the founder keeps ten votes a share; the carrier is the charter, which converts high-vote shares to one vote when they leave the founder's hands, so the founder's control is a power that cannot be sold onward, only held, and passes by sunset clause or by death; the rate is the dual-class discount, a few percent off for the vote given up; found one-sided when the founder's judgment goes and nothing but the calendar can retrieve the vote; not the proxy card, which lends a vote that survives the lending, since this is a vote the carrier kills to keep it from being lent at all.

Sword for quarter: the party that surrenders gives its residual power to fight and receives quarter; the carrier is the ceremony and the law that makes a prisoner a status rather than a corpse; the rate is set by what the residual resistance would cost the victor, so the garrison that can still make the siege expensive gets terms and the one that cannot gets none, which is why terms must be asked while the walls still stand; consumed in the giving, since the disarmed cannot rearm and the victor's side of the trade is enforced only by the victor's own need for the next surrender; the wolf that shows the throat gives the same thing at a rate set by the winner's need for a pack; not deference, which is given again each morning and can be withheld tomorrow.

Queen for a day: a witness gives what it knows and receives use immunity under a proffer letter, which bars the prosecutor from using the words themselves; the carrier is the letter; the witness's power was the exclusivity of the fact, and it is consumed by the telling, since a fact once on the record is a record and not a lever, so the trade must be struck before the fact is spoken and the price can only fall after; found one-sided when derivative use arrives, the leads the words opened being chargeable though the words are not; not the sword, whose carrier passes to the victor, since here the carrier is copied and what dies is being the only one who holds it.

Kingmaker's tax: a small party gives its votes in the chamber and receives ministries, at a rate set by pivotality and not by size, so five seats that complete a majority buy more than forty that do not; the carrier is the coalition agreement and the confidence vote; the trade consumes not the power given but its source, since on a common reading the junior partner's voters, who elected it to be an alternative, punish it for having been a government, so the votes return at the next election and the electorate does not; not the veto, which keeps a future from happening, since the kingmaker makes one happen and is billed for it.

Key man's lever: investors in a fund give their commitment and receive the power to suspend the fund's investing if named partners leave; the carrier is the limited partnership agreement; the rate looks cheap to the firm, which does not plan to lose the named, but the trade mints a power in a hand that was never a party to it and was often the firm's own voice at the table, since each named partner now holds a lever over its own firm, leaving triggers the suspension, and can price its staying at every renegotiation; the firm's power over its own partners is what was quietly sold; found one-sided when a named partner asks for more carry with the agreement open on the table; not a hostage, who is held, since the key man holds.

source.register: Operator-grade and concrete: proxy cards, seat thresholds, no-shops, no-strike clauses, customs receiverships, protective provisions, drag and tag, first looks, embargoes, exchanged sons, letterheads, nominee registries, dual-class charters, surrender ceremonies, proffer letters, coalition agreements, key-man clauses; drawn from venture terms, fund agreements, labor contracts, sovereign debt, prosecution practice, the law of war, and parliamentary coalitions.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism; two items rest on contested readings and say so (Hostage returned as partisan on Roman practice, Kingmaker's tax on junior coalition partners); no item is invented-world, and the wolf in Sword for quarter is an illustration, not a claim about wolves.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a taxonomy or a partition; a real term sheet or treaty runs several of these trades at once, and the list makes no claim to cover every kind.
The seriation is an itinerary of what becomes of the given power, not a ranking of danger, value, or historical order; the map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (the Ottoman and Dominican receiverships, Roman hostages, proffer practice, dual-class charters, junior coalition partners) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about the specific histories; Hostage returned as partisan and Kingmaker's tax rest on contested readings and say so in the item.
Trades of money for goods, and of money for a single exercise of a power (the bribe, the fee for a decision), are outside: no power moves, only an outcome.

Powers a party trades with itself or with the world (the burned bridge, the Ulysses contract, the precommitment) are outside, since nothing is received from a counterparty; they belong to the leverage maps.

seriation.axis: What becomes of the given power: from powers lent, which return by their own carrier's clock with nothing worn off, through powers whose paper returns while the power does not, powers that return lighter, powers that return only by an act the carrier never wrote, powers that fire or lapse with which future arrives, powers that accumulate in the taker's hand with every exercise withheld, powers that return transformed by a party outside the trade, for the other side, as a sign, or as a summons, powers that cannot be passed on, and powers consumed in the giving, to powers the trade creates in a hand that was never a party to it.
seriation.note: An authored walk, not a scale of danger or of value. Card for one meeting opens it because nothing about the vote changes in the lending; Key man's lever closes it because the power did not exist before the trade. Seat for the check → Fence around the process is the consequential adjacency: both return by the paper on a date, but the seat's paper is the power (the vote is the seat) while the fence's paper points at a power that lives in the bidders, so the return clause returns the paper and not the power. That is the map's one operator test: before selling a power for a term, ask whether the carrier is the power or a pointer to it. Sword for quarter → Queen for a day → Kingmaker's tax is the hinge, three routes by which a power is consumed rather than returned: the carrier passes to the other side, the carrier is copied and exclusivity dies, the source behind the power is spent while the power itself comes back. Key man's lever follows because consumption and creation are the same failure of conservation seen from the two ends: a power trade need not be zero-sum in power. Hostage returned as partisan, Name on the door, and Blame-bearer's fee sit together as powers that return transformed, with the transformation decided by a party outside the trade: the raised hostage, the client, the process server.

relations.from: Fence around the process: a founder gives the power to run an auction for thirty days and receives a term sheet whose only binding clause is the fence; the carrier is the no-shop together with the other bidders' calendars, and the clause returns the power on its date, but the power was never in the clause, it lived in the bidders' heat, and bidders told to wait find other deals, so an auction paused does not resume at the temperature it was paused at; the rate is written as thirty days and paid as the auction, and the party inside the fence can lower its price in the last week knowing this; not a breakup fee, which prices the walk, since the fence prices nothing and consumes the alternative.
relations.to: First look that chills the room: a founder gives an investor the right to match or lead the next round and receives a better price now; the carrier is the clause; the rate is written as an option and paid as a chill, since outsiders will not spend a month of diligence on a round they can be matched out of, so what was given was not a first look but the outsiders' willingness to bid; found one-sided when the next process is run and the serious bidders decline to come, and returned only by a waiver the holder can sell a second time; not the fence, which consumes a process already running, since the first look keeps the next one from starting. Adds to impasse-inventions' right of first refusal the mechanism by which the right is worth more than its text.
relations.label: If the fence lapses without a close, the process it returns is cold, and a founder with no live bidders has no price at which to refuse a first look on the next round; the cold auction recruits the first look.

relations.from: First look that chills the room: a founder gives an investor the right to match or lead the next round and receives a better price now; the carrier is the clause; the rate is written as an option and paid as a chill, since outsiders will not spend a month of diligence on a round they can be matched out of, so what was given was not a first look but the outsiders' willingness to bid; found one-sided when the next process is run and the serious bidders decline to come, and returned only by a waiver the holder can sell a second time; not the fence, which consumes a process already running, since the first look keeps the next one from starting. Adds to impasse-inventions' right of first refusal the mechanism by which the right is worth more than its text.
relations.to: Fence around the process: a founder gives the power to run an auction for thirty days and receives a term sheet whose only binding clause is the fence; the carrier is the no-shop together with the other bidders' calendars, and the clause returns the power on its date, but the power was never in the clause, it lived in the bidders' heat, and bidders told to wait find other deals, so an auction paused does not resume at the temperature it was paused at; the rate is written as thirty days and paid as the auction, and the party inside the fence can lower its price in the last week knowing this; not a breakup fee, which prices the walk, since the fence prices nothing and consumes the alternative.
relations.label: If the first look is held by an insider when the next round opens, there is no outside bidder for a fence to keep out, so the next fence is granted for nothing; with the previous edge this closes a loop in which each round's exclusivity lowers the price of the next round's exclusivity.

relations.from: Veto sold as an improbability: a founder gives an investor class consent rights over named future states, a sale below a price, a new financing, a change to the charter, and receives a higher valuation now; the carrier is the charter's protective provisions, held by class vote; the rate is set by the founder's estimate of how unlikely those states are, so the veto is sold at the price of an improbability and exercised at the price of a certainty, and the buyer, who has seen a hundred companies reach those states, knows the base rate better than the seller who has seen one; found one-sided the day the improbable arrives and the acqui-hire that would save the team needs a signature from a class that would receive nothing; not control, since a veto can keep a future from happening and cannot make one happen.
relations.to: Drag for tag: a minority gives the majority the power to force its shares into a sale and receives the right to join any sale the majority makes; the carrier is the shareholders' agreement; the rate is symmetric in the text and asymmetric in frequency, since drags fire at nearly every exit and tags almost never, because majorities rarely sell in part, so a swap of two powers over two futures is priced as if the futures were equally likely and pays out as if only one existed; found one-sided when the drag fires at a price the majority's preference makes handsome and the minority's common makes nothing. Adds to impasse-inventions' swap of vetoes the shape of the rate: a power-for-power swap is priced by which future arrives, not by the powers' text.
relations.label: If the drag and the veto sit in different hands, as when a senior series triggers the drag on a sale at its own preference and a junior series holding its own protective provisions would receive nothing, the drag cannot fire without a signature that has no reason to come, so two powers each sold as an improbability collide in the same improbable state and only one can hold; standard paper hides the collision by lodging both powers in one preferred majority, and a stacked syndicate brings it back.

relations.from: Leased strike: a union gives the strike for the term of the contract and receives binding arbitration of grievances, a procedure that makes the employer obey a third party's answer; the carrier is the agreement and the arbitrator; the rate is flat across the term though the strike's value peaks in the employer's busy season, and arbitration pays out at the pace of the docket; the power returns at expiry in law, but a strike not run in twenty years returns as a threat the employer no longer believes and the members no longer know how to run, so what is leased comes back lighter each term; not ghost leverage, an obsolete power still obeyed, but a live one atrophied by disuse, since an employer that tests it may find it still works.
relations.to: Sword for quarter: the party that surrenders gives its residual power to fight and receives quarter; the carrier is the ceremony and the law that makes a prisoner a status rather than a corpse; the rate is set by what the residual resistance would cost the victor, so the garrison that can still make the siege expensive gets terms and the one that cannot gets none, which is why terms must be asked while the walls still stand; consumed in the giving, since the disarmed cannot rearm and the victor's side of the trade is enforced only by the victor's own need for the next surrender; the wolf that shows the throat gives the same thing at a rate set by the winner's need for a pack; not deference, which is given again each morning and can be withheld tomorrow.
relations.label: If the leased power goes unexercised for long enough, its return at expiry is indistinguishable from surrender, since a strike no one can run is a sword already handed over; the passage from returned lighter to consumed is crossed without a ceremony, and the operator cannot tell which side of it the union is on until someone calls.

relations.from: Name on the door: a partner gives share and receives the name on the letterhead, and a founder gives the chief executive's chair and receives the chairman's; the power given is a share of decisions and profits, the thing received is a sign, and the carrier is the sign plus whoever routes through it; the rate is settled afterward by third parties, since a sign that captures a flow, the client who will deal only with the named partner, the press that calls the founder, regenerates the substance it was traded for, while a sign that captures no flow decays into a room where the meetings are held elsewhere; found one-sided on the day one learns which kind one holds; not a status conversion, which turns one standing into another in the same holder, since here the substance passes to a counterparty and outsiders set what the sign is worth.
relations.to: Blame-bearer's fee: a principal gives the visible power, the signature on the filing, the name in the registry, the responsible person on the license, and receives invisibility, while a nominee gives its name and receives a fee; the carrier is the registry that names the nominee, so the summons goes where the registry points; the rate prices the ordinary year, and the liability that arrives in the rare one was never priced, since the fee is set as if the nominee's name were only a name; found one-sided when the liability arrives and the nominee learns that the decision was never theirs and the answer for it is; not the name on the door, whose sign draws clients, since this sign draws process servers.
relations.label: If the sign captures a flow of clients or press it regenerates the share that was traded for it; if it captures the summons instead, it is the nominee's; the same signature on the same letterhead forks by which third parties route through it, and the holder learns which branch it is on only when someone arrives.

relations.from: Card for one meeting: holders lend their votes to an activist by proxy card, giving the exercise of the vote and receiving a campaign they did not have to run; the carrier is the card, good for one meeting and revoked by any later-dated card up to the hour of the vote, so the power returns by its own clock with nothing worn off; the rate is zero at the margin, since each lender gives a vote worth nothing alone and the borrower assembles a majority from votes nobody priced; found one-sided when the activist settles with the board for two seats before the vote and the lenders learn their votes were the borrower's bargaining chip and never their ballot; not a sale, since the vote never leaves the share.
relations.to: Vote that dies in transit: the public gives its vote and receives the position, a share at a measured small discount, while the founder keeps ten votes a share; the carrier is the charter, which converts high-vote shares to one vote when they leave the founder's hands, so the founder's control is a power that cannot be sold onward, only held, and passes by sunset clause or by death; the rate is the dual-class discount, a few percent off for the vote given up; found one-sided when the founder's judgment goes and nothing but the calendar can retrieve the vote; not the proxy card, which lends a vote that survives the lending, since this is a vote the carrier kills to keep it from being lent at all.
relations.label: If the charter counts a proxy to an outsider as a transfer, as transfer sunsets commonly do with an exception for cards the board itself solicits, an activist can borrow from every holder except the founder, whose high vote dies when it moves; the proxy market exists only among votes that survive transfer, so the trade at the head of the itinerary is barred from the one holder with the most to lend.

relations.from: Hostage returned as partisan: a party gives another a power to punish it through a body it values, and receives a hold or a confirmation back, as in the medieval exchange of sons between truce-makers, which ran both ways, and the hostages Rome took from client kings, which ran one way and paid in the king's throne; the carrier is the body together with the giver's continuing love for it, since a hostage the giver stops valuing holds nothing, so the rate is set by the givers' caring and not by the ranks of the persons given; the trade inverts, on the standard reading of Roman practice, when the hostage raised in the holder's house returns as its friend, so the giver gave a hold and got back a party of the other side; not the ugly hostage of who-can-be-bound, a token worth nothing to its holder, since here the holder comes to value the body too, and that is what lets it be turned.
relations.to: Key man's lever: investors in a fund give their commitment and receive the power to suspend the fund's investing if named partners leave; the carrier is the limited partnership agreement; the rate looks cheap to the firm, which does not plan to lose the named, but the trade mints a power in a hand that was never a party to it and was often the firm's own voice at the table, since each named partner now holds a lever over its own firm, leaving triggers the suspension, and can price its staying at every renegotiation; the firm's power over its own partners is what was quietly sold; found one-sided when a named partner asks for more carry with the agreement open on the table; not a hostage, who is held, since the key man holds.
relations.label: If the giver goes on valuing the hostage, the hostage holds a lever of its own over the giver, and one raised to be the holder's friend holds one over both, so a hostage trade mints in the body exchanged the power the key-man clause mints in the named partner; the passage from inverted to minted runs through a person who learns it is valued by both sides.

exploration.first_question: By what mechanisms does power itself, rather than money or goods, change hands between parties, and which of the powers so traded can be traded back?
exploration.changed_question: Where does a traded power actually go: back to the giver by its own carrier, back lighter, back for the other side, nowhere, or into a hand that never sat at the table? Breath one assumed two parties and a return path; pressing on the carrier of the no-shop showed that the clause returns the paper and not the power, and the exchanged hostage refused to sit still, acquiring a lever of its own, so the question of trading back became the question of where the power went and whether the trade conserved it at all.

priorities.item: Fence around the process: a founder gives the power to run an auction for thirty days and receives a term sheet whose only binding clause is the fence; the carrier is the no-shop together with the other bidders' calendars, and the clause returns the power on its date, but the power was never in the clause, it lived in the bidders' heat, and bidders told to wait find other deals, so an auction paused does not resume at the temperature it was paused at; the rate is written as thirty days and paid as the auction, and the party inside the fence can lower its price in the last week knowing this; not a breakup fee, which prices the walk, since the fence prices nothing and consumes the alternative.
priorities.why: Every raise runs it, its carrier and its power are visibly different objects, and the gap between them can be measured from a fund's own records without any theory.
priorities.next_question: From one fund's files, take every term sheet whose no-shop lapsed without a close and record the bidders live at signing and the bidders who returned when the fence came down; the question is whether the heat that returns falls with the fence's length or drops to nothing at any length, which decides whether a shorter fence is a smaller loss or the same loss.

priorities.item: Kingmaker's tax: a small party gives its votes in the chamber and receives ministries, at a rate set by pivotality and not by size, so five seats that complete a majority buy more than forty that do not; the carrier is the coalition agreement and the confidence vote; the trade consumes not the power given but its source, since on a common reading the junior partner's voters, who elected it to be an alternative, punish it for having been a government, so the votes return at the next election and the electorate does not; not the veto, which keeps a future from happening, since the kingmaker makes one happen and is billed for it.
priorities.why: Low confidence that the tax is caused by the trade rather than by governing as such, high generative promise: it is the map's one case where the trade consumes the source of a power rather than the power, and if that shape is real it should appear wherever a delegated power is exercised in the delegator's name.
priorities.next_question: Find one junior partner that took only the power to withdraw (confidence and supply) and no ministries, and one that took ministries, in comparable parliaments, and compare their next elections; if the tax falls with the portfolio and not with the votes, what is consumed is the visible office, and the same test then applies to the key man who takes a title and the investor who takes a seat.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after repairing four items (Silence on the tab, which as written was a per-story fee the map's own bribe exclusion bars, now naming the source's accumulating veto; Hostage returned as partisan, whose mutual definition its Roman case contradicts; Customs house, whose 'expulsion' both named receiverships refute; Key man's lever, whose named partner sat at the table as the firm and is repaired to 'never a party') and sharpening two edge labels whose antecedents could not fail as written (Veto sold as an improbability → Drag for tag, Card for one meeting → Vote that dies in transit) and relabeling Hostage returned as partisan → Key man's lever to follow the Hostage repair, after failing to collapse Veto sold as an improbability into Drag for tag.

neighbors.left: Sword for quarter: the party that surrenders gives its residual power to fight and receives quarter; the carrier is the ceremony and the law that makes a prisoner a status rather than a corpse; the rate is set by what the residual resistance would cost the victor, so the garrison that can still make the siege expensive gets terms and the one that cannot gets none, which is why terms must be asked while the walls still stand; consumed in the giving, since the disarmed cannot rearm and the victor's side of the trade is enforced only by the victor's own need for the next surrender; the wolf that shows the throat gives the same thing at a rate set by the winner's need for a pack; not deference, which is given again each morning and can be withheld tomorrow.
neighbors.right: Queen for a day: a witness gives what it knows and receives use immunity under a proffer letter, which bars the prosecutor from using the words themselves; the carrier is the letter; the witness's power was the exclusivity of the fact, and it is consumed by the telling, since a fact once on the record is a record and not a lever, so the trade must be struck before the fact is spoken and the price can only fall after; found one-sided when derivative use arrives, the leads the words opened being chargeable though the words are not; not the sword, whose carrier passes to the victor, since here the carrier is copied and what dies is being the only one who holds it.
neighbors.separating_case: A defector who comes over with a pistol and the address of the safe house: handing over the pistol is the sword, consumed because the carrier passes, and the defector keeps every fact and can price each one separately afterward; giving the address is the proffer, consumed because the fact is now a record, and the defector keeps every weapon. Each power is consumed by a different route and a party can spend one while holding the other, so surrender and disclosure do not collapse into one item.

checks.boundary_case: A bribe, money for a decision, is out: the official exercises the power in the payer's favor and keeps it, so nothing moves but the outcome, and the same official can be bought again tomorrow by someone else. Seat for the check is in on exactly that contrast, since the vote itself changes hands and the buyer can cast it against the seller. Buying a controlling stake is the tempting middle case and is kept out as a goods trade in which power comes bundled with ownership; the map's terms (drag, veto, first look, super-vote) are in because each unbundles a power from the shares and prices it alone.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a loop the sequence conceals: Fence around the process → First look that chills the room → Fence around the process, where each round's exclusivity lowers the price of the next round's exclusivity, so a founder who reads the itinerary as one trade at a time never sees the ratchet. It shows an incompatibility at Veto sold as an improbability → Drag for tag, two powers each sold as improbable that collide in the same improbable state when they sit in different hands, where only one can hold. It shows a fork at Name on the door → Blame-bearer's fee, the same signature branching by which third parties route through it. It shows two passages between levels: Leased strike → Sword for quarter, where a power returned lighter each term is at some term indistinguishable from a power consumed, and Hostage returned as partisan → Key man's lever, where a power that returns inverted is seen to have minted a third party's power along the way. And Card for one meeting → Vote that dies in transit shows a dependency between the two ends of the itinerary: the market for lending votes exists only among votes that survive transfer, so the founder's super-vote is excluded from the proxy market by the same carrier that keeps it.
checks.target_preserved: Judged by the Fable critic in a fresh context, not a self-read: the critic tried to collapse Veto sold as an improbability into Drag for tag and could not, tested the hired agent as a boundary case and ruled it out because ordinary agency leaves the power at the principal's address while every member here has the carrier re-address it, and found the four repaired items type-compliant and stranger after repair, so the strange members (a paper that returns without the power, a hostage the holder comes to value and so can be turned, a sign that draws the summons, a vote that dies if it moves, a fact consumed by telling, a source's veto that accumulates in the reporter's own withheld stories, a trade that arms one side's own voice against it) remain mechanisms rather than advice.

name: power-law-behaviors
of: A mechanism by which a venture fund's arithmetic, its size, its fees, its carry, its reserves, its concentration cap, its term, and the quarterly letter that carries its marks, dictates how an investor behaves toward a founder at the table, named with the arithmetic, its carrier, the behavior it produces, and the founder-side move that exploits or defends against it, and sorted by whether the behavior would vanish if the fund were half its size or persists at any size because the money is other people's.
items: Below the care line: a check smaller than the fund's smallest meaningful position is priced by the fund as an option on seeing the next round rather than as an investment, as a two-billion-dollar fund's two-million-dollar seed cannot return the fund whatever the company does, since a hundred times on it is a tenth of the fund; the carrier is the ratio of the check to the fund, the behavior is indifference, an associate in the board seat, no fight over terms and none for the company, and the founder's move is to take the money only as passive capital beside a lead whose fund the check is large enough to hurt; not the partner's inattention, which is a person, since the same partner cares at a fund a tenth the size, and the one behavior on the map that vanishes entirely when the fund is resized.

Table below the line: a round made only of checks that sit below each writer's own care line has no holder whose arithmetic makes it show up at the bridge, so the party round of twelve small checks is cheap and quick to raise and nobody's when the company needs a lead, a bridge, or a signature in a hurry; the carrier is the largest check-to-fund ratio on the table rather than any one check, since the table is silent only while every ratio sits below its writer's line, the behavior is a cap table that goes silent at once, and the founder's move is to seat at least one holder for whom the position is large relative to its fund, even at a worse price, since that holder will do the work; not Below the care line, which is one indifferent check, since twelve indifferent checks make a second thing, a table with no seat, and it vanishes the moment any one check crosses its writer's line.

Fund on one exit: a fund that must return about three times its capital from one or two positions, after fees have eaten fifteen to twenty percent of it, requires of each company an exit that, at the ownership the fund will still hold after dilution, returns the whole fund, as a five-hundred-million-dollar fund holding ten percent at exit needs a five-billion-dollar sale; the carrier is the fund size divided by the ownership at exit, the behavior is the pass on a business that will very probably sell for three hundred million, delivered as 'not venture scale', and the founder's move is to raise from a fund whose size the plausible exit does return, since a fifty-million-dollar fund at ten percent is returned by five hundred million; not a judgment of odds, since the ninety-percent case is passed and the five-percent case is taken, and the threshold halves when the fund does.

Round sized from the far end: the fund's model fixes an ownership it must hold at exit and the dilution it expects between, so it fixes the ownership it must buy now, and its check size, fixed by fund size over the number of positions, then fixes the round, so a ten-million-dollar check at twenty percent is a fifty-million post-money whether or not the company needs ten million, and the fund asks the founder to 'raise a proper round' or to take the check at a lower price, counting its ownership net of the option pool the pre-money must carry; the carrier is the ownership target, the behavior is a round whose size was derived on the fund's side before the plan was read, and the founder's move is to learn the fund's check and target, back out the round it can say yes to, or split the target between two leads who each accept less; not Fund on one exit, which passes, since this one accepts and resizes, and the check halves with the fund while the target does not.

Silence of the one who could have: when a fund large enough to lead the next round takes a small position in this one, its later absence from the round is read by every outsider as knowledge, since the party with the most information and the most money declined, so the seed from the big fund carries a signal at the A that the same seed from a fund that never leads As cannot carry; the carrier is the insider's capacity relative to the round, the behavior is the outsider's question 'why isn't your seed investor leading', which the insider cannot answer without either leading or damning, and the founder's move is to take seed from funds too small to lead, or from a program the big fund has walled off by policy so that its silence is a rule rather than a verdict; not Pockets, not opinion, where the absence is arithmetic, since this absence is a choice, and the signal exists only where the fund is big enough to have had one.

Fund that grew away: management fees are a percentage of committed capital, so the partners' income doubles when the fund does, and the successor fund is sized by what the limited partners will give and what the fees need rather than by what the portfolio will need, so the fund that led the seed at fifty million has raised five hundred by the A, and the company is run through Fund on one exit a second time with a denominator ten times larger, which a company whose plausible exit returns fifty million at ten percent no longer passes; the grown fund could still lead by resizing the round to its check, as in Round sized from the far end, so its refusal is the failed test and the check the A cannot absorb is the symptom; the carrier is the fee on committed capital, the behavior is the insider who cheers the company and will not lead its next round at either size, which then reads as the silence above, and the founder's move is to ask which fund the pro-rata will be drawn from, to read the insider's own fundraising as a forecast of who will be at the next table, and to rerun the fund-returner test against the successor's size before counting on the insider; contested as a critique of managers, kept here as arithmetic about which fund exists when the next round comes; not Below the care line, since this fund was the right size when it arrived and moved, and the mirror of Living dead by denominator, where the denominator shrinks by secondary instead of growing by fees.

Living dead by denominator: after investment the fund sorts its portfolio by which companies can still return it, and a company that cannot is assigned no reserves and no partner time and is offered a quick sale, because a five-million-dollar check that comes back as thirty million, six times, adds six percent to a half-billion fund while the sale frees a board seat and returns capital the fund may recycle into a fresh position, so the small early exit has a value to the fund unrelated to its multiple; the carrier is the reserve model and the recycling provision, the behavior is the conversation about 'finding a home', and the founder's move is to notice that the label lives in the denominator, since the same thirty million returns a thirty-million-dollar fund whole, and to move the position to that fund by secondary, often below the last price, which frees the company and gives the seller the distribution it wanted; not Fund on one exit, which is run at entry, since this company was admitted, and the hinge of the map, since the label vanishes when the fund is halved and the triage does not.

Big holder wants the high price: on a round it partly funds, an investor's stake in the price has the sign of its pro-rata share of the round minus its new dollars, since its ownership after the round is its old shares plus its new money over the post-money, and that fraction rises with the price exactly when the new money is below pro-rata, so a holder with twenty percent that puts two million into a twenty-million-dollar round, where its pro-rata is four, argues the price up, a two-percent holder putting in the same two million argues it down, and the new lead, with no old shares, argues it down hardest, while a holder taking exactly its pro-rata is indifferent in ownership and argues up only for the letter, which marks every old share at the new price whatever the holder paid for the new ones; the carrier is the ratio of new money to pro-rata, the behavior is the largest insider taking the founder's side on price at the bridge, and the founder's move is to read each holder's stance on price off the cap table and the round size before the meeting rather than off its faith in the company, and to let the big holder name the number the new money must meet; not generosity, and reversed the moment the holder's new money exceeds its pro-rata, as at a recapitalization it funds alone, where the same holder wants the price down.

Stranger's price on the letter: a fund carries a position at the last round's price only when the price was set at arm's length, so a round priced by insiders alone marks little and a round led by an outsider marks the insider's whole position, which is why the insider that could fund the round by itself shops it to strangers and gives up allocation to get a stranger's number; the carrier is the fair-value rule the fund's auditor applies, the behavior is the insider distributing the deck and introducing the leads it will then compete with for allocation, and the founder's move is to take the insider's shopping as free distribution and to price the outsider's lead against the insider's need for the mark, since the insider will backstop the round to keep the stranger in; not what-a-price-does' Price for the stranger's eyes, where a seller protects a recorded number, since here a buyer procures a stranger to set one, and the item on which Big holder wants the high price depends, since a price nobody outside will sign at marks little.

Mark kept by structure: a fund's mark is made on the headline price and not on the preference-adjusted value, so a fund facing a down round prefers a flat price with a senior preference, a multiple, or a ratchet to a lower price with clean terms, because the letter records the price and the structure is invisible to it, and the founder's ownership drains through the preference stack at a price that never moved; the carrier is a valuation policy that reads price and not terms, the behavior is 'we can hold the valuation if we add some protection', and the founder's move is to price the structure as the down round it is, to take the clean lower price when the common's share of the plausible exits is higher under it, and to hear the insider's preference for structure as a statement about its letter and not about the company; adds to dilution-carriers' Headline bought with terms, which prices the trade, the investor's motive for it, a letter that cannot see the terms; not the preference itself, which is a term, and present at any fund size, since the letter is written for whoever's money it is.

Vintage's two appetites: a fund raises its successor on its marks two to four years in and on its distributions after, and is wound up at ten years plus extensions, so a young fund wants a priced up-round before its next raise and an old fund wants cash, and the same company hears 'raise more, go bigger' from one board seat and 'take the offer' from the other, each seat reading its own fund's calendar, as the whaling agent wanted the ship home with the oil while the captain wanted one more whale; the carrier is the term in the limited partnership agreement and the fundraising it forces, the behavior is a board split by vintage rather than by belief, and the founder's move is to read each investor's stance on the fork from its fund's age before asking, and to seat funds whose calendars agree; not tollgates-that-must-buy's Powder that must be lit, which is the compulsion to buy by a date, since this is what the fund needs to have happened to your company by when, and Sequoia's 2021 restructuring of its US and European business into an open-ended fund without a term removed the term and with it this behavior, while sharpening the letter items, since an open-ended fund's mark is also the price at which its limited partners may leave.

Call option at the board: carry is a share of profit above capital returned, a call option on the whole fund, so a fund whose portfolio is under water holds an option out of the money and wants variance, opposing the sale at one times that would return capital and pressing for the raise that might return the fund, while a fund already past its strike wants to lock in and supports the sale, and where the agreement carries a preferred return the strike sits above capital, so a fund at one and a half times in its seventh year under an eight-percent hurdle is still out of the money and still wants the swing; the carrier is the moneyness of the carry, the behavior is a board seat's stance on the acquisition offer set by the rest of that fund's portfolio, which the founder never sees, and the founder's move is to ask how the fund is doing before asking what it thinks, and to expect the under-water fund to want the swing that a diversified holder would not; by analogy the whaling captain on a lay with an empty hold late in the voyage hunts the worse water; not Fund on one exit, which is applied at entry to a company, since this is applied at exit by a portfolio's state, and it does not move when the fund is halved.

Chips bought off the table: a founder holds one undiversified position and prefers the sure three hundred million, while the fund holds thirty and prefers the swing, so the fund buys the founder's risk aversion with cash, allowing or arranging a secondary sale of founder shares at the round so that the founder will refuse the acquisition the fund does not want; the carrier is the founder's concave utility set against the fund's near-linear one, the behavior is secondary offered exactly at the round where an offer might come, and the founder's move is to ask for it there, since it is the price of variance and the fund is the buyer; contested, since some funds hold that a founder with money stops swinging, so the same arithmetic produces the opposite policy at other tables, and the map keeps both as one mechanism with a disputed sign; not a liquidity event, since the cash is bought for what it does to the founder's next decision.

Orphan on the board: carry is divided among partners by attribution, and a partner's standing rides on the deals carried under their name inside their own promotion window, so a junior partner wants a visible markup by a brand-name lead before the partnership vote and will help the founder get one at a lower ownership, and when a partner leaves the company loses the one person in the reserve model whose carry it was, so the successor, who gets no credit for it, lets it drift into the living dead regardless of its numbers; the carrier is the attribution of carry and the partner's clock inside the fund's, the behavior is a company whose treatment changes on a personnel move nobody at the company made, and the founder's move is, on the way up, to time the A to the sponsor's promotion window and let the sponsor's need for a brand-name markup pay for the ownership the fund would otherwise hold out for, and, on departure, to negotiate a named successor with attribution, or to buy the position out; adjacent to deal-deaths' Champion's single-tender want, which kills a deal before signing, since this changes the treatment of a company already owned.

Cap that sells the winner: the partnership agreement caps any one position at ten to twenty percent of the fund, so the fund cannot keep buying its best company past the cap and must watch the rounds it wants most go to outsiders or to a second vehicle it raises for the purpose, which then must price a round its own first fund also holds; the carrier is the concentration limit written by the limited partners, the behavior is a fund that fights for super pro-rata in the middling companies and cannot take pro-rata in the good one, and a fund that arrives with an opportunity fund and an appetite above its rights, and the founder's move is to run the second vehicle's appetite as competitive tension for the outside lead's price; not a reserve shortage, since the money exists and the rule forbids it, and it does not move when the fund is halved, since the cap is a fraction.

source.register: Operator-grade and concrete: fund sizes over ownership at exit, reserve ledgers, concentration caps, fair-value marks, carry moneyness, partner attribution, pro-rata assignments; drawn from venture practice with the whaling voyage as the one remote case.
source.mode: Analytical mechanisms with stylized illustrative arithmetic (two-and-twenty, a ten-year term, a three-times target) and observed cases simplified to one mechanism each; two items (Fund that grew away, Chips bought off the table) carry contested modality and say so, and the whaling captain is an analogy. Mark kept by structure is scoped by its carrier clause to valuation policies that read the headline price; option-pricing backsolves that see the preference stack are common under fair-value audits, and the item is not universal.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored analytical fieldwork with stylized arithmetic (two-and-twenty, a ten-year term, a three-times target, a ten-to-twenty-percent cap); real funds vary, Mark kept by structure holds only for valuation policies that read the headline price and not an option-pricing backsolve, and a real behavior at a table usually has several of these arithmetics behind it at once.

The seriation is an itinerary from behaviors that vanish when the fund is resized to behaviors that persist at any size, not a ranking of importance; its far pole is really 'intrinsic to a closed-end fund that writes a quarterly letter', and an evergreen or corporate vehicle removes some of it, as the Sequoia case shows for one item.

The illustrative cases (the whaling lay, the signaling discourse around big-fund seeds, the 2021 open-ended restructuring) are simplified to one mechanism each and the whaling captain is an analogy, not a claim about whaling history.

Two items carry contested modality: Fund that grew away is a critique of managers kept only as arithmetic about which fund exists at the next round, and Chips bought off the table has a disputed sign that practitioners resolve both ways.

Limited-partner behaviors (defaults on capital calls, sales of fund interests), corporate and sovereign investors without carry or a term, and the tactical use of the absent principal ('my LPs won't allow it') are outside the map.

seriation.axis: What the behavior is a function of: from the fund's size relative to your check and your round, so that resizing the fund removes it, through ratios inside the cap table that fund size does not touch, to the fund's state under other people's money (the letter, the term, the carry, the cap, the reserve ledger, the agreement), which persists as the money is halved and halved again to nothing.
seriation.note: An authored itinerary, not a scalar of importance or of harm. Below the care line opens it because it is the only behavior that vanishes outright when the fund is resized; Table below the line, Fund on one exit, Round sized from the far end, Silence of the one who could have, and Fund that grew away follow as behaviors whose threshold, check, signal, or successor scales with the fund. Living dead by denominator is the hinge: the label (living dead, fund-returner) moves with the denominator and vanishes when the fund is halved, while the triage that acts on the label (no reserves, no time, find a home) is partner time and recycling, which no resizing removes, so one item straddles the two halves and the edge from it to Fund on one exit is the founder's way to cross. Big holder wants the high price follows as the first behavior that fund size cannot touch, since its sign is the holder's pro-rata share of the round minus its new money, which scales with the fund and keeps its sign when the fund is halved. Fund that grew away, repaired as the fund-returner test rerun with a fee-grown denominator, is the hinge's mirror: Living dead by denominator shrinks the denominator by secondary and this one grows it by fees. The second half, Stranger's price on the letter through Vote without a checkbook, runs by which piece of other people's money carries the behavior: the letter's valuation rule (Stranger's price, Mark kept by structure), the term (Vintage's two appetites), the carry (Call option at the board, Chips bought off the table, Orphan on the board), the limited partners' cap (Cap that sells the winner), the reserve ledger (Pockets, not opinion), and finally the bare agreement (Vote without a checkbook), which closes the walk because it is what remains at size zero. Pockets, not opinion → Vote without a checkbook is the consequential adjacency: the same absence is a curable fact about one company on one side and a standing veto about the whole fund on the other, and the founder's move changes kind, from asking for a letter to buying the seat. The second half is a grouping by carrier rather than a gradient, so its inner adjacencies (letter to term, carry to cap) teach less than the two this note defends; the Fable critic's honesty note, kept here.
