relations.label: If the partner whose carry the company was leaves, then the company enters the triage with no advocate in the reserve model, so the denominator test is run against it by someone with nothing to gain from passing it, and numbers that would have kept it alive under its sponsor no longer do.

exploration.first_question: By what mechanisms does a venture fund's arithmetic (its size, its fees, its carry, its reserves, its term) dictate how a partner behaves toward a founder at the table, and what does each behavior let the founder do?
exploration.changed_question: Which of these behaviors are functions of the fund's size relative to the company, so that a fund half the size would not produce them, and which are functions of the fund's state under other people's money, a letter, a term, a carry, a cap, a ledger, an agreement, so that no resizing removes them? The first breath put every behavior at the round, in the price, the size, and the pass; sharpening reserves against the zombie showed that the most consequential behaviors happen between rounds and at the exit, and come from the fund's state, its moneyness, its age, its ledger, its partner's tenure, rather than its size.
exploration.new_member: Call option at the board: carry is a share of profit above capital returned, a call option on the whole fund, so a fund whose portfolio is under water holds an option out of the money and wants variance, opposing the sale at one times that would return capital and pressing for the raise that might return the fund, while a fund already past its strike wants to lock in and supports the sale, and where the agreement carries a preferred return the strike sits above capital, so a fund at one and a half times in its seventh year under an eight-percent hurdle is still out of the money and still wants the swing; the carrier is the moneyness of the carry, the behavior is a board seat's stance on the acquisition offer set by the rest of that fund's portfolio, which the founder never sees, and the founder's move is to ask how the fund is doing before asking what it thinks, and to expect the under-water fund to want the swing that a diversified holder would not; by analogy the whaling captain on a lay with an empty hold late in the voyage hunts the worse water; not Fund on one exit, which is applied at entry to a company, since this is applied at exit by a portfolio's state, and it does not move when the fund is halved.

priorities.item: Big holder wants the high price: on a round it partly funds, an investor's stake in the price has the sign of its pro-rata share of the round minus its new dollars, since its ownership after the round is its old shares plus its new money over the post-money, and that fraction rises with the price exactly when the new money is below pro-rata, so a holder with twenty percent that puts two million into a twenty-million-dollar round, where its pro-rata is four, argues the price up, a two-percent holder putting in the same two million argues it down, and the new lead, with no old shares, argues it down hardest, while a holder taking exactly its pro-rata is indifferent in ownership and argues up only for the letter, which marks every old share at the new price whatever the holder paid for the new ones; the carrier is the ratio of new money to pro-rata, the behavior is the largest insider taking the founder's side on price at the bridge, and the founder's move is to read each holder's stance on price off the cap table and the round size before the meeting rather than off its faith in the company, and to let the big holder name the number the new money must meet; not generosity, and reversed the moment the holder's new money exceeds its pro-rata, as at a recapitalization it funds alone, where the same holder wants the price down.
priorities.why: It is a sign computed from three numbers every founder already has, each holder's ownership, the round size, and its check, and it predicts a stance most founders get backwards, so it can be tested on paper against any bridge round that has minutes.
priorities.next_question: Take five bridge or extension rounds from the last two years where each holder's position on price is on record; for each holder compute its pro-rata share of the round, its ownership fraction times the round size, minus the new dollars it will put in, predict its stance on price from the sign, with a holder at exactly pro-rata predicted to argue up only as far as the letter rewards it, and count the misses; a miss rate under one in five makes the cap table and the round size a better predictor of the price argument than anyone's faith in the company.

priorities.item: Living dead by denominator: after investment the fund sorts its portfolio by which companies can still return it, and a company that cannot is assigned no reserves and no partner time and is offered a quick sale, because a five-million-dollar check that comes back as thirty million, six times, adds six percent to a half-billion fund while the sale frees a board seat and returns capital the fund may recycle into a fresh position, so the small early exit has a value to the fund unrelated to its multiple; the carrier is the reserve model and the recycling provision, the behavior is the conversation about 'finding a home', and the founder's move is to notice that the label lives in the denominator, since the same thirty million returns a thirty-million-dollar fund whole, and to move the position to that fund by secondary, often below the last price, which frees the company and gives the seller the distribution it wanted; not Fund on one exit, which is run at entry, since this company was admitted, and the hinge of the map, since the label vanishes when the fund is halved and the triage does not.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that anyone builds it and high generative promise: if the label lives in the denominator, then a fund whose whole business is buying living-dead positions from big funds and leading their next rounds is a lead investor that never competes for a new deal, and its existence would be a test of the map's hinge.
priorities.next_question: List twenty secondary sales of a single venture position from a fund over five hundred million to a fund under one hundred million; record the price against the last round and whether the buyer then led the company's next round; if the buyer led in most cases at a price below the seller's mark, the denominator arbitrage exists and the hinge holds.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after repairing the price-stance arithmetic in Big holder wants the high price and its dependent edge, restating Fund that grew away as the fund-returner test rerun with a fee-grown denominator, correcting the carrier of Table below the line, scoping the Sequoia claim, naming the carry's strike under a hurdle, and giving Orphan on the board's promotion-window half its founder move; the repairer also closed two worked cases the critic did not test (Living dead by denominator now uses a six-times, thirty-million outcome that a thirty-million fund is returned by; Below the care line says a hundred times on the seed is a tenth of the fund) and matched Stranger's price on the letter's discriminator to its mechanism (marks little, not nothing).

neighbors.left: Silence of the one who could have: when a fund large enough to lead the next round takes a small position in this one, its later absence from the round is read by every outsider as knowledge, since the party with the most information and the most money declined, so the seed from the big fund carries a signal at the A that the same seed from a fund that never leads As cannot carry; the carrier is the insider's capacity relative to the round, the behavior is the outsider's question 'why isn't your seed investor leading', which the insider cannot answer without either leading or damning, and the founder's move is to take seed from funds too small to lead, or from a program the big fund has walled off by policy so that its silence is a rule rather than a verdict; not Pockets, not opinion, where the absence is arithmetic, since this absence is a choice, and the signal exists only where the fund is big enough to have had one.
neighbors.right: Pockets, not opinion: reserves are allocated per company from a finite pool, and a fund whose reserves are spent, on other companies or on this one in an earlier bridge, cannot take its pro-rata, so its absence from the round looks like the silence of the one who could have while being arithmetic, and the fund usually will not say so, since 'we are out of reserves' is heard by its other companies and by its next fund's investors; the carrier is the reserve ledger, the behavior is an unexplained absence that kills the round, and the founder's move is to make the ledger visible by asking the fund to sell or assign its pro-rata right to a co-investor or a special-purpose vehicle, which is the one act that says out of money rather than out of faith; adds to term-sheet-powers' Reserves test in loyalty's clothing, which sorts the syndicate by reserves, and its Option on the next round's information, which prices the right, the fund's motive for silence and the assignment as the founder's cure; not Silence of the one who could have, since the tell cures this one, and the last stop before the fund's money reaches zero.
neighbors.separating_case: The same absence from the same round from two insiders. A two-billion-dollar fund with untouched reserves that took the seed and does not lead the A: nothing the founder can produce cures it, since the fund's absence is a choice and the only cure was a policy the fund set before the seed. A sixty-million-dollar fund that bridged this company twice and has nothing left: its absence is a ledger fact, and the founder cures it by getting the fund to assign its pro-rata right to a co-investor, which no fund with money and doubt would do. One absence is cured by the fund's public policy, the other by its public ledger, and a fund cannot fake the second cure without giving up the right.

checks.boundary_case: 'My limited partners would never allow it' is the tempting nonmember: it is other people's money at its purest, and it is out, because it works as a bargaining shield whether or not any arithmetic stands behind it, so it is an authority tactic and belongs with the ratifier in deal-deaths and with negotiation lists, not here. The constraints the limited partners actually wrote that produce behavior by arithmetic, the concentration cap and the term, are in as Cap that sells the winner and Vintage's two appetites.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a loop the itinerary conceals, Round sized from the far end → Fund that grew away: the ownership target sizes the round, the round's size justifies the successor fund's size, and the successor's check needs a larger round, so the company's need is an input nowhere in the cycle. It shows a fork at Vintage's two appetites → Call option at the board: an old fund in the money wants your sale and an old fund under water wants your swing, so the vintage, which the sequence presents as one appetite per age, does not predict the vote without the moneyness. It shows two dependencies: Stranger's price on the letter → Big holder wants the high price, where the letter half of the holder's price preference is worth nothing until an outsider signs and only the ownership arithmetic remains, and Orphan on the board → Living dead by denominator, where the triage depends on who is left to argue. It shows an incompatibility at Cap that sells the winner → Big holder wants the high price: past the cap a fund can keep the mark or the ownership, not both. It shows a passage between levels at Pockets, not opinion → Vote without a checkbook, where an absence about one company becomes a veto about the whole fund and the founder's move changes kind. And the edge Living dead by denominator → Fund on one exit is the live question drawn: the one place where halving the fund, by moving the position to a fund half the size, changes a behavior after the fact.
checks.target_preserved: Fable critic (fresh context, 2026-09-08) judged the target preserved and the verdict admit-with-repairs: the strange members survive as mechanisms, the largest holder as the founder's ally on price now with the correct sign, the fund that cannot buy more of its best company sharper under that sign as the purest price hawk, the letter paid in mark for structure, the veto from a seat with no money, and the secondary that reruns the fund-returner test, now mirrored by the fund that grew away; the two contested items keep their modality.

name: term-sheet-powers
of: Mechanisms by which a term in a financing carries power beyond its price, each named with the future state in which it bites, who holds the power when that state arrives, and the case in which the term proved worthless or fatal, including terms whose only cash value is the price of their own waiver and terms exercised by a holder who never signed them.
items: Redemption clock: after a stated number of years the preferred may demand its money back, which bites only in the state where the company is alive, unsold, and unable to raise, and there it is rarely a claim on cash, since a Delaware company may redeem only from funds legally available and the board decides what those are, as the ThoughtWorks investors learned when their demand yielded a determination rather than a payment; the power is not the money but the standing to put the company in default, which is then sold back as forbearance.

Claim on the middle: a one-times non-participating preference exists only for exits between the preference and the point where converting to common pays more, since at the top it converts and adds nothing and at zero it is a claim on nothing, as the stack of preferences that exceeds a company's realistic sale price leaves the common underwater and makes the acquirer buy the management back with a carve-out plan; not downside protection, which would pay at the bottom, but a claim on the modal exit that nobody at signing rehearses.

Flat where the founder is steep: in the band where the preferred's payoff is flat, from the preference up to the conversion point for non-participating stock and from the cap up to it for capped participation, the preferred gains nothing from a higher price while the common's payoff is at its steepest, so a holder with a vote on the sale prefers the certain offer now to a better one later, as when the investors accept an acquirer's price inside the flat band and the founders, whose every extra dollar would be theirs, are dragged; not the size of the claim but its slope, and an uncapped participating preferred has the claim without the flatness.

Stack that sorts the syndicate: seniority among series decides who is paid first in the middling exit and so sorts the investors into parties with different preferences over the same sale, since the senior holder is whole at any price above its own preference and the junior is whole only above the whole stack, as when the later fund's senior preference makes it a seller at a price at which the earlier fund is a holdout; not investor against founder but the rules of a fight among investors, which the founder signs and later meets as a board that cannot agree to sell.

Chair that owes the room: a board seat is a vote that matters only when the board is split, a place at the information every month, and a duty that runs to the common as residual claimant rather than to the fund that appointed the director, so in the middling exit where the preference takes the price and the common takes nothing the seat becomes an exposure in the very state it was taken for, as litigated in the Trados sale, where the preferred took the proceeds, the management plan took the rest, and the common took nothing; not control, since one seat controls nothing, but a channel that carries a duty against its holder, which is why a fund sometimes prefers the observer's chair, information without duty.

First to know it is dying: monthly financials and inspection rights are worth the lag between holders, since whoever learns first that the company is failing can stop reserving, mark down, sell a position, or decline the bridge before the others know it is needed, as the major investor who passes on the rescue it was first to see coming while the holders below the threshold find out at the wash-out; not a power over the company but a power relative to the other holders, and worthless in the company that never sends the reports and is never made to, which on this map's reading of the practice is most companies until the state arrives.

Pass that stamps the sale: a right of first refusal on transfers, held by the parties who also hold the information, makes every secondary sale a lemons market before any refusal is given, since the outside buyer wins only in the case where the insiders, who saw the numbers, chose not to match, so it bids as if it had already lost every case worth winning, and the founder or angel who needs liquidity finds the outsider's price discounted by a pass that has not yet happened while the insiders may match at that discount; not a price set for the stranger's eyes but a refusal read before it is given, and it bites hardest on the holder who needs the sale most.

Fired into the cliff: founder shares vest on a schedule the board can cut short by terminating the founder, and the voting agreement fixes the board that the founder's majority of common might otherwise unseat, so the cap table is changed by a personnel act rather than by a vote on shares, as the cofounder let go in the eleventh month, one short of the cliff, whose entire grant is bought back at cost by the company the board controls; not a hold on pay still owed but a hold on ownership already granted, released or seized by whoever controls employment, and an acquirer's double trigger is the same term read from the other side.

Veto priced by the clock: protective provisions let a class block a sale, a senior round, or new debt, and the block is worth exactly what the blocked party's speed is worth, so the same veto is a formality in a cash-rich year and a power over survival with three weeks of runway, as the seed class that holds up the rescue round for a better conversion until the round dies; not the right to demand anything but the right to delay everything, and series-by-series votes multiply the vetoes while a single-class vote lets the large series override the small.

Option on the next round's information: pro rata is a call on the next round at the next round's price, worth the gap between what the insider knows and what the price reflects, so it is worth most in the oversubscribed round of a winner, where it crowds the new lead who wants the allocation, and nothing in the down round or in the hands of a fund with no reserves left to exercise it, as the seed fund whose whole return sat in the pro rata of two companies it could not afford to follow; not a promise of support but a free option granted as a courtesy, and its value concentrates exactly where the founder has the most alternatives.

Threshold that quietly disenfranchises: information rights, pro rata, and the rest are granted to a major investor defined by a fraction of the stock or by a share count restated in each round's paper, so a later round that dilutes a holder below the fraction, or lifts the count above its holding, strips its powers by arithmetic or by definition rather than by any vote of the holder stripped, as the seed fund that learns of the sale from the press because it fell out of the definition two rounds earlier; not a term with a bite of its own but the key that decides who holds the others, and its holder is whoever writes the next definition.

Reserves test in loyalty's clothing: pay-to-play converts the preferred of any investor who does not fund its share of the down round into common, or strips its anti-dilution, so it bites on funds without reserves rather than on founders and sorts the syndicate by dry powder under the name of commitment, as the small seed fund in its eighth year whose entire position converts; not a founder's term at all, since the founder is an incidental beneficiary, and not the fade by formula that clean-exits carries as the leaver's price fixed at entry, but a term investors sign against each other while imagining they would always play, whose bite is decided by a reserve ledger written at another table.

Ratchet that must be waived: full-ratchet anti-dilution reprices the earlier round to the down round's price, and exercised as written it wipes the common, so the new lead refuses to fund a cap table with no management incentive, and unless the ratchet's holder leads the down round itself, the round the ratchet was written for is the round in which it must be waived; not protection against the down round but a chip that matures into it, and its whole value is the price of its own waiver, paid in a board seat, a fee, or a gentler formula.

Claim on terms not yet written: a most-favored-nation clause copies the best terms of any later instrument to every earlier holder, so a sweetener the desperate company offers one rescuer is multiplied across everyone who holds the clause, and the rescue that needed one sweetener cannot afford the propagated one; a term priced by a negotiation between two other parties that has not happened yet, and unlike the most-favored promise offered to break an impasse, its bite is the multiplier it becomes later.

Threshold that ends independence: drag-along names the coalition, usually the board plus a preferred majority, that can force every holder to sell, and it bites when the investors' clocks diverge from the company's, as the fund past its tenth year that needs distributions and pulls the drag at a price inside the stack where the common takes nothing; not the minority's same-price protection but the trigger and whose clock sets it, and it is worthless without a buyer, who knows this and prices the drag into the offer.

New money rewrites the old paper: any term that bites only through an outside arrival can be made a condition of the arrival, so the new lead demands the ratchet waived, the stack collapsed, pay-to-play imposed, or every earlier preferred converted to common at a fraction, and the old terms are worth at most what the arrival is worth to their holders, as in the recapitalization that turns three rounds of preferences into common in one afternoon; not a term but the state that reprices terms, and the true counterparty of a state-contingent power is whoever supplies the state.

Successor in the chair: a term is held by an entity and exercised by whoever holds the entity's pen when the state arrives, so the veto priced against a friendly partner is pulled by that partner's replacement, by a secondary buyer who took the position at a discount and breaks even at a different price, by a continuation vehicle with a fresh clock, or by the liquidating manager handed a fund's book in wind-down, as the drag that was a courtesy at signing and a sale order twelve years later from a hand that never signed; not the same holder whose clock has run, which Threshold that ends independence carries, but the replacement of the holder, and the counterparty of the term was never the counterparty of the negotiation.

source.register: Operator-grade and concrete: preferences, ratchets, vetoes, drags, thresholds, and seats as they appear in United States venture preferred-stock documents, with two Delaware decisions (ThoughtWorks on redemption, Trados on the preferred's director) and the fund's own life cycle as the remote domain that sharpens the last two items.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism; the recapitalization and the successor cases are readings of a common practice rather than of a named dispute, and the thesis that terms are mispriced in proportion to the distance of their biting state is an authored interpretation carried by the seriation, not a measurement.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored fieldwork on the United States venture form set, chiefly NVCA-style preferred stock; not a survey of every term, not a legal opinion, and the same handle can bite differently under another draft or another jurisdiction.

The mispricing thesis is an interpretation: the seriation is an itinerary of how much must change from the day of signing before a term bites, not a measured scale of mispricing, and no empirical claim about which terms parties misprice is made.

The illustrative cases (ThoughtWorks, Trados, the eleventh-month firing, the recapitalization, the fund past its tenth year) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not accounts of the specific histories.

Price itself is outside: valuation, the pre-money option pool, discounts, caps, and the cumulative dividend that accrues into the preference without anyone exercising it, and every route by which ownership drains other than through a power in a state, belong to another map.
Debt covenants, warrants, and the fund's own partnership terms are outside except as cases; Successor in the chair points at fund-level terms without mapping them.

seriation.axis: How much must change from the day of signing before the term bites: nothing but the calendar (a redemption date arrives), then the company's own fortunes (the middling exit, the flat band, the split syndicate, the conflicted seat, the decline seen first, the founder's sale, the founder's firing), then an outside arrival (the party whose speed prices the veto, the next round and the major-investor definition it restates, the down round, the rescuer, the buyer), and finally the parties themselves (the arrival that rewrites the paper, the holder who is replaced).
seriation.note: An authored itinerary, not a ranking of severity or a scale of mispricing. Redemption clock opens it because nothing but the calendar need change for it to bite, and even there the bite is a determination rather than a payment; Successor in the chair closes it because the party exercising the term is no longer the party who priced it. The route's interpretive claim is that the further along it a term sits, the less anyone at the table rehearses its state, which is the live question answered as an itinerary rather than as a finding. Claim on the middle → Flat where the founder is steep is the first teaching adjacency: the claim says where the preferred is paid, the flatness says where it stops caring, and between them lies the band in which the investor's vote is for the sale and the founder's is against it. Threshold that quietly disenfranchises sits at the arrival stop beside the next round, on the critic's correction: a line is crossed only when a later issuance dilutes the holder or restates the definition, never by the calendar, so its earlier filing at the first stop was a misassignment. New money rewrites the old paper → Successor in the chair is the hinge: once a term bites only through an arrival, the arrival can rewrite it, and once the holder is replaced, the term is exercised by someone who never priced it, so the last two stops are where the signer neither supplies the state nor holds the power, and every earlier stop is repriced from there.

relations.label: If the refusal right sits with the holders who also receive the reports, then the outsider bids only for the case in which those holders chose not to match, so the information lag is what gives the refusal its price; strip the lag (reports shared with every holder and with the buyer) and the refusal becomes a courtesy and the outsider's discount vanishes. The refusal depends on the lag; nothing returns to the insiders' book.

relations.from: New money rewrites the old paper: any term that bites only through an outside arrival can be made a condition of the arrival, so the new lead demands the ratchet waived, the stack collapsed, pay-to-play imposed, or every earlier preferred converted to common at a fraction, and the old terms are worth at most what the arrival is worth to their holders, as in the recapitalization that turns three rounds of preferences into common in one afternoon; not a term but the state that reprices terms, and the true counterparty of a state-contingent power is whoever supplies the state.
relations.to: Threshold that quietly disenfranchises: information rights, pro rata, and the rest are granted to a major investor defined by a fraction of the stock or by a share count restated in each round's paper, so a later round that dilutes a holder below the fraction, or lifts the count above its holding, strips its powers by arithmetic or by definition rather than by any vote of the holder stripped, as the seed fund that learns of the sale from the press because it fell out of the definition two rounds earlier; not a term with a bite of its own but the key that decides who holds the others, and its holder is whoever writes the next definition.
relations.label: If the new lead's paper raises the major-investor line, then the earlier holders lose their information and pro rata rights one round before the state in which they would have used them; the rewriting is silent because the powers vanish by definition rather than by vote, and the same arrival that supplies the state decides who is still entitled to see it.

exploration.first_question: Which terms in a financing carry power beyond their price, in which future state does each bite, who holds the power then, and in which case did the term prove worthless or fatal? And which of them are priced by the parties who sign them?
exploration.changed_question: Breath one assumed each term is exercised as written in its state. Sharpening the ratchet, the redemption right, and the class veto against their own states showed that each is unusable as written in exactly the state it was written for (the ratchet kills the round it protects against, the redemption demands cash the law will not release, the veto delays a rescue the vetoing class also needs), so each is cashed as consent, the price of its waiver, paid by whoever must supply the state. The question moved to: who supplies the state in which a term bites, and who holds the term when it arrives? Both answers name parties who are never in the room at signing, the new money whose arrival triggers the state and can rewrite the paper as a condition of arriving, and the successor who holds the term after the partner, the fund, or the position has changed hands. The pointer's title stands; the of-sentence now includes waiver-only terms and unsigning holders.
exploration.new_member: New money rewrites the old paper: any term that bites only through an outside arrival can be made a condition of the arrival, so the new lead demands the ratchet waived, the stack collapsed, pay-to-play imposed, or every earlier preferred converted to common at a fraction, and the old terms are worth at most what the arrival is worth to their holders, as in the recapitalization that turns three rounds of preferences into common in one afternoon; not a term but the state that reprices terms, and the true counterparty of a state-contingent power is whoever supplies the state.

priorities.item: Flat where the founder is steep: in the band where the preferred's payoff is flat, from the preference up to the conversion point for non-participating stock and from the cap up to it for capped participation, the preferred gains nothing from a higher price while the common's payoff is at its steepest, so a holder with a vote on the sale prefers the certain offer now to a better one later, as when the investors accept an acquirer's price inside the flat band and the founders, whose every extra dollar would be theirs, are dragged; not the size of the claim but its slope, and an uncapped participating preferred has the claim without the flatness.
priorities.why: It is arithmetic on a cap table rather than a reading of documents, so it can be checked on any real company in an hour; and it names the modal disagreement over a sale, which founders experience as a difference of ambition when it is a difference of slope.
priorities.next_question: Take one real cap table with two or three series, compute each holder's payoff slope at every exit value from zero to the last conversion point, and mark the bands in which a holder with a sale vote has zero slope; then list every acquisition offer the company received and ask which offers fell inside a flat band, and whether those were the offers the investors urged accepting.

priorities.item: Successor in the chair: a term is held by an entity and exercised by whoever holds the entity's pen when the state arrives, so the veto priced against a friendly partner is pulled by that partner's replacement, by a secondary buyer who took the position at a discount and breaks even at a different price, by a continuation vehicle with a fresh clock, or by the liquidating manager handed a fund's book in wind-down, as the drag that was a courtesy at signing and a sale order twelve years later from a hand that never signed; not the same holder whose clock has run, which Threshold that ends independence carries, but the replacement of the holder, and the counterparty of the term was never the counterparty of the negotiation.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that it can be priced at signing, high generative promise: it asks whether any state-contingent term can be priced without a model of who its holder will be in that state, which turns the term sheet into a question about the fund's partnership agreement, and nobody negotiates one against the other.
priorities.next_question: For one company's cap table, list each term's holder as of signing and as of today (partner in the seat, fund year, secondary transfers, continuation vehicles, key-person events) and mark the terms whose effective holder changed; then ask which of those terms was priced against the original holder's clock, and whether a single clause (a consent right over transfers of the preferred, a sunset on the veto at fund year ten) would have kept the term with the party who priced it.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference
gate.independent_review: Fable critic: admitted after cutting one item that was a drain rather than a power and duplicated a sibling, repairing the reversed causal order in the refusal-right item and the successor item's overlap with the drag, adding a missing discriminator against clean-exits, relabeling three edges (the claimed loop is a dependency, the veto passage is preventable by a clause outside the veto, and the reach-back to the first stop was an artifact of misfiling the threshold on the seriation). The repairer also applied the critic's three modality touches (the Trados seat is an exposure, not a liability; the ratchet's waiver is forced unless its holder leads the down round itself; 'most companies' is marked as the map's reading) and corrected three kept items against worked cases: the junior series is whole, not merely paid, only above the whole stack; a firing in the eleventh month forfeits the entire grant, not three quarters; and a major-investor line fixed as a share count or dollar figure is never crossed by dilution, so the threshold item now names the fraction that is and the restated count that is lifted.

neighbors.left: Claim on the middle: a one-times non-participating preference exists only for exits between the preference and the point where converting to common pays more, since at the top it converts and adds nothing and at zero it is a claim on nothing, as the stack of preferences that exceeds a company's realistic sale price leaves the common underwater and makes the acquirer buy the management back with a carve-out plan; not downside protection, which would pay at the bottom, but a claim on the modal exit that nobody at signing rehearses.
neighbors.right: Flat where the founder is steep: in the band where the preferred's payoff is flat, from the preference up to the conversion point for non-participating stock and from the cap up to it for capped participation, the preferred gains nothing from a higher price while the common's payoff is at its steepest, so a holder with a vote on the sale prefers the certain offer now to a better one later, as when the investors accept an acquirer's price inside the flat band and the founders, whose every extra dollar would be theirs, are dragged; not the size of the claim but its slope, and an uncapped participating preferred has the claim without the flatness.
neighbors.separating_case: An uncapped participating preferred: it holds a claim in the middling exit, taking its preference and then its share, so Claim on the middle is present; but its payoff rises with every dollar of price, so there is no band in which its holder stops caring, and Flat where the founder is steep is absent. Conversely a one-times non-participating preferred is flat from the preference to the conversion point. Participation keeps the claim and removes the flatness, which pulls the two mechanisms apart: one is where the claim exists, the other is where its slope is zero.

checks.boundary_case: The pre-money option pool, sized by the investor and counted in the pre-money so the founders alone are diluted by it, is a tempting member: it moves ownership without a vote and bites in a state the founder did not picture (a pool left unissued at exit). It is out because it has no state in which it does anything other than lower the effective price; it is price in disguise, and belongs to a map of ownership drains. Registration rights fail from the other side: there is no state in which they bite that the underwriters do not control, so they are a fossil at signing rather than a power.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a fork the sequence conceals: Option on the next round's information and Reserves test in loyalty's clothing sit at different stops but draw on the same reserve in opposite states, so a fund cannot fully hold both without dry powder kept for both weathers. It shows two passages between levels: Ratchet that must be waived → New money rewrites the old paper, where a term over the founder becomes a chip against whoever supplies its state, and Veto priced by the clock → Successor in the chair, where the term passes from its wording to its holder, preventable only by a clause outside the veto. It shows three dependencies: First to know it is dying → Pass that stamps the sale, where the information lag is what gives the refusal its price (the author drew this as a loop returning to the insiders' own mark; the critic struck the return, since the insiders' preferred never passes through the refusal gate they hold and funds mark to the last round's price); Stack that sorts the syndicate → Threshold that ends independence, where the drag's counting rule decides whose split preference governs; and New money rewrites the old paper → Threshold that quietly disenfranchises, two terms at the arrival stop where the same arrival that supplies the state decides who is still entitled to see it. And it shows a claim recruiting a duty against its own holder at Claim on the middle → Chair that owes the room.
checks.target_preserved: The Fable critic's judgment, not a self-read: each item names a term, the state in which it bites, the holder in that state, and a case where it was worthless or fatal; the strange members (a claim on the middle that buys back the management it stripped, a term whose whole value is its own waiver, a seat that is an exposure in the state it was taken for, a refusal read before it is given, a holder who never signed) survived the critic's pressure as mechanisms rather than being softened into advice, and the one member cut, the accruing dividend, was cut under the map's own type and boundary for being a drain that nobody exercises.

name: walkaway-manufactures
of: A mechanism by which a party builds, borrows, or fakes an alternative to the table it is at, or a leaving that needs no alternative, named with the carrier that holds the alternative, what it costs to keep it credible, the tell by which a counterparty detects a fake, and the fake that survives detection, and sorted by where the alternative's existence is held: in a state of the world, in a contract or a certificate, in another party's patience, money, calendar, or jurisdiction, in a depleting quantity or a relationship's temperature, in the record, in the holder's own knowledge, in the checker's bill, in the counterparty's prior, or in the counterparty's ignorance.
items: Nothing to leave: the walkaway is the state the party already stands in, so a company that covers its costs declines a round by doing nothing, and the option needs no counterparty, no paper, and no belief; the carrier is the profit-and-loss statement, which the investor reads in diligence; keeping it credible costs the growth forgone to stay there, so the option is paid for every month in hires not made; the tell is the burn line and whether the company has ever actually chosen the state, since 'we could be profitable by cutting' names a state the company has never stood in; the fake that survives is the cut never made, because the investor cannot see which team would go or whether the product survives their going; not survival-floors' Plot that must be tended, a floor under a person outside any wage, since here the floor is under the firm's refusal and is priced against the round it declines.

Paid floor: an outside option is bought as a real bid, as the stalking-horse bidder in a bankruptcy sale signs a binding purchase agreement and is paid a break-up fee if outbid, so the seller's walkaway exists by contract before the auction opens; the carrier is the signed agreement and the court-approved fee; keeping it credible costs the fee, a few percent of the price, plus a floor set below where the seller hopes to finish; the tell is the fee's size and the expense reimbursement beside it, since a large fee reveals that nobody expected a second bidder and prices the option the seller had to buy; no fake is needed because the option is real by construction, and its failure is the horse chosen because it would win; not power-trades' Fence around the process, which sells the auction's power to one bidder, since here the seller buys a bidder so that there is an auction at all.

Qualified on paper: the alternative is proven feasible without being used, as the second supplier whose parts passed qualification lots and sit on the approved-vendor list with no orders, so the incumbent faces a certificate that a switch could be made; the carrier is the qualification record and its date; keeping it credible costs re-qualification every time the specification moves and the second source's line staying tooled, so an unrevised certificate decays as the product changes under it; the tell is the date of the last qualifying lot against the date of the last design change, and whether the second line still exists; the fake that survives is the qualification of a superseded part, which the incumbent cannot check without the customer's revision history; not lead-time-floors' Understudy, a replacement finished and waiting, since the understudy is bought for the day the source dies and the certificate for the day the source is priced.

Fed suitor: the alternative is a party with wants of its own, so the second supplier or the rival employer stays an option only while it is given something, a share of the volume, a real chance at the position, and stops quoting the third time it learns it was the stalking horse; the carrier is the suitor's patience; keeping it credible costs a dual-source tax, the ten or twenty percent of volume placed with the second source at a worse price, or the interviews one actually sits; the tell is how long the suitor has been in place and what it has received, since a second source at zero share for three years is a name and not an option; the fake that survives is the suitor who knows and stays because it is paid to, which is the Paid floor by another door; not Qualified on paper, where the certificate needs no one's consent and decays with the spec, since here the option decays with a person's willingness.

Rented war chest: the walkaway is the ability to go the distance, to trial rather than settlement, to the tenth week, to the next quarter, and it is supplied by a third party who buys a share of the outcome, as the litigation funder who pays the plaintiff's costs against a slice of the award, or the parent whose guarantee lets a subsidiary refuse a supplier's terms; the carrier is the funding agreement, which the funder holds and the holder does not fully own; keeping it credible costs the funder's slice and the funder's continuing belief in the case; the tell is disclosure, since defendants ask whether a funder exists and some courts now require the answer, and then the terms, since a funder who may withdraw below a settlement threshold owns the walkaway; the fake that survives is the funder disclosed without its terms, so the defendant knows the chest exists and not who may close it; not survival-floors' Accident only, a priced floor from a stranger paid before the fall, since the funder is paid after, and from the win.

Absent owner's clock: a deadline whose owner is not at the table cannot be negotiated with the party who is, so the offer from elsewhere that expires Friday and the fund whose investment period ends in June import an urgency the table cannot soften; the carrier is the other party's calendar; keeping it credible costs letting it bind, since a clock named and then quietly extended discounts every clock the party names afterward; the tell is whether any deadline this party ever named was allowed to expire, and a request to see the offer with its date on it; the fake that survives is the clock the counterparty cannot watch expire, a private offer whose extension is never disclosed, which works until the counterparty sees the party still seated after the date; not impasse-inventions' invented deadline, which both sides adopt to share urgency, since here the urgency is owned by someone who was never asked.

Higher court's door: the walkaway is an appeal to a table above this one, bought from the higher power, as the medieval borough's charter let the town's disputes go to the king's court rather than the lord's, and as an arbitration clause or a regulator's complaint line does now; the carrier is the grant, recorded and paid for; keeping it credible costs the higher party's fee and its continuing interest in having the lower party as a client, so the door closes when the crown stops needing the town; the tell is the record of the grant and whether the door has ever been used; the fake that survives is the forged charter, which monastic houses produced in quantity and which the crown honored often enough when the forgery's side was the side it preferred, so a fake stands as long as the verifier wants it to be real; not register-jumps' carriers, which move a live situation into a new register, since here the jump is only threatened and its credibility is a document in a chest.

Second table in the square: the walkaway from the private table is a public one, the activist's open letter, the employees' petition, the leak, and it is credible in proportion to an audience that would care and a party that has published before; the carrier is the audience; keeping it credible costs earlier tables, since the audience that would care is built by letters already sent, each of which ended the private negotiation it threatened, so the option is one-shot at any table and its credibility at this one is bought with tables lost before; the tell is whether the audience exists and can hurt, a following, a reporter's number, a prior letter that landed, and a drafted letter shown privately is the tell of a party that would rather not send it; the fake that survives is the audience the counterparty overestimates, since the counterparty cannot poll the crowd before the letter goes; not Higher court's door, which appeals to a superior with jurisdiction, since the square has none and cannot be bought.

Meter on the walkaway: the option is credible in proportion to a visible quantity that depletes while it is displayed, as the strike fund whose balance the employer divides by weekly strike pay to get weeks, or the mobilized army whose daily cost the neighbor can estimate; the carrier is the fund or the payroll, and in the United States the union's annual filing makes the balance public; keeping it credible costs dues, or the standing cost of the mobilization, paid whether or not the option is used; the tell is the arithmetic, and a counterparty who can read the meter and outlast it waits for it to run down rather than conceding to it, while one who cannot outlast it concedes to the number; the fake that survives is the hidden reserve, a sympathy pledge from another union or an undisclosed credit line, which makes the meter read low on purpose; not runway-illusions' Watched burn, which is the operator's own life repriced by watchers, since here the metered quantity is the threat and the watcher is its target.

Kettle on the hob: the alternative is a relationship kept at a temperature, as the acquirer's corporate-development team met every quarter so that 'we have inbound interest' stays true, and each meeting costs the founder a slice of information and gives the acquirer a free look; the carrier is the cadence of contact; keeping it credible costs the leak, since a kettle kept warm is being read, and the acquirer is keeping the founder warm as its own option, so the two parties are each other's walkaway and neither knows which of them is the real one; the tell is depth, whether the acquirer's engineers have looked at the code or only its dealmakers have had coffee, and who proposed the last meeting; the fake that survives is inbound interest that was a form letter, since an investor cannot call the acquirer without telling it there is a deal; not Fed suitor, which is paid in the deal's own currency, a share of volume or an interview actually sat, where the incumbent can count what it lost, since the kettle is paid in information about the holder that the counterparty never sees on any ledger.

Walk on record: the option is credible because the party has walked before, as the retailer that dropped a national brand for a season and the union that struck once a decade ago, so the counterparty reads the record rather than the present alternative; the carrier is the record, which the party does not control once it exists; keeping it credible costs periodically walking from a deal the party would rather have taken, so the reputation is bought with real losses on a schedule the counterparties set by testing it; the tell is whether any walk is on the record at all and how old the last one is; the fake that survives is the forced exit written up as a chosen one, the deal that died for another reason and reads as a walk, since the record keeps outcomes and not motives; not power-trades' Silence on the tab, a repeated game that prices access, since here the repeated game prices the refusal.

Silent floor: the option is known to the holder alone and works through what the holder will let die, as the employee whose spouse's income means the job is not necessary, so the counterparty sees a calm it cannot source; the carrier is the holder's own knowledge and the posture it produces; keeping it credible costs nothing, since it is never claimed, but a real floor also changes what the holder accepts while the fake changes only how the holder looks; the tell is the brink, since a party with a real floor lets the deal die there and a party without one folds in the last hour, so a counterparty who can afford one dead deal can sort them; the fake that survives is the rehearsed calm against a counterparty who cannot afford the brink, which is most of them; not negotiator-check-loops' walk-away rehearsal, the holder's inner check, since here the question is what the counterparty reads and at what price it can test.

Tied hands: unwillingness is converted into inability, as the negotiator whose board will not approve above a figure, the buyer whose policy forbids the term, the ransom negotiator who says the family has already sold the house, so the walkaway is a constraint persuasion cannot reach because its owner is not in the room; the carrier is the constraint's paper or its absent principal; keeping it credible costs consistency, since a party that later finds the money has revealed every future constraint as a choice; the tell is the constraint's edges, since a counterparty who asks for something the constraint does not cover finds that a real constraint yields easily there and a fake one resists everywhere; the fake that survives is the constraint whose owner cannot be reached, a policy nobody can produce, a board that does not meet; not Absent owner's clock, which borrows someone else's date, since this borrows someone else's refusal; and not impasse-inventions' invented principal whose ratification buys distance and delay, a chip both sides adopt to break a deadlock, since here the principal belongs to one side and its refusal is meant to hold.

Ringer: a competing bid is manufactured by a confederate who will not close, as the shill in the auction room whose bids raise the price and who never wins, or the friendly fund that offers a sheet it does not mean to sign so the real lead sees competition; the carrier is the confederate and the conspiracy, and in most auction venues the shill is unlawful; keeping it credible costs the confederate's exposure and the risk that the ringer wins by accident and must be let off, which is the tell, since a ringer's bids never close and a lot the ringer won reappears in the next sale; the fake that survives is the sealed-bid ringer, whose bid is never seen and whose failure to close is never announced; not Paid floor, a real bid bought by contract, since the ringer's bid is real only until it is accepted.

Check that tips the rival: a claimed option is protected from verification because verifying it hands the alternative the deal, as the incumbent lead who would call the rival fund to confirm the competing term sheet and by calling tells the rival there is a round worth fighting for; the carrier is the small market in which the check leaks; keeping it credible costs naming the rival, since an unnamed sheet is a rumor and a named one is a sheet the incumbent could check at a price; the tell is the refusal to name, and the name itself when the fund named is one known to issue sheets it does not close; the fake that survives is the named sheet that does not exist, since the check costs the checker more than the concession, and a founder who has read the checker's bill knows it; not Kettle on the hob, which has no paper, since here there is a paper the counterparty could ask to see and chooses not to.

Cheap to claim, ruinous to check: the walkaway destroys both parties, liquidation rather than a down round, the regulator rather than the settlement, the founder who leaves rather than takes the terms, and it is credible in proportion to a small probability of madness times a large loss, so it need not be likely to work; the carrier is the counterparty's estimate of what the holder has done to itself before; keeping it credible costs occasionally doing something ruinous, which is why the reputation is rarely maintained and the threat usually discounted; the tell is whether the holder has ever burned anything of its own, and a counterparty who finds nothing in the record calls it; the fake that survives is the one the counterparty cannot afford to test at any probability, because the concession is smaller than the expected ruin; not a walkaway to an alternative, since there is no alternative and the leaving is the point, which it shares only with Tied hands, where the leaving is an excuse and here it is a threat.

Option they built for you: the counterparty supplies the option from its own prior, so the founder with the right resume is assumed to hold competing sheets and the surgeon assumed to hold offers, and the holder claims nothing; the carrier is the counterparty's model of the market and of the holder's kind; keeping it credible costs nothing while the prior holds and cannot be bought when it does not, since a claim would invite the check the prior spared; the tell is that there is none, because the counterparty never asks, and the option fails only when the prior updates, a down market, a public failure, a rival who checked; the fake that survives is the whole item, since no fake is manufactured, and a party who learns to look the part has built nothing and holds the strongest untested option on this map; not Silent floor, which the holder knows and the counterparty reads off posture, since here the holder may hold nothing and know it.

Pawn-shop option: a real outside option that discredits its holder when shown, as the insider bridge that lets a founder refuse an outside lead's terms and that, once named, tells the lead the outsiders did not come, so a genuine alternative lowers the price it was meant to hold up; the carrier is the counterparty's reading of why the alternative is the alternative; keeping it credible costs silence, since the option is worth most while the counterparty does not know it exists, and its holder must refuse terms without saying what the refusal rests on; the tell is any mention of it, and a counterparty who suspects a bridge asks whether the insiders have already committed; the fake that survives is the unmentioned bridge, which works as a Silent floor until the day it is exercised and becomes a discount; not an option that fails when tested, since this one fails when displayed, and a line that sorts options by whether they must exist has no place for one that exists and must not be seen.

source.register: Operator-grade and concrete: burn lines, stalking-horse fees, approved-vendor lists, dual-source volume, litigation-funding disclosure, exploding offers, borough charters, open letters, strike-fund arithmetic, corporate-development coffees, brand delistings, a spouse's income, absent boards, shills, term-sheet back-channels, liquidation threats, insider bridges; drawn from venture rounds, bankruptcy sales, procurement, employment, litigation, labor bargaining, mobilization, medieval charters, auctions, and ransom practice.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism. Two items rest on readings that are contested or speculative and say so: Option they built for you (that a counterparty's prior alone can carry an option, with no claim made) is an analytical claim the map cannot verify, and Cheap to claim, ruinous to check states the madman shape as a mechanism rather than as a description of any actual holder. Higher court's door's forgery case draws on the documented scale of medieval charter forgery, simplified. No item is invented-world.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a taxonomy or a partition; a real raise, strike, or sale runs several of these manufactures at once, often with one hidden behind another, and the list makes no claim to cover every kind.

The seriation is an itinerary of where the alternative's existence is held, not a ranking of strength, honesty, or cost; the map edges are conditional authored claims, and the fork, loop, incompatibility, and passage they draw are interpretations.

The illustrative cases (stalking-horse fees, union financial filings, monastic charter forgery, litigation-funding disclosure orders, shill bidding, insider bridges) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about specific transactions; shill bidding is unlawful in many venues and is described here as a mechanism, not as a practice to adopt.

Moves that destroy one's own alternatives to make staying credible (the burned ships, the precommitment to fight) and moves that destroy the counterparty's alternatives (locking up every supplier, buying the rival bidder) are outside; first-mover-forecloses and cooperation-ignitions carry those, and this map takes only what makes leaving credible on the holder's own side, an alternative built or faked or a leaving that needs none. A precommitment to leave, the floor announced to the press or the staff with no buyer in hand, is in type and absent from the map; it would be held in the holder's reputation, between Walk on record and Tied hands.

traces-of-the-unlived covers how an alternative that never occurs changes the episode it shadows; this map covers only how such an alternative is made to exist in a counterparty's model and what that costs, and it says nothing about the holder's psychology beyond the posture leak in Silent floor.

seriation.axis: Where the alternative's existence is held: from an alternative that is a state of the world and needs no believer, through alternatives held in a contract or a certificate, in another party's patience, money, calendar, or jurisdiction, in a crowd's care, in a depleting quantity or a relationship's temperature, in the record of the past, in the holder's own knowledge, in a constraint claimed on an absent owner's behalf, in a confederate's refusal to close, in the checker's bill and then the checker's ruin, in the counterparty's prior, to an alternative that is real and is held only in the counterparty's ignorance of it.
seriation.note: An authored walk, not a scale of strength or of honesty. Nothing to leave opens it because the option needs no one to believe anything; Pawn-shop option closes it because the option is real and its whole credibility is that nobody knows. Qualified on paper → Fed suitor is the consequential adjacency: both are second sources, but the certificate needs no one's consent and decays with the specification, while the suitor needs a person's continuing willingness and decays with its patience, so a buyer who moves from one to the other trades re-qualification money for a share of the business, and the counterparty's tell changes from 'when was the last lot?' to 'how much have they had?'. Check that tips the rival → Cheap to claim, ruinous to check sits where the fake's shelter stops being the holder's craft and becomes the checker's bill, first as a leak and then as the catastrophe itself. Two stops on the walk hold no alternative at all, only a credible leaving: Tied hands, held in an absent owner's refusal, and Cheap to claim, held in the checker's ruin; the itinerary places them by where the leaving's credibility is held, exactly as it places the others, which is why the type had to widen rather than the walk. Option they built for you → Pawn-shop option is the hinge: both work by the counterparty's model unaided by any claim, but the first works by what the counterparty wrongly believes and the second by what it does not know, so the walk ends where a real thing fails on display and the axis of existence runs out. Silent floor and Pawn-shop option are the same place seen from two sides, the holder's knowledge and the counterparty's ignorance, so the last stop is not a new location; its place at the end is earned by what display does to the option, not by where it is held.

relations.from: Fed suitor: the alternative is a party with wants of its own, so the second supplier or the rival employer stays an option only while it is given something, a share of the volume, a real chance at the position, and stops quoting the third time it learns it was the stalking horse; the carrier is the suitor's patience; keeping it credible costs a dual-source tax, the ten or twenty percent of volume placed with the second source at a worse price, or the interviews one actually sits; the tell is how long the suitor has been in place and what it has received, since a second source at zero share for three years is a name and not an option; the fake that survives is the suitor who knows and stays because it is paid to, which is the Paid floor by another door; not Qualified on paper, where the certificate needs no one's consent and decays with the spec, since here the option decays with a person's willingness.
relations.to: Paid floor: an outside option is bought as a real bid, as the stalking-horse bidder in a bankruptcy sale signs a binding purchase agreement and is paid a break-up fee if outbid, so the seller's walkaway exists by contract before the auction opens; the carrier is the signed agreement and the court-approved fee; keeping it credible costs the fee, a few percent of the price, plus a floor set below where the seller hopes to finish; the tell is the fee's size and the expense reimbursement beside it, since a large fee reveals that nobody expected a second bidder and prices the option the seller had to buy; no fake is needed because the option is real by construction, and its failure is the horse chosen because it would win; not power-trades' Fence around the process, which sells the auction's power to one bidder, since here the seller buys a bidder so that there is an auction at all.
relations.label: If the suitor learns it is being used as leverage and the holder wants it to stay, the holder must pay it, and if the payment is written down as a fee for losing, the fed suitor becomes a paid floor whose existence no longer depends on anyone's patience.

relations.from: Fed suitor: the alternative is a party with wants of its own, so the second supplier or the rival employer stays an option only while it is given something, a share of the volume, a real chance at the position, and stops quoting the third time it learns it was the stalking horse; the carrier is the suitor's patience; keeping it credible costs a dual-source tax, the ten or twenty percent of volume placed with the second source at a worse price, or the interviews one actually sits; the tell is how long the suitor has been in place and what it has received, since a second source at zero share for three years is a name and not an option; the fake that survives is the suitor who knows and stays because it is paid to, which is the Paid floor by another door; not Qualified on paper, where the certificate needs no one's consent and decays with the spec, since here the option decays with a person's willingness.
relations.to: Ringer: a competing bid is manufactured by a confederate who will not close, as the shill in the auction room whose bids raise the price and who never wins, or the friendly fund that offers a sheet it does not mean to sign so the real lead sees competition; the carrier is the confederate and the conspiracy, and in most auction venues the shill is unlawful; keeping it credible costs the confederate's exposure and the risk that the ringer wins by accident and must be let off, which is the tell, since a ringer's bids never close and a lot the ringer won reappears in the next sale; the fake that survives is the sealed-bid ringer, whose bid is never seen and whose failure to close is never announced; not Paid floor, a real bid bought by contract, since the ringer's bid is real only until it is accepted.
relations.label: If the same suitor is paid to stay but the payment is kept off the paper, because the holder wants the counterparty to read a real rival and not a bought one, the fed suitor becomes a ringer, and the holder has traded the counterparty's knowledge of the fee for the confederate's exposure and its own.

relations.from: Absent owner's clock: a deadline whose owner is not at the table cannot be negotiated with the party who is, so the offer from elsewhere that expires Friday and the fund whose investment period ends in June import an urgency the table cannot soften; the carrier is the other party's calendar; keeping it credible costs letting it bind, since a clock named and then quietly extended discounts every clock the party names afterward; the tell is whether any deadline this party ever named was allowed to expire, and a request to see the offer with its date on it; the fake that survives is the clock the counterparty cannot watch expire, a private offer whose extension is never disclosed, which works until the counterparty sees the party still seated after the date; not impasse-inventions' invented deadline, which both sides adopt to share urgency, since here the urgency is owned by someone who was never asked.
relations.to: Walk on record: the option is credible because the party has walked before, as the retailer that dropped a national brand for a season and the union that struck once a decade ago, so the counterparty reads the record rather than the present alternative; the carrier is the record, which the party does not control once it exists; keeping it credible costs periodically walking from a deal the party would rather have taken, so the reputation is bought with real losses on a schedule the counterparties set by testing it; the tell is whether any walk is on the record at all and how old the last one is; the fake that survives is the forced exit written up as a chosen one, the deal that died for another reason and reads as a walk, since the record keeps outcomes and not motives; not power-trades' Silence on the tab, a repeated game that prices access, since here the repeated game prices the refusal.
relations.label: If a borrowed clock is allowed to run out even once, with the deal still open, the record gains a walk the party never had to choose; if it is extended instead, every later clock the party names is discounted, so the expiry is the fork at which a borrowed option becomes a record or a discredit.

relations.from: Walk on record: the option is credible because the party has walked before, as the retailer that dropped a national brand for a season and the union that struck once a decade ago, so the counterparty reads the record rather than the present alternative; the carrier is the record, which the party does not control once it exists; keeping it credible costs periodically walking from a deal the party would rather have taken, so the reputation is bought with real losses on a schedule the counterparties set by testing it; the tell is whether any walk is on the record at all and how old the last one is; the fake that survives is the forced exit written up as a chosen one, the deal that died for another reason and reads as a walk, since the record keeps outcomes and not motives; not power-trades' Silence on the tab, a repeated game that prices access, since here the repeated game prices the refusal.
relations.to: Absent owner's clock: a deadline whose owner is not at the table cannot be negotiated with the party who is, so the offer from elsewhere that expires Friday and the fund whose investment period ends in June import an urgency the table cannot soften; the carrier is the other party's calendar; keeping it credible costs letting it bind, since a clock named and then quietly extended discounts every clock the party names afterward; the tell is whether any deadline this party ever named was allowed to expire, and a request to see the offer with its date on it; the fake that survives is the clock the counterparty cannot watch expire, a private offer whose extension is never disclosed, which works until the counterparty sees the party still seated after the date; not impasse-inventions' invented deadline, which both sides adopt to share urgency, since here the urgency is owned by someone who was never asked.
relations.label: If a walk is on the record, the party can name clocks whose owners the counterparty never checks, since the record answers the question the clock's owner would have, so the record buys clocks and the clocks, let expire, buy record; a party that starts with neither has to pay for the first one in a deal it wanted.

relations.from: Tied hands: unwillingness is converted into inability, as the negotiator whose board will not approve above a figure, the buyer whose policy forbids the term, the ransom negotiator who says the family has already sold the house, so the walkaway is a constraint persuasion cannot reach because its owner is not in the room; the carrier is the constraint's paper or its absent principal; keeping it credible costs consistency, since a party that later finds the money has revealed every future constraint as a choice; the tell is the constraint's edges, since a counterparty who asks for something the constraint does not cover finds that a real constraint yields easily there and a fake one resists everywhere; the fake that survives is the constraint whose owner cannot be reached, a policy nobody can produce, a board that does not meet; not Absent owner's clock, which borrows someone else's date, since this borrows someone else's refusal; and not impasse-inventions' invented principal whose ratification buys distance and delay, a chip both sides adopt to break a deadlock, since here the principal belongs to one side and its refusal is meant to hold.
relations.to: Cheap to claim, ruinous to check: the walkaway destroys both parties, liquidation rather than a down round, the regulator rather than the settlement, the founder who leaves rather than takes the terms, and it is credible in proportion to a small probability of madness times a large loss, so it need not be likely to work; the carrier is the counterparty's estimate of what the holder has done to itself before; keeping it credible costs occasionally doing something ruinous, which is why the reputation is rarely maintained and the threat usually discounted; the tell is whether the holder has ever burned anything of its own, and a counterparty who finds nothing in the record calls it; the fake that survives is the one the counterparty cannot afford to test at any probability, because the concession is smaller than the expected ruin; not a walkaway to an alternative, since there is no alternative and the leaving is the point, which it shares only with Tied hands, where the leaving is an excuse and here it is a threat.
relations.label: If the absent owner whose refusal ties the party's hands also owns the act that would burn both sides, as when the board that will not approve the price is the body that would have to vote liquidation, the party cannot in the same room make its walkaway a willingness to burn, since the constraint that excuses the refusal denies it the agency the burning needs, and a counterparty who hears both knows one is manufactured; where the constraint and the ruin have different owners, the family that cannot pay more and can still call the police, both stand.

relations.from: Rented war chest: the walkaway is the ability to go the distance, to trial rather than settlement, to the tenth week, to the next quarter, and it is supplied by a third party who buys a share of the outcome, as the litigation funder who pays the plaintiff's costs against a slice of the award, or the parent whose guarantee lets a subsidiary refuse a supplier's terms; the carrier is the funding agreement, which the funder holds and the holder does not fully own; keeping it credible costs the funder's slice and the funder's continuing belief in the case; the tell is disclosure, since defendants ask whether a funder exists and some courts now require the answer, and then the terms, since a funder who may withdraw below a settlement threshold owns the walkaway; the fake that survives is the funder disclosed without its terms, so the defendant knows the chest exists and not who may close it; not survival-floors' Accident only, a priced floor from a stranger paid before the fall, since the funder is paid after, and from the win.
relations.to: Tied hands: unwillingness is converted into inability, as the negotiator whose board will not approve above a figure, the buyer whose policy forbids the term, the ransom negotiator who says the family has already sold the house, so the walkaway is a constraint persuasion cannot reach because its owner is not in the room; the carrier is the constraint's paper or its absent principal; keeping it credible costs consistency, since a party that later finds the money has revealed every future constraint as a choice; the tell is the constraint's edges, since a counterparty who asks for something the constraint does not cover finds that a real constraint yields easily there and a fake one resists everywhere; the fake that survives is the constraint whose owner cannot be reached, a policy nobody can produce, a board that does not meet; not Absent owner's clock, which borrows someone else's date, since this borrows someone else's refusal; and not impasse-inventions' invented principal whose ratification buys distance and delay, a chip both sides adopt to break a deadlock, since here the principal belongs to one side and its refusal is meant to hold.
relations.label: If the funder's agreement lets it veto a settlement below a threshold, the plaintiff's rented walkaway passes to the funder's terms, and the plaintiff can honestly say its hands are tied; the option's owner has become the constraint, and the defendant must now negotiate with a party that is not in the room and was never a party to the harm.

relations.from: Meter on the walkaway: the option is credible in proportion to a visible quantity that depletes while it is displayed, as the strike fund whose balance the employer divides by weekly strike pay to get weeks, or the mobilized army whose daily cost the neighbor can estimate; the carrier is the fund or the payroll, and in the United States the union's annual filing makes the balance public; keeping it credible costs dues, or the standing cost of the mobilization, paid whether or not the option is used; the tell is the arithmetic, and a counterparty who can read the meter and outlast it waits for it to run down rather than conceding to it, while one who cannot outlast it concedes to the number; the fake that survives is the hidden reserve, a sympathy pledge from another union or an undisclosed credit line, which makes the meter read low on purpose; not runway-illusions' Watched burn, which is the operator's own life repriced by watchers, since here the metered quantity is the threat and the watcher is its target.
relations.to: Silent floor: the option is known to the holder alone and works through what the holder will let die, as the employee whose spouse's income means the job is not necessary, so the counterparty sees a calm it cannot source; the carrier is the holder's own knowledge and the posture it produces; keeping it credible costs nothing, since it is never claimed, but a real floor also changes what the holder accepts while the fake changes only how the holder looks; the tell is the brink, since a party with a real floor lets the deal die there and a party without one folds in the last hour, so a counterparty who can afford one dead deal can sort them; the fake that survives is the rehearsed calm against a counterparty who cannot afford the brink, which is most of them; not negotiator-check-loops' walk-away rehearsal, the holder's inner check, since here the question is what the counterparty reads and at what price it can test.
